26	## Project Overview
27	
28	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains local canonical skills (`skills/local/`), first-party project skills (`skills/owned/`), and cherry-picked third-party skills (`skills/vendor/`). Owned and vendor copies sync from their canonical upstream repos.
29	
30	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`owned/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	```bash
35	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
36	make sync
37	
38	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)

40	
41	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
42	make kanban
43	
44	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
45	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
46	make marketplace
47	
48	# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
49	make native-marketplace-smoke
50	
51	# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
52	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
53	make lint-frontmatter
54	
55	# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
56	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
57	make validate
58	
59	# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
60	make install-hooks
61	
62	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
63	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
64	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill

90	
91	## Source categories and upstream sync
92	
93	- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
94	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
95	- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.
96	
97	`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
98	`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
99	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
100	with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
101	cannot serve as a distributable copy.
102	
103	An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
104	contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
105	After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
106	Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).
107	
108	## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)
109	
110	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
111	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
112	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
113	
114	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
115	
116	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
117	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
118	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
119	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
120	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
121	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
122	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
123	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
124	
125	Active series in this repo:
126	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
127	
128	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
129	
130	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
131	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
132	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
133	
134	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
135	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
136	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
137	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
138	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
139	  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
140	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
141	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
142	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
143	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
144	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
145	
146	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
147	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
148	
149	## Marketplace Catalog
150	
151	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
152	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
153	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
154	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
155	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
156	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
157	for the full mechanism.
158	
159	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
160	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
161	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
162	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
163	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
164	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
165	
166	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
167	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
168	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
169	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
170	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
171	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
172	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
173	within-group caveat in
174	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
175	
176	## SKILL.md Format
177	
178	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
179	
180	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
181	
182	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
183	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
184	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
185	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
186	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
187	
188	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
189	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
190	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
191	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
192	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
193	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
194	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
195	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
196	
197	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
198	
199	```bash
200	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
201	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
202	
203	# …or remove them afterward
204	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
205	```
206	
207	## Project Memory Workflow
208	
209	<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance -->
210	### Issue-driven workflow (GitHub)
211	
212	This project uses GitHub Issues as the canonical backlog and GitHub
213	Discussions for evaluative/research topics. The `forge-native-dev` skill
214	provides the scripts below.
215	
216	| Information | Lives in | Why |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| Actionable work (bugs, features, chores) | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) | Searchable, assignable, cross-linkable |
219	| Evaluations, "should we?", research | [Discussions](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/discussions) | Threaded, collaborative |
220	| Research docs, trade-off analysis | `backlog/` | In-repo, diffable, reviewed in PRs |
221	| Past traps, debugging knowledge | `pitfalls/` | Grep-able by symptom, portable |
222	| Backlog visualization | [Project board](https://github.com/users/daviddwlee84/projects/11) | Built-in to the forge |
223	| Historical record | `TODO.md` `## Done` section | In git |
224	
225	**Capture intent as Issues** — when the user describes a bug, idea, or
226	"maybe later" item, create an Issue with appropriate labels. Do not ask
227	"should I create an issue?" — default to creating one.
228	
229	**Work lifecycle:**
230	1. Start: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start <issue-number>`
231	2. Work in the worktree, commit conventionally
232	3. Finish: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh finish <issue-number>`
233	4. After merge: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-cleanup.sh`
234	
235	**Check for work:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-issue.sh list --assignee @me`
236	
237	**Dashboard:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-status.sh`
238	
239	**PRs are review gates, not proposals.** The issue describes intent; the
240	PR is the diff to review. Default merge strategy: **squash and merge**.
241	<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance (end) -->
242	
243	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
244	
245	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
246	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
247	own conventions). It has four subareas:
248	
249	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
250	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
251	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
252	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
253	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
254	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
255	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
256	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
257	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
258	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
259	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
260	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
261	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
262	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
263	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
264	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
265	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
266	  status / license / last_verified`).
267	
268	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
269	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
270	
271	| Status | Meaning |
272	|---|---|
273	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
274	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
275	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
276	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
277	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
278	
279	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
280	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
281	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
282	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
283	
284	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
285	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
286	
287	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
288	
289	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
290	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
291	
292	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
293	2. The root cause
294	3. The workaround
295	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
296	
297	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
298	the explanation they do not know yet.

311	  default; writes require `--apply`. JSON goes to stdout and diagnostics to
312	  stderr. It stages and validates candidates before replacement, is
313	  idempotent, and never overwrites a foreign build helper.
314	  - Flags: `--target-dir DIR`, `--apply`, `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--json`.
315	  - Exit codes: `0` safe/migrated; `10` affected legacy config found during
316	    audit/dry-run; `11` manual actions remain; `12` strict verification failed.
317	
318	## Reference files
319	
320	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
321	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
322	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
323	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
324	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
325	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
326	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
327	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
328	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
329	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
330	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
331	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
332	- `references/i18n-llmstxt-migration.md` — Audit/apply/verify migration guide,
333	  exit-code contract, automatic patch boundary, and manual fallback. Read this
334	  **before repairing or upgrading an existing i18n + llmstxt site**.
335	- `references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` — Why the stack pins `mkdocs<2` and
336	  `mkdocs-material<10`. Captures the MkDocs 2.0 plugin-removal situation,
337	  Material team's Zensical replacement, and the criteria for lifting the
338	  caps. Read whenever a user asks about upgrading MkDocs or why the docs
339	  build is on 1.x.
340	
341	## Bundled assets
342	
343	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
344	
345	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + environment-guarded llmstxt,
346	  copy-to-llm, i18n-ready `docs_dir`, and pymdownx.snippets; parameterized with
347	  `{{SITE_NAME}}`, `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__`
348	  marker lines that `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
349	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
350	  optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
351	- `assets/build-docs-site.py` — Managed two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] helper copied to the downstream
352	  project's `scripts/build-docs-site.py`. Keep its managed marker intact so the
353	  migration tool can distinguish it from a user-owned script.
354	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
355	  paths filter, uv setup, the managed strict build helper, and Pages deploy.
356	  Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__` marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
357	- `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
358	  `init-docs-site.sh --social` is [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
359	  plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
360	  `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
361	  Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
362	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
363	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
364	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
365	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
366	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
367	  terminology-rule admonition.
368	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
369	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
370	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
371	
372	## Gotchas
373	
374	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
375	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
376	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
377	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
378	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
379	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
380	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
381	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
382	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
383	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
384	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
385	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
386	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
387	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
388	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
389	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
390	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
391	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
392	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
393	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
394	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
395	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
396	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
397	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
398	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
399	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
400	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
401	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
402	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
403	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
404	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
405	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
406	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
407	  `select()` form.
408	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
409	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
410	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
411	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
412	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
413	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
414	- **`pymdownx.snippets` include fragments belong in recursive `exclude_docs`.**
415	  `not_in_nav` only suppresses warnings and still publishes standalone HTML;
416	  the template excludes root and nested `_snippets/` directories.
417	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
418	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
419	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
420	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
421	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
422	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
423	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
424	  Counter-intuitive name.
425	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
426	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
427	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
428	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
429	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
430	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
431	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
432	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
433	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
434	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
435	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
436	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
437	- **A single multilingual build silently corrupts `mkdocs-llmstxt` output.**
438	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` performs a full build per locale, while llmstxt clears
439	  its page state and overwrites the same root `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` on
440	  every [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. The final locale can therefore leave nearly empty or wrong-locale
441	  output. Removing `--strict` only hides warnings; it does not repair the files.
442	  Always use `scripts/build-docs-site.py` for the deployable artifact. Root
443	  `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars intentionally contain only
444	  the default language.
445	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
446	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
447	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
448	  is just acting on it.
449	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
450	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
451	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
452	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
453	
454	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
455	
456	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, don't silently "upgrade" it; customizations may
457	not match the template. For an explicit i18n/llmstxt repair request, use
458	`migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh` audit-first. Apply only after showing its planned
459	changes and preserve every shape it reports as a manual action.
460
````

```text
1	# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
2	
3	The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
4	`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
5	the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
6	**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
11	  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
12	  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
13	- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
14	  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
15	  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
16	- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
17	  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
18	  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
19	  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
20	- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
21	  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.
22	
23	## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
24	
25	Per the Material team's analysis
26	([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):
27	
28	| Change | Impact on this stack |
29	|---|---|
30	| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
31	| Theme system rewritten — nav [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
32	| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
33	| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
34	| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |
35	
36	The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
37	describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
38	publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
39	There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
40	maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
41	user-driven (solve a specific pain).
42	
43	## Material team's response — Zensical
44	
45	[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
46	MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
47	MkDocs 1.x**.
48	
49	What's known:
50	
51	- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
52	- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
53	- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
54	  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
55	- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
56	  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
57	- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.
58	
59	The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
60	due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
61	strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.
62	
63	## Why we cap explicitly
64	
65	Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
66	which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
67	accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:
68	
69	- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
70	- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
71	  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
72	- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
73	  else's defensive pin to stay correct.
74	
75	The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
76	bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
77	patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.
78	
79	## When to re-evaluate
80	
81	Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
82	following are true**:
83	
84	1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
85	   equivalent project signal of API stability).
86	2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
87	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
88	   per-language search).
89	3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
90	   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
91	   per-page raw-markdown links).
92	4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
93	   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).
94	
95	Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
96	MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
97	them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.
98	
99	## What to avoid
100	
101	- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
102	  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
103	- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
104	  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
105	  individual users.
106	- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
107	  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
108	  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
109	- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
110	  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
111	  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.
112	
113	## Re-checking the situation
114	
115	A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:
116	
117	1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
118	   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
119	   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
120	2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
121	   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
122	3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
123	   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
124	   release date been set?
125	4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
126	   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
127	   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
128	   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.
129	
130	## Source links
131	
132	- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
133	  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
134	- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
135	- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
136	- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>
137	- MkDocs 2.0 community discussion (#4077):
138	  <https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077>
139
```

```text
### Shipped support

The page describes Zensical’s listed plugins as native implementations: “continue to work with your existing configuration and project structure.”

- **search — supported**, since 0.0.3. It is enabled by default, even if omitted from `plugins`. Only `enabled` and `separator` affect Zensical search; settings including `lang`, `pipeline`, `fields`, and `indexing` are ignored.
- **mkdocstrings — supported**, since 0.0.11. Install `mkdocstrings-python` for the Python handler. Sources outside the project directory are not watched during preview, and `watch` is ignored.
- **autorefs — supported**, since 0.0.22. Provides cross-page links; tooltip and HTML-stripping behavior can depend on theme settings.
- **awesome-nav — supported**, since 0.0.58. Uses `.nav.yml`; extglob patterns are unsupported, and `not_in_nav` does not affect its generated navigation.
- **mike — supported**, since 0.0.30. Requires the compatible fork described in the versioning guide; `css_dir` and `javascript_dir` are ignored.
- **literate-nav — supported**, since 0.0.58. Defines navigation with Markdown lists; the page lists its settings without additional differences.
- **llmstxt — supported**, since 0.0.67. Custom Python preprocessing does not run; `full_output` must be a relative file path inside `site_dir`, distinct from `llms.txt`.
- **include-markdown — supported**, since 0.0.71. Per-inclusion arguments are accepted but ignored; glob patterns, several named options, and some transformations are unsupported or ignored. Snippets settings take precedence over mapped plugin settings.
- **macros — supported**, since 0.0.40. The environment is created per rendered page, only `define_env` is called automatically, and several MkDocs APIs and hooks are unavailable.
- **redirects — supported**, since 0.0.58. The page notes support for anchor-based redirects.
- **minify — supported**, since 0.0.58. Unparseable assets retain their original content; inline JS and CSS options are Zensical-only.

### Unsupported, planned, or not specified here

- **gen-files — explicitly unsupported.** The page says, “Zensical does not currently support `gen-files`.” It suggests generating files separately; the described `uvx` approach requires `mkdocs.yml` and does not work with `zensical.toml`.
- **git-revision-date-localized — planned**, not described as shipped. It appears under “Planned” in the compatibility roadmap.
- **static-i18n, i18n, copy-to-llm — not mentioned in the supplied page.** Their support status cannot be established from this content.

### Plugin API and ignored configuration

On custom plugins, the page states: “Zensical does not currently run arbitrary MkDocs plugins or expose the MkDocs plugin API.” A separate Module API is in development, with early access planned through Zensical Spark before public release.

For configuration not listed as supported, it says: “Configuration for plugins not listed under Supported plugins is silently ignored.” It also says settings marked ignored are silently ignored without validation or warnings; unknown settings for supported plugins produce a configuration error.
```

- The article says Material for MkDocs is incompatible with MkDocs 2.0: **“If your documentation is built with Material for MkDocs, it will cease to work with MkDocs 2.0.”**

196	def validate_env_contract(config_file: Path, config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
197	    probe_docs = str(config_file.parent / ".mkdocs-site-bootstrap-env-probe")
198	    plugin_names = ("i18n", "llmstxt", "copy-to-llm", "social")

206	    common = {ENV_DOCS_DIR: probe_docs}
207	    disabled = load_config_with_env(
208	        config_file,
209	        {**common, **{variable: "false" for variable in plugin_env.values()}},
210	    )
211	    enabled = load_config_with_env(
212	        config_file,
213	        {**common, **{variable: "true" for variable in plugin_env.values()}},
214	    )

217	    if disabled.get("docs_dir") != probe_docs or enabled.get("docs_dir") != probe_docs:

221	        _, enabled_config = plugin_definition(enabled, name)
222	        if disabled_config.get("enabled") is not False or enabled_config.get("enabled") is not True:

229	        for value in values:

231	                continue

233	            if item.startswith("./"):
234	                item = item[2:]
235	            normalized.add(item)

278	def assert_safe_tree(source: Path, target: Path, site_dir: Path) -> None:
279	    if not source.exists() or not source.is_dir():
280	        raise BuildFailure(f"Docs directory not found: {source}", 2)
281	    if source.is_symlink():
282	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked docs directory: {source}", 2)
283	    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(source, followlinks=False):
284	        root_path = Path(root)
285	        for name in [*dirs, *files]:
286	            candidate = root_path / name
287	            if candidate.is_symlink():
288	                raise BuildFailure(
289	                    f"Refusing symlink inside docs tree: {candidate.relative_to(source)}", 2
290	                )
291	
292	    if not is_relative_to(source, target):
293	        raise BuildFailure(
294	            f"Docs directory must stay inside --target-dir: {source} (target: {target}).",
295	            2,
296	        )
297	    if not is_relative_to(site_dir, target) or site_dir == target:
298	        raise BuildFailure(
299	            f"Site directory must be a child of --target-dir, not {site_dir}.", 2
300	        )
301	    if (
302	        site_dir == source
303	        or is_relative_to(source, site_dir)
304	        or is_relative_to(site_dir, source)
305	    ):
306	        raise BuildFailure("site_dir and docs_dir may not contain one another.", 2)
307	    if site_dir.is_symlink():
308	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked site directory: {site_dir}", 2)
309	    if site_dir.exists() and not site_dir.is_dir():
310	        raise BuildFailure(f"site_dir exists but is not a directory: {site_dir}", 2)

313	def is_translated_source(path: Path, nondefault_locales: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
314	    name = path.name.casefold()
315	    return any(
316	        name.endswith(f".{locale.casefold()}{extension}")
317	        for locale in nondefault_locales

322	def copy_docs_tree(
323	    source: Path,
324	    destination: Path,
325	    *,
326	    nondefault_locales: Iterable[str] = (),
327	) -> None:
328	    blocked = tuple(nondefault_locales)
329	
330	    def ignore(directory: str, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
331	        base = Path(directory)
332	        return [name for name in names if is_translated_source(base / name, blocked)]
333	
334	    shutil.copytree(source, destination, ignore=ignore if blocked else None)

389	def llmstxt_expected_pages(config: dict[str, Any], docs_dir: Path) -> set[str]:
390	    present, llms = plugin_definition(config, "llmstxt")
391	    if not present:
392	        return set()
393	    sections = llms.get("sections", {})
394	    if not isinstance(sections, dict):
395	        raise BuildFailure("Plugin `llmstxt.sections` must be a mapping.", 2)
396	    source_uris = [
397	        path.relative_to(docs_dir).as_posix()
398	        for path in docs_dir.rglob("*")
399	        if path.is_file()
400	    ]
401	    expected: set[str] = set()
402	    for inputs in sections.values():
403	        if not isinstance(inputs, list):
404	            raise BuildFailure("Every `llmstxt.sections` value must be a list.", 2)
405	        for item in inputs:
406	            value = next(iter(item)) if isinstance(item, dict) and item else item
407	            if not isinstance(value, str):
408	                raise BuildFailure("llmstxt section entries must be paths or path mappings.", 2)
409	            if "*" in value:
410	                expected.update(fnmatch.filter(source_uris, value))
411	            else:
412	                expected.add(value)
413	    return expected

431	def local_markdown_links(llms_file: Path, site_url: str) -> list[Path]:
432	    parsed_site = urlparse(site_url)
433	    base_path = parsed_site.path.rstrip("/") + "/"
434	    links: list[Path] = []
435	    destinations: list[str] = []
436	    for line in llms_file.read_text("utf-8").splitlines():
437	        match = re.match(r"^\s*-\s+\[[^]]*\]\((.+?)\)(?::.*)?\s*$", line)
438	        if match:
439	            destinations.append(match.group(1))
440	    for destination in destinations:
441	        parsed = urlparse(destination.strip("<>"))
442	        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
443	            if (parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) != (parsed_site.scheme, parsed_site.netloc):
444	                continue
445	            path = parsed.path
446	        elif parsed.path.startswith("/"):
447	            path = parsed.path
448	        else:
449	            path = base_path + parsed.path
450	        if not path.startswith(base_path):
451	            raise BuildFailure(
452	                f"Generated llms.txt contains a local URL outside site_url: {destination}"
453	            )
454	        relative = unquote(path[len(base_path) :]).lstrip("/")
455	        candidate = Path(relative)
456	        if candidate.suffix == ".md":
457	            if candidate.is_absolute() or ".." in candidate.parts:
458	                raise BuildFailure(f"Unsafe generated Markdown URL: {destination}")
459	            links.append(candidate)
460	    return links

463	def has_locale_path(path: Path, nondefault_locales: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
464	    folded_parts = {part.casefold() for part in path.parts}
465	    name = path.name.casefold()
466	    return any(
467	        locale.casefold() in folded_parts
468	        or name.endswith(f".{locale.casefold()}.md")
469	        for locale in nondefault_locales
470	    )

547	def atomic_replace_tree(staged: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
548	    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549	    backup = destination.parent / f".{destination.name}.backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
550	    had_destination = destination.exists()
551	    if had_destination:
552	        os.replace(destination, backup)
553	    try:
554	        os.replace(staged, destination)
555	    except BaseException:
556	        if had_destination and backup.exists():
557	            os.replace(backup, destination)
558	        raise
559	    if backup.exists():
560	        try:
561	            shutil.rmtree(backup)
562	        except OSError as error:
563	            log(f"warning: could not remove previous site backup {backup}: {error}")

````text
1	# `.skills/preferences.yaml` schema
2	
3	Per-repo preferences file used by `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and any future
4	skill that needs to remember a user decision across sessions.
5	
6	## Location
7	
8	Always at `<repo-root>/.skills/preferences.yaml`. **Per-repo, not global.**
9	Each repository carries its own decisions; never write to `~/.skills/` or
10	`~/.config/`.
11	
12	The directory is created on first write. Add `.skills/preferences.yaml` to
13	`.gitignore` if the user prefers it private, but the default assumption is
14	that it's committed (decisions about *this repo's tooling* belong in the
15	repo).
16	
17	## Top-level structure
18	
19	```yaml
20	# .skills/preferences.yaml
21	# Decisions recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill namespace.
22	
23	mkdocs_site_bootstrap:
24	  enabled: true                  # null = never asked, true = opted in, false = opted out
25	  decided_at: 2026-04-23
26	  stack: mkdocs-material         # which docs stack variant
27	  auto_deploy: true              # deploy via GitHub Actions on push
28	  pages_deployed: true           # has the first deploy succeeded
29	  pages_enabled_at: 2026-04-23
30	  existing_docs_decision: skipped  # skipped | wrapped | none
31	  site_url: https://owner.github.io/repo/
32	  repo_slug: owner/repo
33	  # i18n keys — written by add-language.sh, read by add-docs-page.sh.
34	  languages: ["en", "zh-TW"]      # ordered list; first is default
35	  keep_english_terms: true         # injects terminology admonition into non-default stubs
36	  i18n_structure: suffix           # suffix | folder (folder reserved, not yet implemented)
37	
38	# Future skills add their own top-level keys with the same shape.
39	# example_other_skill:
40	#   enabled: true
41	#   decided_at: 2026-05-01
42	```
43	
44	## Conventions for skill namespaces
45	
46	- **Namespace key matches the skill's directory name** with `-` → `_`
47	  (YAML-friendly): `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` → `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`.
48	- **Always include `enabled` and `decided_at`.** These are the universal
49	  fields. `enabled` is the consent state; `decided_at` lets the agent see
50	  how stale the decision is.
51	- **Don't store secrets.** This file is meant to be safely committable.
52	  API tokens, [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]words, etc. go in `.env` (gitignored) or in CI secrets.
53	- **Don't store derived state.** Anything reproducible from other files
54	  (e.g., "is mkdocs.yml present") should be re-checked, not cached. Only
55	  store decisions and timestamps.
56	
57	## Three-state semantics for `enabled`
58	
59	| Value | Meaning | Agent behavior |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| key absent or `null` | Never asked | Run the interview |
62	| `true` | User opted in | Proceed without re-asking |
63	| `false` | User opted out | Don't pester. If the user is now asking for it, confirm they want to reverse the decision, then `--reset` and re-interview |
64	
65	This three-state model is why we don't use a marker file (presence-only)
66	or a boolean (only two states). The "never asked" state matters.
67	
68	## Reading and writing
69	
70	Always go through `scripts/check-preferences.sh` rather than parsing the YAML
71	yourself. It handles:
72	
73	- Creating the file and `.skills/` dir if missing
74	- Preserving the comment header
75	- Atomic writes (write to `.tmp`, then `mv`)
76	- Friendly errors for malformed input
77	
78	```bash
79	# Read one key
80	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
81	
82	# Set one or more keys
83	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
84	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
85	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
86	
87	# Reset an entire skill namespace (returns to "never asked" state)
88	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
89	
90	# Dump everything
91	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --list
92	```
93	
94	The script supports `--json` for structured output that an agent can parse
95	reliably.
96	
97	## When to reset
98	
99	The user explicitly says one of:
100	
101	- "I changed my mind about <skill>" → `--reset <namespace>`
102	- "Stop nagging me about docs" → `--set <namespace>.enabled=false`
103	- "Re-ask me next time" → `--reset <namespace>`
104	
105	Don't reset proactively. The whole point is to *avoid* re-asking.
106	
107	## Cross-skill coordination
108	
109	Two skills shouldn't share namespace keys. If `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and
110	some hypothetical `docs-publisher` skill both care about whether a docs site
111	exists, the answer is to **detect from the filesystem** (does `mkdocs.yml`
112	exist?), not to share a preference key. Preferences record *intent*; the
113	filesystem records *state*.
114	
115	## i18n keys (added when `add-language.sh` runs)
116	
117	| Key | Type | Meaning |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| `languages` | ordered list of locale codes | First entry is the default language. Empty / missing means monolingual (default). |
120	| `keep_english_terms` | bool | Whether to inject the "Terminology rule" admonition into non-default-language stubs. Defaults to `true`; the user can flip this if they don't want the admonition. |
121	| `i18n_structure` | `suffix` \| `folder` | How translated files are laid out. **Currently only `suffix` is implemented.** `folder` is reserved for future work; setting it now will not change script behavior. |
122	
123	`add-docs-page.sh` reads `languages` to decide whether to generate
124	`*.<LANG>.md` siblings alongside the default-language page. If the key is
125	missing or has only one entry, it stays mono-lingual (existing behavior).
126	
127	## Array values via `--set`
128	
129	`check-preferences.sh --set` recognises YAML flow sequences (`[…]`) and
130	mappings (`{…}`) and [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es them through to `yq` unquoted. Use this for the
131	`languages` key:
132	
133	```bash
134	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
135	  --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en", "zh-TW"]'
136	```
137	
138	Bare strings, booleans, and numbers still work as before.
139	
140	## Schema versioning
141	
142	If we ever need to change the shape, add a top-level `schema_version: 1`
143	key and bump it. Until then, treat the schema as version 0 / implicit.
144	
145	## Validation
146	
147	`check-preferences.sh --validate` is a future addition (not yet implemented).
148	For now, trust the script's writes and don't hand-edit the file unless you
149	re-read it after to verify.
150
````

1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	If you are building documentation for a project that consumes one of the
4	skills in this repo (especially [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
5	or [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)),
6	this is the docs stack we recommend.
7	
8	It's the same stack this repo uses for its own docs, plus the optional
9	`mkdocstrings` layer for projects that have a Python API to document.
10	
11	## TL;DR
12	
13	```toml
14	# pyproject.toml
15	[project.optional-dependencies]
16	docs = [
17	  "mkdocs>=1.6",
18	  "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
19	  # "mkdocs-material[imaging]>=9.5",  # only with --social (cairosvg+pillow)
20	  "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.24",   # only if you have a Python API
21	  "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
22	  "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
23	  "pymdown-extensions>=10.0",
24	]
25	```
26	
27	```bash
28	# Local preview
29	uv sync --extra docs
30	uv run mkdocs serve
31	
32	# Build static site
33	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
34	
35	# Safe HTML-only preview (llmstxt stays disabled)
36	uv run mkdocs build --strict
37	```
38	
39	## Why this stack
40	
41	- **MkDocs + Material** — Markdown-first authoring, built-in search, a
42	  theme that doesn't need overrides for ~90% of projects, GitHub Pages
43	  deploy is one workflow file.
44	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — render API docs from Python docstrings via
45	  `::: package.module.symbol` directives in your Markdown. Only relevant
46	  if your project has a Python API; skip it otherwise.
47	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt`** — generates `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` so
48	  AI agents can discover and consume your docs without scraping HTML.
49	  Upstream is in maintenance mode and must be isolated from a multilingual
50	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` build; the managed helper does that. If it stops working
51	  even in the default-language [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], replace it with a post-build generator.
52	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`** — adds "Copy to LLM / Open in ChatGPT / Open
53	  in Claude" buttons on every page. Pure UX sugar; harmless if your
54	  audience doesn't use it.
55	- **Managed strict build helper** — keeps `mkdocs-static-i18n` and
56	  `mkdocs-llmstxt` out of the same plugin lifecycle. Multilingual HTML is built
57	  separately from default-language LLM artifacts, validated, and merged before
58	  `site/` is replaced.
59	
60	## Why not these?
61	
62	- **Sphinx + Furo + MyST + autodoc.** Strictly more powerful, but the
63	  setup and maintenance cost is meaningful. Recommended only if AI-facing
64	  Markdown output becomes a first-class requirement, or if your project
65	  has the kind of cross-project reference graph Sphinx is built for.
66	- **pdoc.** Single-file API doc generator. Great for "I just want HTML
67	  for my package", but no good story for guides, conventions pages, or
68	  llms.txt.
69	- **Rspress.** Best-in-class for AI-native output, but it's
70	  Node-first / frontend-product-docs-first; Python API reference is a
71	  bolt-on. Not a fit unless you're already on the Node ecosystem.
72	- **Quarto.** Excellent for notebook / tutorial / research-report
73	  workflows; not optimized for Python library documentation.
74	
75	The longer version of this analysis (with the upstream-vs-inference
76	distinction made explicit) is preserved in the reference repo
77	[`mlflow-widgets/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets/blob/main/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md).
78	
79	## Minimum `mkdocs.yml`
80	
81	```yaml
82	site_name: Your Project
83	site_description: One sentence about your project.
84	site_url: https://yourname.github.io/your-project/
85	repo_url: https://github.com/yourname/your-project
86	edit_uri: edit/main/docs/
87	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
88	
89	theme:
90	  name: material
91	  features:
92	    - navigation.instant
93	    - navigation.sections
94	    - navigation.indexes
95	    - search.suggest
96	    - content.code.copy
97	    - content.action.edit
98	    - toc.follow
99	
100	plugins:
101	  - search
102	  # Optional (opt-in via `init-docs-site.sh --social`): OG/Twitter preview
103	  # cards. Needs system cairo/pango + mkdocs-material[imaging]. Omit for a
104	  # dependency-free build.
105	  # - social:
106	  #     enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
107	  #     cards_layout_options:
108	  #       background_color: "#3f51b5"
109	  #       # font_family: Noto Sans TC   # set a CJK font if titles are CJK
110	  - mkdocstrings:        # remove this block if no Python API
111	      handlers:
112	        python:
113	          paths: [src]
114	          options:
115	            show_source: true
116	            show_root_heading: true
117	            members_order: source
118	            docstring_style: google
119	            merge_init_into_class: true
120	  - llmstxt:
121	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
122	      full_output: llms-full.txt
123	      sections:
124	        Guides: [index.md, getting-started.md]
125	        API Reference: [reference/*.md]
126	  - copy-to-llm:
127	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
128	      repo_url: "https://yourname.github.io/your-project"
129	
130	markdown_extensions:
131	  - admonition
132	  - tables
133	  - toc:
134	      permalink: true
135	  - pymdownx.superfences
136	  - pymdownx.highlight
137	  - pymdownx.snippets:
138	      base_path:
139	        - .
140	        - !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
141	      check_paths: true
142	
143	nav:
144	  - Home: index.md
145	  - Getting Started: getting-started.md
146	  - API Reference:
147	      - Overview: reference/index.md
148	```
149	
150	## GitHub Pages workflow
151	
152	`.github/workflows/docs.yml`:
153	
154	```yaml
155	name: Docs
156	
157	on:
158	  push:
159	    branches: [main]
160	    paths:
161	      - 'docs/**'
162	      - 'mkdocs.yml'
163	      - 'pyproject.toml'
164	      - 'scripts/build-docs-site.py'
165	      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
166	  workflow_dispatch:
167	
168	permissions:
169	  contents: read
170	  pages: write
171	  id-token: write
172	
173	concurrency:
174	  group: pages
175	  cancel-in-progress: true
176	
177	jobs:
178	  build:
179	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
180	    steps:
181	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
182	      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
183	        with:
184	          enable-cache: true
185	      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
186	        with:
187	          python-version: "3.13"
188	      # Only with --social (OG cards): cairo + pango render the card, and the
189	      # cache avoids re-rendering unchanged pages. Omit both steps otherwise.
190	      - name: Install Cairo/Pango for social cards
191	        run: |
192	          sudo apt-get update
193	          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
194	            libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev \
195	            libffi-dev libjpeg-dev libpng-dev
196	      - name: Cache social cards
197	        uses: actions/cache@v4
198	        with:
199	          path: .cache/plugin/social
200	          key: social-${{ hashFiles('mkdocs.yml') }}-${{ hashFiles('docs/**/*.md') }}
201	          restore-keys: |
202	            social-${{ hashFiles('mkdocs.yml') }}-
203	            social-
204	      - run: uv sync --extra docs
205	      - run: uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
206	      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
207	        with:
208	          path: site
209	
210	  deploy:
211	    needs: build
212	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
213	    environment:
214	      name: github-pages
215	      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
216	    steps:
217	      - id: deployment
218	        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
219	```
220	
221	You also need to enable Pages in your repo settings: **Settings → Pages
222	→ Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**. One-time setup.
223	
224	## Multilingual build contract
225	
226	When `mkdocs-static-i18n` is enabled, add the same `enabled: !ENV [...]`
227	guard to its plugin block (and to `social` when present):
228	
229	```yaml
230	plugins:
231	  - i18n:
232	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_I18N_ENABLED, true]
233	      docs_structure: suffix
234	      languages:
235	        - locale: en
236	          default: true
237	          name: English
238	        - locale: zh-TW
239	          name: 繁體中文
240	          build: true
241	  - social:
242	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
243	      # ... only when social cards are enabled
244	```
245	
246	Do not deploy a multilingual site with a single direct `mkdocs build`:
247	`mkdocs-static-i18n` runs the build once per locale, while `mkdocs-llmstxt`
248	resets its page index and overwrites the same root files each time. The result
249	can be nearly empty or contain the wrong locale even when a non-strict build
250	exits successfully.
251	
252	The scaffolded `scripts/build-docs-site.py` is the production entry point:
253	
254	- monolingual: one strict [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] with llmstxt enabled;
255	- multilingual with llmstxt: one strict default-language LLM [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] plus one
256	  strict full HTML [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], followed by validation and an atomic replacement of
257	  `site/`;
258	- multilingual without llmstxt: one strict HTML [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri];
259	- root `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars: default language only;
260	- direct `mkdocs serve` / `mkdocs build --strict`: safe HTML-only preview.
261	
262	If an older scaffold still invokes `mkdocs build --strict` in CI, follow
263	[`i18n-llmstxt-migration.md`](i18n-llmstxt-migration.md). Updating the skill
264	downloads the migration tool but does not modify the project.
265	
266	## Linking rules inside `docs/`
267	
268	`mkdocs build --strict` enforces these rules. Knowing them up front
269	saves an afternoon:
270	
271	- Links **between files inside `docs/`** → relative paths (e.g.
272	  `[scripts](../reference/scripts.md)`).
273	- Links to **`.md` files outside `docs/`** → absolute GitHub URL
274	  (e.g. `https://github.com/yourname/your-project/blob/main/TODO.md`).
275	  Relative paths to `.md` files outside `docs/` are rejected by
276	  `--strict`.
277	- Links to **directories or non-`.md` files outside `docs/`** → relative
278	  paths are tolerated (downgraded to INFO).
279	- Links to root build artifacts such as `llms.txt` → use full URLs based on
280	  `site_url` (for example,
281	  `https://yourname.github.io/your-project/llms.txt`). They are not source
282	  Markdown files and should not be used as relative source links. Do not use
283	  `/llms.txt` for GitHub project Pages; that drops the repository subpath.
284	
285	If you want stricter validation (catch broken anchors too):
286	
287	```yaml
288	validation:
289	  links:
290	    not_found: warn
291	    anchors: warn
292	```
293	
294	## What this repo skips and why
295	
296	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — there's no Python API to document. We
297	  installed everything else from the recipe to keep the patterns aligned
298	  with downstream projects.
299	- **Versioned docs (e.g. `mike`)** — single-version docs are enough for
300	  a personal skills collection. Add `mike` if you ever need to keep
301	  docs for old releases live.
302
````

````text
1	# Migrate an existing i18n + llmstxt site
2	
3	Use this guide when a site created by an older `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` release
4	has both `mkdocs-static-i18n` and `mkdocs-llmstxt`, especially when:
5	
6	- `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` is almost empty after adding a language;
7	- the files contain only the final locale;
8	- strict builds report `Page URI ... not found`; or
9	- CI removed `--strict` to make the build [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri].
10	
11	The safe target is a strict two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build: multilingual HTML in one [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri],
12	default-language LLM artifacts in another, then validation and an atomic merge.
13	
14	## Updating the skill is not the migration
15	
16	From the downstream project's root, first download the current tooling:
17	
18	```bash
19	npx skills@latest update mkdocs-site-bootstrap --project --yes
20	```
21	
22	This updates the installed skill under `.agents/skills/`. It deliberately does
23	**not** edit the project's `mkdocs.yml`, workflow, Makefile, or scripts. Run the
24	migration tool separately and review its findings.
25	
26	## Audit, preview, apply, verify
27	
28	### 1. Audit without writing
29	
30	```bash
31	bash .agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh \
32	  --target-dir . --json
33	```
34	
35	Audit is the default. Exit `10` is an expected result: it means the legacy
36	affected shape was found. Read `changes[]` and `manual_actions[]` in the JSON
37	before proceeding.
38	
39	### 2. Preview the conservative patch
40	
41	```bash
42	bash .agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh \
43	  --target-dir . --apply --dry-run --json
44	```
45	
46	`--apply --dry-run` computes the same patch as a real apply but writes nothing.
47	If a proposed change would replace intentional customization, stop and perform
48	that item manually.
49	
50	### 3. Apply and run strict verification
51	
52	```bash
53	bash .agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh \
54	  --target-dir . --apply --verify --json
55	```
56	
57	On a fully recognized old scaffold this:
58	
59	- adds `docs_dir` and plugin environment guards to `mkdocs.yml`;
60	- rewrites the exact legacy snippets base path (`.`, `docs`,
61	  `docs/_snippets`) to follow the guarded docs directory;
62	- adds Material's `content.action.edit` feature;
63	- installs or refreshes the marker-owned `scripts/build-docs-site.py`;
64	- changes the exact scaffolded workflow/Makefile build command to invoke the
65	  helper; and
66	- adds the helper to the workflow path filter.
67	
68	It also audits non-default `*.LOCALE.md` / `*.LOCALE.markdown` sources for
69	relative links to `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, or generated `*/index.md`
70	sidecars. Each unsafe link is reported as a manual action; the tool does not
71	guess the deployment URL or rewrite prose automatically.
72	
73	The tool stages and validates every candidate before replacing project files,
74	and the migration is idempotent. A second identical run reports `status: safe`
75	and `changed: false`. Verification invokes the helper (using
76	`uv run --extra docs` when the project declares that optional dependency
77	group), so both the default-language LLM [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] and full multilingual HTML [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
78	remain strict.
79	
80	## Exit codes and JSON
81	
82	| Exit | Meaning |
83	|---:|---|
84	| `0` | Already safe, or migrated and verified with no manual work remaining |
85	| `10` | Audit/dry-run found an affected legacy configuration; no files changed |
86	| `11` | Safe apply completed, but `manual_actions[]` still requires work |
87	| `12` | The strict two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] verification failed |
88	| `1` | Invalid arguments or incompatible flag use |
89	| `2` | Target/config file is missing |
90	| `4` | Required `yq`/config parsing or migration staging failed |
91	
92	With `--json`, stdout is one object suitable for an agent or CI wrapper:
93	
94	```json
95	{
96	  "status": "affected",
97	  "affected": true,
98	  "changed": false,
99	  "dry_run": false,
100	  "verified": null,
101	  "changes": [],
102	  "manual_actions": []
103	}
104	```
105	
106	Diagnostics and build logs go to stderr. Do not treat exit `10` as a generic
107	tool crash; it is the audit signal that a migration is needed. `verified` is
108	`null` when verification was not requested, `true` after a successful helper
109	run, and `false` on exit `12`.
110	
111	## Automatic patch boundary
112	
113	The tool only edits shapes it can identify without guessing:
114	
115	- absent `docs_dir`, or literal `docs_dir: docs`;
116	- the exact legacy `pymdownx.snippets.base_path` list `[., docs,
117	  docs/_snippets]`;
118	- map-form `i18n`, `llmstxt`, `copy-to-llm`, and optional `social` plugin
119	  entries whose `enabled` values are not already customized;
120	- a missing helper, or a helper carrying the exact
121	  `# mkdocs-site-bootstrap-managed: two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]-build-v1` marker;
122	- the exact build line from the scaffolded GitHub workflow; and
123	- the exact scaffolded `docs-build` Makefile command.
124	
125	It refuses to overwrite or infer around:
126	
127	- a custom/out-of-repo `docs_dir` or symlinked source tree;
128	- top-level MkDocs `INHERIT` or a custom snippets `base_path` shape;
129	- custom plugin `enabled` expressions or non-map plugin shapes;
130	- a same-named helper without the managed marker;
131	- custom CI, deployment, or Makefile build logic;
132	- folder-layout i18n or an ambiguous default locale; and
133	- relative generated-artifact links inside localized sources.
134	
135	Those cases are returned in `manual_actions[]`; exit `11` keeps them visible.
136	Do not use `--force` or copy over a foreign helper. Adapt the manual recipe
137	below to the project's existing conventions.
138	
139	## Manual recipe for customized sites
140	
141	Preserve the project's values while introducing these invariants:
142	
143	```yaml
144	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
145	
146	theme:
147	  features:
148	    - content.action.edit
149	
150	plugins:
151	  - i18n:
152	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_I18N_ENABLED, true]
153	      # preserve the existing i18n settings
154	  - llmstxt:
155	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
156	      # preserve full_output and sections
157	  - copy-to-llm:
158	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
159	      # preserve the existing settings
160	
161	markdown_extensions:
162	  - pymdownx.snippets:
163	      base_path:
164	        - .
165	        - !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
166	      check_paths: true
167	```
168	
169	If `social` exists, give it
170	`enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]` as well. Copy the
171	current canonical helper only when it will not overwrite a project-owned
172	script, then change production build entry points to:
173	
174	```bash
175	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
176	```
177	
178	Keep direct `mkdocs serve` / `mkdocs build --strict` for HTML-only preview.
179	Root `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars intentionally represent
180	the default language only; do not create or link to guessed locale-relative
181	paths such as `/zh-TW/llms.txt`.
182	
183	Replace reported generated-artifact links with full URLs derived from the
184	project's `site_url`, including any GitHub Pages repository subpath. For
185	example, use `https://owner.github.io/project/llms.txt`, not `/llms.txt`.
186	
187	Finally, run the helper and inspect at least one default-language sidecar, one
188	translated HTML page, and both root llms files. Removing `--strict` or demoting
189	link warnings is not a migration: it can make CI green while leaving the LLM
190	artifacts corrupted.

````text
1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` omits `nav` so MkDocs auto-generates navigation
36	  from the filesystem. (`nav: []` is not equivalent: it explicitly selects no
37	  pages.)
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing `.md` and `.markdown` page paths
46	  into an explicit path-only `nav:` list** so the user can see/reorder them
47	  later. Paths are relative to `docs/`, safely YAML-quoted, and sorted
48	  alphabetically under the C locale; non-Markdown files and `_snippets/`
49	  include fragments are not navigation pages.
50	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to use a
51	  deterministic alphabetical order.
52	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
53	  content is already there.
54	
55	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
56	
57	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
58	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
59	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
60	  has been asked once.
61	
62	## What "non-hidden files" means
63	
64	For the purposes of this check:
65	
66	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
67	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
68	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
69	  "no existing content".
70	
71	Implementation hint:
72	
73	```bash
74	find docs -type f \
75	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
76	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
77	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
78	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
79	  | head -50
80	```
81	
82	## Things this skill must NOT do
83	
84	- **Don't follow symlinks under `docs/`.** Refuse the bootstrap before writing;
85	  `--force` must never turn a linked page into an overwrite outside the target
86	  repository.
87	- **Don't enable build plugins that mutate existing docs implicitly.** The
88	  generated `skip`/`wrap` configuration omits `copy-to-llm` because its build
89	  hook writes `docs/assets/copy-to-llm/`; adding it later is a separate opt-in.
90	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
91	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
92	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
93	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
94	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
95	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
96	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
97	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
98	  breaks rendering.
99	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
100	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
101	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
102	
103	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
104	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
105	
106	## After bootstrap
107	
108	Whichever option was chosen, run the complete strict validation path:
109	
110	```bash
111	uv sync --extra docs
112	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
113	```
114	
115	There is no non-strict compatibility escape hatch. The helper uses one strict
116	[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] for these llmstxt-free `skip`/`wrap` configurations and is also the
117	production entry point if plugins are enabled later. Report:
118	
119	- Any errors or warnings → must be fixed before deploy; preserve the user's
120	  content and ask before a fix would rewrite it
121	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
122	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
123	
124	## Recording the decision
125	
126	```bash
127	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
128	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
129	```
130	
131	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
132	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
133
