1	# Bilingual / multi-language docs
2	
3	How to add a non-English language (typically Traditional Chinese, `zh-TW`) to
4	a MkDocs Material site bootstrapped by this skill, and how to keep
5	terminology consistent so future contributors — human or agent — don't
6	introduce ambiguity.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	```bash
11	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
12	uv sync --extra docs
13	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
14	```
15	
16	The Material header gains a language switcher. The managed build helper keeps
17	both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es strict, publishes all locale HTML, and produces root `llms.txt`,
18	`llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars from the default language only. Translate
19	the stub bodies when ready.
20	
21	For local HTML preview, `uv run mkdocs serve` and direct `uv run mkdocs build
22	--strict` remain safe: the config disables `llmstxt` unless the helper enables
23	it. Use the helper for every artifact that will be deployed.
24	
25	## Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure
26	
27	[Squidfunk's recommended approach](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/discussions/2346)
28	for content translation is the
29	[`mkdocs-static-i18n`](https://github.com/ultrabug/mkdocs-static-i18n) plugin.
30	We use **`docs_structure: suffix`** rather than `folder` because:
31	
32	- **Zero file moves on retrofit.** Existing `docs/index.md`,
33	  `docs/getting-started.md`, etc. stay where they are. The `folder` mode
34	  would force you to move every file into `docs/en/` first.
35	- **Relative links keep working.** Sibling files share the same directory.
36	- **Per-page opt-in to translation.** A page is only translated when
37	  `<page>.<lang>.md` exists; otherwise the plugin falls back to the default
38	  language (`fallback_to_default: true`).
39	
40	The trade-off: directory listings get crowded once you have many languages.
41	For sites that grow to 5+ languages the `folder` structure starts to win on
42	readability — but you can migrate later.
43	
44	## Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement)
45	
46	This is the rule for any non-English page in a project that uses this skill:
47	
48	> **在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞首次出現時，以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現。**
49	> 例：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」、「型別檢查 (type checking)」。
50	> 後續同段內可只用中文。
51	>
52	> **不自創翻譯。** 若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
53	> `mkdocs-static-i18n`、`pymdownx.snippets`）。
54	>
55	> **代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。**
56	
57	The reason: Chinese-language tech writing has competing translations for
58	many terms (e.g. `cache` → 快取 / 緩存 / 暫存; `repository` → 倉庫 / 儲存庫 /
59	版本庫). Keeping the English original on first mention removes the ambiguity
60	without forcing readers to guess which translation the author meant. It also
61	keeps the page grep-able for English search terms.
62	
63	`add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh` inject this rule as an admonition
64	at the top of every non-default-language stub so authors see it before they
65	start translating.
66	
67	## What `add-language.sh` does, step by step
68	
69	For users who want to apply pieces by hand or audit what the script touched:
70	
71	1. **Locates `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD.
72	2. **Detects existing i18n state.** `yq` query against `.plugins[]` checks
73	   for an `i18n:` map.
74	3. **Inserts or extends `plugins.i18n`.**
75	   - If absent: prepends a fresh i18n block before `search`, with
76	     `[default-lang, new-lang]` as the language list.
77	   - If present and the new locale isn't there: appends to
78	     `plugins[].i18n.languages`.
79	   - If the locale is already present: no-op.
80	4. **Sets `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
81	   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` warns when `theme.language` is missing).
82	5. **Removes `navigation.instant` / `navigation.instant.progress`** from
83	   `theme.features` (the language switcher's contextual link can't be
84	   rewritten by instant navigation).
85	6. **Keeps default-language `mkdocs-llmstxt` output by default.** It adds the
86	   environment guards and managed `scripts/build-docs-site.py` required to
87	   isolate llmstxt from the multilingual build. Use `--remove-llmstxt` for an
88	   explicit opt-out. Legacy `--drop-strict` is a deprecated no-op;
89	   `--keep-llmstxt` is a deprecated alias for the default behavior.
90	7. **Walks `docs/`** for `*.md` files (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`),
91	   and for each non-locale-suffixed source page, creates a sibling
92	   `*.<LANG>.md` from `assets/translation-stub.md.template`.
93	8. **Updates `.skills/preferences.yaml`** with three keys:
94	   `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages` (ordered list, default first),
95	   `keep_english_terms: true`, `i18n_structure: suffix`.
96	9. **Un-comments `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2`** in `pyproject.toml`. If the
97	   line isn't there at all, prints a hint asking you to add it manually.
98	
99	The script is idempotent: re-running with the same `--lang` is a no-op. Exit
100	`11` means the locale/stubs were added and the safe migration subset was
101	applied, but custom downstream files still need the manual actions reported by
102	`migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh --json`.
103	
104	## `theme.language` vs plugin `languages`
105	
106	These are two different things:
107	
108	- [`theme.language`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/)
109	  is **Material's UI strings** (search placeholder, "Edit this page", footer
110	  navigation hints). One value site-wide. Material ships translations for
111	  ~70 locales out of the box.
112	- `plugins.i18n.languages` is **content translation**. A list. Each entry
113	  declares a locale that has translated `*.<lang>.md` files.
114	
115	You almost always want `theme.language` set to your default content language
116	so the UI matches when readers land on a default-language page.
117	
118	## `nav_translations`
119	
120	To translate section titles in the nav (e.g. `Workflows` → `工作流程`), use
121	`mkdocs-static-i18n`'s per-language `nav_translations`:
122	
123	```yaml
124	plugins:
125	  - i18n:
126	      docs_structure: suffix
127	      languages:
128	        - locale: en
129	          name: English
130	          default: true
131	        - locale: zh-TW
132	          name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
133	          nav_translations:
134	            Workflows: 工作流程
135	            Reference: 參考資料
136	```
137	
138	`add-language.sh` does **not** populate `nav_translations` for you —
139	section names are project-specific and translating them is a deliberate
140	authorial choice. Add them by hand once you have section titles to translate.
141	
142	!!! warning "Don't apply 「中文 (English original)」 to nav labels"
143	    The terminology rule that governs body prose **does not extend to
144	    `nav_translations` values.** Nav entries are navigation chrome — short
145	    labels in a sidebar — and bilingual labels like
146	    `Reference: 參考資料 (Reference)` are too long, wrap awkwardly, and
147	    duplicate information the URL slug already preserves.
148	
149	    For nav labels: pick the most common Chinese term for each section
150	    and stick with it. Stay consistent across the whole nav. The URL
151	    slug still uses the English source name (`/zh-TW/reference/...`),
152	    so search engines and direct-link sharing are unaffected.
153	
154	    Examples:
155	
156	    | English heading | Good zh-TW label | Bad zh-TW label |
157	    |---|---|---|
158	    | `Reference` | `參考資料` | `參考資料 (Reference)` |
159	    | `Workflows` | `工作流程` | `工作流程 (Workflows)` |
160	    | `Skills` | `Skills` (keep — domain term, no canonical translation) | `技能 (Skills)` |
161	    | `Getting started` | `快速開始` | `快速開始 (Getting started)` |
162	
163	    The "keep English" exception (third row) is reserved for terms where
164	    no canonical Chinese translation exists. When in doubt, keep English
165	    — it matches the body-prose rule's spirit (don't invent) without
166	    duplicating into the label.
167	
168	## Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`
169	
170	### Why one multilingual build is unsafe
171	
172	This is not merely a strict-mode compatibility warning, and
173	`reconfigure_material` is not the root cause:
174	
175	1. `mkdocs-static-i18n` performs a full MkDocs build for each locale.
176	2. `mkdocs-llmstxt` resets its collected page state for each build.
177	3. Every locale writes the same root `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` paths.
178	
179	The last locale therefore overwrites the valid default-language output. With
180	explicit `sections:` paths, translated source URIs no longer match and the
181	last files may contain only a heading. With globs, the files may look large but
182	contain the wrong locale. Strict mode exposes `Page URI ... not found`
183	warnings; a non-strict build silently ships the corrupted files. Removing
184	`--strict`, changing plugin order, toggling `reconfigure_material`, or using
185	globs does not solve the lifecycle collision.
186	
187	### Canonical two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build
188	
189	Run:
190	
191	```bash
192	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
193	```
194	
195	For a multilingual site with llmstxt enabled, the helper:
196	
197	1. Builds a temporary default-language-only source tree with i18n,
198	   copy-to-llm, and social disabled and llmstxt enabled.
199	2. Verifies `llms.txt`, the configured full output, every expected section,
200	   and generated `.md` sidecars.
201	3. Builds the full multilingual source tree with i18n/copy/social enabled and
202	   llmstxt disabled.
203	4. Merges the verified default-language LLM artifacts, rejects non-default
204	   locale paths, and only then replaces the final `site/` directory.
205	
206	Both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es are strict. The helper has no non-strict escape hatch. A failed
207	[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] leaves the previous `site/` untouched; use `--keep-temp` only when you
208	need to inspect the staged trees.
209	
210	The corresponding `mkdocs.yml` guards are:
211	
212	```yaml
213	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
214	
215	plugins:
216	  - i18n:
217	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_I18N_ENABLED, true]
218	      # ...
219	  - llmstxt:
220	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
221	      # ...
222	  - copy-to-llm:
223	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
224	      # ...
225	  - social:
226	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
227	      # ... only when social cards were enabled
228	```
229	
230	The default `false` for llmstxt is deliberate: direct `mkdocs serve` and
231	`mkdocs build --strict` are HTML-only and cannot accidentally overwrite the
232	canonical LLM artifact. CI and deploy workflows must invoke the helper.
233	
234	### Output and copy-to-LLM contract
235	
236	- Root `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and raw `.md` sidecars represent the
237	  **default language only**. This skill does not generate per-locale llms files.
238	- Keep Material's `content.action.edit` feature and a valid `repo_url` /
239	  `edit_uri`. The copy-to-LLM assets use the page's GitHub edit URL to derive
240	  the correct raw source, including a translated `*.zh-TW.md` sibling, instead
241	  of guessing from the locale site URL.
242	- `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button labels remain English-only on non-English pages.
243	  This is cosmetic and does not affect the source selected by the button.
244	
245	To opt out of LLM artifacts entirely:
246	
247	```bash
248	bash scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --remove-llmstxt
249	```
250	
251	Do not use `validation.links.not_found: info` or remove strict merely to make a
252	red build green. Fix source links and use a full deployed URL derived from
253	`site_url`, such as `https://owner.github.io/project/llms.txt`. A leading
254	`/llms.txt` is wrong for GitHub project Pages because it drops the repository
255	subpath.
256	
257	- **The translation-stub admonition is zh-TW-specific.** The terminology
258	  rule it injects is written for Traditional Chinese and uses the
259	  「中文 (English original)」 format. If you add `--lang ja` or another
260	  language, the admonition still says "Terminology rule (ja pages)" but the

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# enable-pages.sh — Enable GitHub Pages (Actions source) and trigger first deploy.
3	#
4	# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `gh` (GitHub CLI), authenticated.
5	#
6	# IMPORTANT: This is a high-trust action. The agent invoking this should have
7	# already obtained explicit user consent for the API call. The script itself
8	# enforces nothing beyond --dry-run; consent gating happens upstream in SKILL.md.
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	usage() {
13	  cat <<'EOF'
14	Usage: enable-pages.sh [OPTIONS]
15	
16	Enable GitHub Pages with Actions as source (POST /repos/:owner/:repo/pages
17	with build_type=workflow), then trigger the docs.yml workflow.
18	
19	Options:
20	  --repo OWNER/REPO     Target repo (default: current repo via `gh repo view`).
21	  --workflow NAME       Workflow file to dispatch (default: docs.yml).
22	  --no-trigger          Enable Pages but don't trigger workflow run.
23	  --dry-run             Print the gh commands without executing.
24	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
25	
26	Examples:
27	  enable-pages.sh --repo daviddwlee84/agent-skills
28	  enable-pages.sh --dry-run
29	  enable-pages.sh --no-trigger --repo owner/repo
30	
31	Exit codes:
32	  0  success
33	  1  invalid arguments
34	  2  gh not installed or not authenticated
35	  3  Pages API call failed (already enabled is OK; other errors not OK)
36	  4  workflow trigger failed
37	EOF
38	}
39	
40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
42	
43	REPO=""
44	WORKFLOW="docs.yml"
45	NO_TRIGGER=0
46	DRY_RUN=0
47	
48	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
49	  case "$1" in
50	    --repo)        REPO="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
51	    --workflow)    WORKFLOW="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --no-trigger)  NO_TRIGGER=1; shift ;;
53	    --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h)     usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)            die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)             die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
57	  esac
58	done
59	
60	command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh CLI not found in PATH (install: brew install gh)" 2
61	gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not authenticated (run: gh auth login)" 2
62	
63	# Resolve repo from current dir if not supplied.
64	if [ -z "$REPO" ]; then
65	  REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null || true)
66	  [ -n "$REPO" ] || die "could not detect repo from current dir; [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] --repo OWNER/REPO" 1
67	fi
68	log "Target repo: $REPO"
69	
70	# --- 1. Enable Pages ---
71	PAGES_CMD="gh api -X POST repos/$REPO/pages -f build_type=workflow"
72	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
73	  log "[dry-run] $PAGES_CMD"
74	else
75	  log "Enabling GitHub Pages..."
76	  # Capture both stdout and stderr; tolerate "already enabled" 409.
77	  set +e
78	  OUT=$(gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/pages" -f 'build_type=workflow' 2>&1)
79	  RC=$?
80	  set -e
81	  if [ $RC -ne 0 ]; then
82	    case "$OUT" in
83	      *"already enabled"*|*"409"*)
84	        log "Pages already enabled — continuing."
85	        ;;
86	      *)
87	        die "Pages API call failed: $OUT" 3

11	usage() {
12	  cat <<'EOF'
13	Usage: check-preferences.sh [OPTIONS]
14	
15	Read, write, or reset entries in .skills/preferences.yaml (per-repo).
16	
17	Options:
18	  --get KEY                  Print the value at KEY (e.g., mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled).
19	                             Prints empty string + exits 0 if absent.
20	  --set KEY=VALUE            Set a key. Repeatable. VALUE is parsed as YAML
21	                             (so 'true', '42', '2026-04-23', and bare strings
22	                             all work). Quote complex values.
23	  --reset NAMESPACE          Delete the entire top-level NAMESPACE key (returns
24	                             that skill to "never asked" state).
25	  --list                     Print the entire file (or "(empty)" if missing).
26	  --file PATH                Override file location (default: .skills/preferences.yaml
27	                             at the current Git worktree root, or in the current
28	                             directory when outside Git).
29	  --json                     Format --get / --list output as JSON.
30	  --dry-run                  Print actions but don't write.
31	  --help, -h                 Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Examples:
34	  check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
35	  check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
36	                       --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
37	  check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
38	  check-preferences.sh --list --json
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0  success (key absent on --get is also success — empty stdout)
42	  1  invalid arguments
43	  2  file/dir not accessible
44	  3  yq missing or yq error
45	EOF
46	}
47

49	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

52	ACTION=""
53	KEY=""
54	NAMESPACE=""
55	FILE=""
56	JSON=0
57	DRY_RUN=0
58	SET_PAIRS=()
59	
60	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
61	  case "$1" in
62	    --get)        ACTION="get"; KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
63	    --set)        ACTION="set"; SET_PAIRS+=("${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
64	    --reset)      ACTION="reset"; NAMESPACE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
65	    --list)       ACTION="list"; shift ;;
66	    --file)       FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
67	    --json)       JSON=1; shift ;;
68	    --dry-run)    DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
69	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
70	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
71	    *)            die "unexpected positional argument: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
72	  esac
73	done

76	
77	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 3
78	
79	# --- file resolution ---

82	    :
83	  else
84	    ROOT="$(pwd)"
85	  fi
86	  FILE="$ROOT/.skills/preferences.yaml"
87	fi
88

91	  dir="$(dirname "$FILE")"
92	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then

94	    mkdir -p "$dir"
95	  fi

97	    [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && { log "[dry-run] touch $FILE with header"; return 0; }
98	    cat >"$FILE" <<'EOF'

103	EOF

83	## `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` — Snyk Med Risk (expected)
84	
85	This one is **not** a transitive-dependency CVE — pinning, bumping, or
86	removing a package will not change the score.
87	
88	- **Rule:** `W011` — Third-party content exposure / indirect prompt injection
89	- **Risk score:** 0.90
90	- **Snyk's rationale (verbatim):**
91	  > The agent will read untrusted, user-generated third-party docs that could
92	  > contain instructions and thus enable indirect prompt injection.
93	
94	The skill ships templates that install `mkdocs-llmstxt` and `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`
95	by default, which produce:
96	
97	- `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` — full-content dumps intended for LLM ingestion
98	- Per-page "copy as markdown for LLM" buttons
99	
100	On multilingual sites, the managed `scripts/build-docs-site.py` isolates
101	`mkdocs-llmstxt` from `mkdocs-static-i18n`: root llms files and raw `.md`
102	sidecars contain the default language only, while translated HTML is built in
103	a separate strict [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. Direct `mkdocs build --strict` is an HTML-only preview.
104	This fixes empty/wrong-locale output; it is **not** a trust boundary and does
105	not sanitize the default-language docs.
106	
107	Any LLM-driven agent that consumes those endpoints is reading whatever ended
108	up in `docs/`. If `docs/` accepts external contributions (e.g. open-source
109	PRs), an attacker can plant prompt-injection payloads in a doc page and have
110	them flow into a downstream agent's context. Snyk's W0xx ruleset flags that
111	agent-facing surface.
112	
113	### Why we accept the score
114	
115	The whole point of dogfooding `mkdocs-llmstxt` + copy-to-llm is to make these
116	docs LLM-friendly; degrading that defeats the skill. A real fix is **trust
117	modeling**, not a dependency change:
118	
119	- Treat `docs/` as an LLM input boundary (CODEOWNERS on `docs/**`, require
120	  review for external PRs).
121	- Document the threat in the skill so downstream users opt in knowingly.
122	
123	A future opt-out flag on `init-docs-site.sh` (e.g. `--no-llmstxt`) for repos
124	that don't want the LLM-facing surface is tracked in `TODO.md` rather than

 `https://zensical.org/docs/setup/language/`

```text
This page documents **theme/interface localization and links to alternate-language sites**, not a workflow for building translated content files.

- **Site language:** Set one canonical language for the whole project with `project.theme.language` in `zensical.toml` (or `theme.language` in `mkdocs.yml`). The page says HTML5 permits “a single language per document,” so Zensical does not describe setting different canonical languages for individual content files.
- **Language selector:** Configure `project.extra.alternate` (or `extra.alternate`) with each language’s name, link, and language code. The link can point to another domain or subdomain; a relative link gets the configured `site_url` domain prepended. The `lang` value is used for the link’s `hreflang`.
- **Language codes:** The list distinguishes Chinese (Taiwanese), `zh-TW`, from Chinese (Traditional), `zh-Hant`. Use the code appropriate to the language you’re identifying.
- **Direction:** Text direction is inferred from the selected language, or set explicitly with `project.theme.direction` / `theme.direction`.

The page does **not** document building multiple content locales from filenames such as `foo.zh-TW.md`, locale fallback for content, or translated navigation. It describes configuring a project’s theme language and listing alternate sites; don’t infer that it provides those other capabilities.
```

```text
### Migration in `mkdocs.yml`
Zensical can use the existing configuration, so switching builders does **not** require rewriting it as `zensical.toml`. The page says the `hooks` setting is not supported.

For `validation`, strict mode, excludes, `markdown_extensions`, watch, redirects, and `site_url`, this page does not specify whether they are supported or ignored. It links to a configuration reference but provides no details about those settings here.

### Theme and overrides
Set `theme.variant` to `classic` to retain the Material for MkDocs appearance; `modern` is the other variant. The page says the HTML structure stays the same. Material for MkDocs template overrides based on version 9.6.18 or later should generally work; older or heavily customized overrides may need changes for MiniJinja compatibility.

### CLI
`gh-deploy` is not provided. The page recommends using a suitable publishing method instead. It also identifies `--theme`, `--use-directory-urls`, and `--site-dir` as unsupported command-line options, with configuration alternatives for the latter two.
```

````text
### `llmstxt` — since 0.0.67

Zensical generates an `llms.txt` index and Markdown versions of selected pages.

```yaml
plugins:
  - llmstxt:
      sections:
        Docs:
          - index.md
          - guides/*.md
      markdown_description: "Optional description"
      base_url: https://example.com
      full_output: llms-full.txt
      autoclean: true
```

The equivalent TOML configuration uses `[project.plugins.llmstxt]` with the same setting names.

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Enable generation. |
| `sections` | Required | Named sections and source pages; page paths may use glob patterns. |
| `markdown_description` | `null` | Markdown description appended after the site description. |
| `base_url` | `site_url` | Base URL for links to generated Markdown pages. |
| `full_output` | `null` | Optional path for a file containing the full text of selected pages. |
| `autoclean` | `true` | Clean generated HTML before converting it to Markdown. |

**Differences:** The theme’s `content.action.copy` feature adds a “Copy as Markdown” button to pages with Markdown equivalents. Custom Python preprocessing via `preprocess` is ignored. Mkdocstrings source listings and empty code elements are omitted even when `autoclean` is disabled. `full_output` must be a relative file path inside `site_dir`, distinct from `llms.txt`; absolute paths and paths with empty, `.` or `..` components are rejected.

The page links to the [llmstxt plugin documentation](https://pawamoy.github.io/mkdocs-llmstxt/).
````
</details></tool-use>

1	# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
2	
3	The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
4	`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
5	the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
6	**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
11	  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
12	  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
13	- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
14	  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
15	  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
16	- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
17	  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
18	  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
19	  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
20	- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
21	  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.
22	
23	## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
24	
25	Per the Material team's analysis
26	([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):
27	
28	| Change | Impact on this stack |
29	|---|---|
30	| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
31	| Theme system rewritten — nav [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
32	| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
33	| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
34	| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |
35	
36	The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
37	describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
38	publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
39	There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
40	maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
41	user-driven (solve a specific pain).
42	
43	## Material team's response — Zensical
44	
45	[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
46	MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
47	MkDocs 1.x**.
48	
49	What's known:
50	
51	- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
52	- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
53	- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
54	  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
55	- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
56	  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
57	- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.
58	
59	The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
60	due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
61	strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.
62	
63	## Why we cap explicitly
64	
65	Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
66	which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
67	accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:
68	
69	- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
70	- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
71	  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
72	- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
73	  else's defensive pin to stay correct.
74	
75	The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
76	bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
77	patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.
78	
79	## When to re-evaluate
80	
81	Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
82	following are true**:
83	
84	1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
85	   equivalent project signal of API stability).
86	2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
87	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
88	   per-language search).
89	3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
90	   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
91	   per-page raw-markdown links).
92	4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
93	   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).
94	
95	Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
96	MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
97	them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.
98	
99	## What to avoid
100	
101	- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
102	  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
103	- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
104	  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
105	  individual users.
106	- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
107	  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
108	  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
109	- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
110	  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
111	  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.
112	
113	## Re-checking the situation
114	
115	A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:
116	
117	1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
118	   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
119	   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
120	2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
121	   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
122	3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
123	   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
124	   release date been set?
125	4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
126	   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
127	   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
128	   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.
129	
130	## Source links
131	
132	- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
133	  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
134	- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
135	- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
136	- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>

168	## Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`
169	
170	### Why one multilingual build is unsafe
171	
172	This is not merely a strict-mode compatibility warning, and
173	`reconfigure_material` is not the root cause:
174	
175	1. `mkdocs-static-i18n` performs a full MkDocs build for each locale.
176	2. `mkdocs-llmstxt` resets its collected page state for each build.
177	3. Every locale writes the same root `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` paths.
178	
179	The last locale therefore overwrites the valid default-language output. With
180	explicit `sections:` paths, translated source URIs no longer match and the
181	last files may contain only a heading. With globs, the files may look large but
182	contain the wrong locale. Strict mode exposes `Page URI ... not found`
183	warnings; a non-strict build silently ships the corrupted files. Removing
184	`--strict`, changing plugin order, toggling `reconfigure_material`, or using
185	globs does not solve the lifecycle collision.
186	
187	### Canonical two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build
188	
189	Run:
190	
191	```bash
192	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
193	```
194	
195	For a multilingual site with llmstxt enabled, the helper:
196	
197	1. Builds a temporary default-language-only source tree with i18n,
198	   copy-to-llm, and social disabled and llmstxt enabled.
199	2. Verifies `llms.txt`, the configured full output, every expected section,
200	   and generated `.md` sidecars.
201	3. Builds the full multilingual source tree with i18n/copy/social enabled and
202	   llmstxt disabled.
203	4. Merges the verified default-language LLM artifacts, rejects non-default
204	   locale paths, and only then replaces the final `site/` directory.
205	
206	Both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es are strict. The helper has no non-strict escape hatch. A failed
207	[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] leaves the previous `site/` untouched; use `--keep-temp` only when you
208	need to inspect the staged trees.
209	
210	The corresponding `mkdocs.yml` guards are:
211	
212	```yaml
213	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
214	
215	plugins:
216	  - i18n:
217	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_I18N_ENABLED, true]
218	      # ...
219	  - llmstxt:
220	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
221	      # ...
222	  - copy-to-llm:
223	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
224	      # ...
225	  - social:
226	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
227	      # ... only when social cards were enabled
228	```
229	
230	The default `false` for llmstxt is deliberate: direct `mkdocs serve` and
231	`mkdocs build --strict` are HTML-only and cannot accidentally overwrite the
232	canonical LLM artifact. CI and deploy workflows must invoke the helper.
233	
234	### Output and copy-to-LLM contract
235	
236	- Root `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and raw `.md` sidecars represent the
237	  **default language only**. This skill does not generate per-locale llms files.
238	- Keep Material's `content.action.edit` feature and a valid `repo_url` /
239	  `edit_uri`. The copy-to-LLM assets use the page's GitHub edit URL to derive
240	  the correct raw source, including a translated `*.zh-TW.md` sibling, instead
241	  of guessing from the locale site URL.
242	- `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button labels remain English-only on non-English pages.
243	  This is cosmetic and does not affect the source selected by the button.
244	
245	To opt out of LLM artifacts entirely:
246	
247	```bash
248	bash scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --remove-llmstxt
249	```
250	
251	Do not use `validation.links.not_found: info` or remove strict merely to make a
252	red build green. Fix source links and use a full deployed URL derived from
253	`site_url`, such as `https://owner.github.io/project/llms.txt`. A leading
254	`/llms.txt` is wrong for GitHub project Pages because it drops the repository
255	subpath.
256	
257	- **The translation-stub admonition is zh-TW-specific.** The terminology
258	  rule it injects is written for Traditional Chinese and uses the
259	  「中文 (English original)」 format. If you add `--lang ja` or another
260	  language, the admonition still says "Terminology rule (ja pages)" but the
261	  body is in Chinese. Either edit
262	  `assets/translation-stub.md.template` to be language-neutral first, or
263	  hand-edit the stubs after creation.
264	
265	## Removing a language
266	
267	To remove `zh-TW` later:

````text
1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	If you are building documentation for a project that consumes one of the
4	skills in this repo (especially [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
5	or [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)),
6	this is the docs stack we recommend.
7	
8	It's the same stack this repo uses for its own docs, plus the optional
9	`mkdocstrings` layer for projects that have a Python API to document.
10	
11	## TL;DR
12	
13	```toml
14	# pyproject.toml
15	[project.optional-dependencies]
16	docs = [
17	  "mkdocs>=1.6",
18	  "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
19	  # "mkdocs-material[imaging]>=9.5",  # only with --social (cairosvg+pillow)
20	  "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.24",   # only if you have a Python API
21	  "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
22	  "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
23	  "pymdown-extensions>=10.0",
24	]
25	```
26	
27	```bash
28	# Local preview
29	uv sync --extra docs
30	uv run mkdocs serve
31	
32	# Build static site
33	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
34	
35	# Safe HTML-only preview (llmstxt stays disabled)
36	uv run mkdocs build --strict
37	```
38	
39	## Why this stack
40	
41	- **MkDocs + Material** — Markdown-first authoring, built-in search, a
42	  theme that doesn't need overrides for ~90% of projects, GitHub Pages
43	  deploy is one workflow file.
44	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — render API docs from Python docstrings via
45	  `::: package.module.symbol` directives in your Markdown. Only relevant
46	  if your project has a Python API; skip it otherwise.
47	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt`** — generates `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` so
48	  AI agents can discover and consume your docs without scraping HTML.
49	  Upstream is in maintenance mode and must be isolated from a multilingual
50	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` build; the managed helper does that. If it stops working
51	  even in the default-language [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], replace it with a post-build generator.
52	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`** — adds "Copy to LLM / Open in ChatGPT / Open
53	  in Claude" buttons on every page. Pure UX sugar; harmless if your
54	  audience doesn't use it.
55	- **Managed strict build helper** — keeps `mkdocs-static-i18n` and
56	  `mkdocs-llmstxt` out of the same plugin lifecycle. Multilingual HTML is built
57	  separately from default-language LLM artifacts, validated, and merged before
58	  `site/` is replaced.
59	
60	## Why not these?
61	
62	- **Sphinx + Furo + MyST + autodoc.** Strictly more powerful, but the
63	  setup and maintenance cost is meaningful. Recommended only if AI-facing
64	  Markdown output becomes a first-class requirement, or if your project
65	  has the kind of cross-project reference graph Sphinx is built for.
66	- **pdoc.** Single-file API doc generator. Great for "I just want HTML
67	  for my package", but no good story for guides, conventions pages, or
68	  llms.txt.
69	- **Rspress.** Best-in-class for AI-native output, but it's
70	  Node-first / frontend-product-docs-first; Python API reference is a
71	  bolt-on. Not a fit unless you're already on the Node ecosystem.
72	- **Quarto.** Excellent for notebook / tutorial / research-report
73	  workflows; not optimized for Python library documentation.
74	
75	The longer version of this analysis (with the upstream-vs-inference
76	distinction made explicit) is preserved in the reference repo
77	[`mlflow-widgets/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets/blob/main/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md).
78	
79	## Minimum `mkdocs.yml`
80	
81	```yaml
82	site_name: Your Project
83	site_description: One sentence about your project.
84	site_url: https://yourname.github.io/your-project/
85	repo_url: https://github.com/yourname/your-project
````

## 1. 優先修正評估文件，不動建置架構

依提供的截至 **2026-10-30** 上游核對結果，更新既有比較文件：

- Zensical 支援部分插件／對應整合，包括 search、mkdocstrings、autorefs、awesome-nav、mike fork，但各有條件；**不代表支援任意 MkDocs plugin API**。不支援的 plugin 設定可能被靜默忽略，hooks、gen-files 亦不能直接沿用。
- UI 語言與 alternate selector **不等於** static-i18n 的內容翻譯、suffix 命名、導覽翻譯及 fallback；完整 i18n 仍在 roadmap。

Material 的 critical/security 維護將於 **2027-05-05** 結束，應據此安排盤點與替代方案預算；但不以日期或版本是否達 1.0，單獨決定採用與否。

## 2. 舊 skill：只做必要維護，保留完整契約

保留初始化、增頁、增語言、migration audit，以及既有測試和來源保護機制。尤其不能簡化掉：

- 兩次隔離的 strict MkDocs build。
- 多語 HTML 合併。

- 原始文件不受破壞、失敗不污染已發布 site 的 staging 行為。

依賴繼續維持 **`mkdocs>=1.6,<2`、`mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`** 及現有 lock。另修正手動 recipe 第 13–24 行與初始化腳本約第 393–410 行的依賴提示，讓其上限與正確模板一致；這是指引一致性修正，不是升級。

收斂舊 skill 的觸發描述，明確涵蓋既有 MkDocs／Material 維護與指定建立 MkDocs。新 skill 僅接明確的 Zensical 新案；使用者只說「建立文件站」時，先確認需求，不自動切換框架。

## 3. 先做小型 fixture，通過後才正式新增

**這一步尚未執行。** 後續經同意，在隔離本機 fixture 建立數個單語頁面，包含巢狀頁面、圖片、程式碼、站內連結及必要 PyMdown 語法；單語可選繁體中文，不必限定英文。

驗收至少涵蓋：

1. **網站輸出**：導覽、搜尋、圖片、相對連結，以及 GitHub Pages 專案子路徑下的 URL。
2. **LLM 輸出**：實際產生 Markdown counterparts、`llms.txt`、full output；確認 sections、內容範圍及連結正確，不只檢查檔案存在。
3. **互動行為**：Copy as Markdown 按鈕實際可用，且內容符合預期。
4. **不支援設定**：由 skill 的前置檢查拒絕已知不支援的 plugins、hooks、gen-files，不能把「build 成功但功能被忽略」當成通過。
5. **安全性**：既有檔案衝突不覆寫、dry-run 不變更目標、建置失敗保留來源及上次有效輸出。

若原生輸出不足，先記錄差距、縮小支援範圍；**不要為了通過測試，立即複製舊版 two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] helper 或自行模擬 static-i18n。**

## 4. 新 skill 的最低完整範圍

通過上述驗證後，新增獨立的 `zensical-site-bootstrap`，至少提供：

- 適用／不適用情境，以及導回既有 MkDocs 流程的條件。
- 單語初始化模板、明確依賴範圍與可重現 lock。
- 增頁與更新導覽的操作流程。
- 本機預覽、建置、輸出驗收與故障排查指引。
- 預設僅檢查和建置的 CI 範例；Pages 部署另外明確 opt-in。
- 初始化、重跑／衝突處理及輸出契約測試。

遵守禁止跨 skill namespace 的偏好，不呼叫 sibling skill 的腳本。既有 Pages helper 雖然框架中立，但獨立安裝不能假設它存在；初版採自足的最小 workflow 範本即可，暫不抽取大型共用框架。

同步維護 marketplace 的 `03-infra-and-docs` 清單，保持既有名稱不變；新 skill 維持 downstream-only，不建立 discovery symlinks。

# GitHub Pages 文件框架與 skill：評估結論及落地順序

## Context

使用者有多個既有專案依賴 `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` 與 MkDocs plugins，想評估新專案是否改用 Zensical，以及是否應另建 skill。這次只做評估：已讀取現有實作並查核官方資料，**未修改技能、遷移站點、安裝套件、執行建置或操作遠端 Issue／部署**。

## 建議結論

**採雙軌：保留 `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`，另外新增範圍較小的 `zensical-site-bootstrap`；不要把舊 skill 原地改造成另一個引擎。** 新 skill 先經小型實際建置驗證，再發布。

| 專案情況 | 建議 |
|---|---|
| 既有 MkDocs + Material，依賴 i18n／自訂 plugins／hooks | 維持 MkDocs 1.x，保留上限與 lockfile，按專案盤點後才遷移 |
| 新的單語 Python／CLI／一般工具文件，需求落在已支援功能 | 優先試用 Zensical；通過驗收後作為此類專案的新預設 |
| 新專案立即需要現有 suffix 雙語、fallback、翻譯導覽與 LLM 輸出契約 | 暫用現有 MkDocs skill；「新專案」不代表應犧牲必要功能 |
| 本 repo 的文件站 | 暫不遷移：目前有完整雙語與兩階段 LLM 建置流程 |

GitHub Pages 仍適合這些站點。它提供靜態資源，建置時的 Python／Rust／Node 工具由 Actions 執行；**換文件引擎與換 hosting 是兩個獨立決策**。暫不增加第三個涵蓋所有框架的 routing skill，也不為這個需求改寫成 Node 生態。

## 截至 2026-10-30 的查核

ChatGPT 建議的大方向合理，但要把「可讀舊設定」與「完整相容舊工作流」分開。

- Zensical 最新 GitHub release 為 **0.0.73（2026-10-26）**。不能僅憑 `0.x` 判定不能使用，也不能把將來版本的承諾當成現有能力。
- **0.0.67（2026-09-30）已加入原生 `llmstxt` 與 Copy as Markdown**。這是比 repo 內 4 月評估明顯進步的地方。
- Zensical **不執行任意 MkDocs plugin，也不提供舊 MkDocs plugin API**；未列為支援的 plugin 設定可能被靜默忽略。`hooks` 不支援；`gen-files` 仍需外部生成等替代流程。
- 官方的介面翻譯與 `extra.alternate` 語言選單，**不能視為 `mkdocs-static-i18n` 的 suffix 內容、fallback、翻譯導覽及搜尋等價實作**。完整 i18n 工作流仍在 roadmap，這是此 repo 的主要遷移阻礙。
- Material 公告安全與重大修補維護到 **2027-05-05**。「先保留」不是承諾往後幾年都不必管；鎖版能防破壞性升級，不能代替安全維護。
- ChatGPT 提到的「2026-11-05 發布 Zensical 0.1.0」本次未取得足夠官方佐證；目前 roadmap 的 11 月 5 日 banner 指向 Studio 產品發布，**不把該日期當作 SSG 遷移依據**。

### 對照我們實際需要的功能

| 現有能力 | Zensical 判斷與驗收重點 |
|---|---|
| Material 風格、搜尋、常用 Markdown extensions | 有相容路徑；仍需驗證實際頁面、搜尋及 snippets／Mermaid 等代表性內容 |
| `llms.txt`、`llms-full.txt`、Markdown sidecars | 官方已支援原生 `llmstxt`；需驗證 sections、輸出完整性及 project Pages 子路徑 |
| `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` | 可考慮以 `content.action.copy` 取代「複製 Markdown」；不宣稱等價取代全部 Open-in-LLM 按鈕與自訂資產 |

| Python API docs | `mkdocstrings` 有官方相容實作；如需 `gen-files` 等搭配，仍須另行驗證，不列入新 skill 首版基本契約 |

# GitHub Pages 文件框架與 skill：評估結論及落地順序

## Context

使用者有多個既有專案依賴 `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` 與 MkDocs plugins，想評估新專案是否改用 Zensical，以及是否應另建 skill。後續補充：理想是**英文完整提供給所有讀者與 agent，部分文章可用繁中自行閱讀**，而非永久只做單語站。

這次只做評估：已讀取現有實作並查核官方資料，**未修改技能、遷移站點、安裝套件、執行建置或操作遠端 Issue／部署**。

## 建議結論

**保留 `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` 作為「英文主站＋可選繁中」的現行方案；Zensical 先作有限試點，不直接取代舊 skill，也不因為是新專案就一律採用。** 未來若封裝 `zensical-site-bootstrap`，使用獨立 skill，不改變既有 skill 的語意與維護入口。

| 專案情況 | 建議 |
|---|---|
| 既有 MkDocs + Material，依賴 i18n／自訂 plugins／hooks | 維持 MkDocs 1.x，保留上限與 lockfile，按專案盤點後才遷移 |
| 新專案要英文為主，現在或近期會提供部分繁中 | 仍優先現有 MkDocs 方案，支援按需翻譯與 fallback |
| 新的單語 Python／CLI／一般工具文件，確定暫不需要內容多語 | 可作 Zensical 試點；不能將這個例外擴大成所有新專案的預設 |
| 本 repo 的文件站 | 暫不遷移：目前有完整雙語與兩階段 LLM 建置流程 |

### 目標語言契約：英文優先，不強迫全站雙語

- 英文是完整 canonical 內容與預設入口；介面預設英文。
- 有需要的頁面才提供 `foo.zh-TW.md`，不要求所有頁面都翻譯。
- 語言切換優先到同一文章的對應版本；缺少繁中時保留英文內容，不顯示空白 placeholder。
- `llms.txt`／`llms-full.txt`／預設 Markdown sidecars 維持英文，繁中頁保留正確的人類閱讀與複製來源。
- 開啟語言選項不等於同意自動翻譯；翻譯仍需明確要求。

**介面翻譯 ≠ 語言選單 ≠ 內容多語。** Zensical 可指定 UI 語言並設定 alternate links，但不會因此自動建立翻譯頁、同頁映射、fallback 或語系搜尋。

本 repo 的 `mkdocs.yml:35–48` 已配置英文預設、繁中及 `fallback_to_default: true`。然而 `add-language.sh` 目前會建立全站翻譯 stubs，`add-docs-page.sh` 也會依語言設定建立 stubs；**存在的 placeholder 不能當成缺譯來回退**。要完全符合按需翻譯，應增補 opt-in 模式，而不是聲稱現有 skill 已毫無落差。

此按需翻譯建議針對下游專案，不撤銷本 repo 對已發布 catalog 頁要求英／繁中成對的規則。

GitHub Pages 仍適合這些站點。它提供靜態資源，建置時的 Python／Rust／Node 工具由 Actions 執行；**換文件引擎與換 hosting 是兩個獨立決策**。暫不增加第三個涵蓋所有框架的 routing skill，也不為這個需求改寫成 Node 生態。

## 截至 2026-10-30 的查核

ChatGPT 建議的大方向合理，但要把「可讀舊設定」與「完整相容舊工作流」分開。

- Zensical 最新 GitHub release 為 **0.0.73（2026-10-26）**。不能僅憑 `0.x` 判定不能使用，也不能把將來版本的承諾當成現有能力。

- Material 公告安全與重大修補維護到 **2027-05-05**。「先保留」不是承諾往後幾年都不必管；鎖版能防破壞性升級，不能代替安全維護。

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/skill-author

# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

# forge-native-dev

An opinionated, issue-driven development workflow that treats GitHub/GitLab as
the single source of truth for intent, backlog, and collaboration — not just
code hosting.

**Core thesis**: Issues are the unit of work. PRs are review gates. With AI
agents, creating a PR is near-zero cost — the human's job shifts from
*proposing* changes (PR-first) to *describing intent* (issue-first) and
*reviewing* results (PR-as-gate).

Lifecycle: **Issue -> branch -> worktree -> work -> PR -> review -> merge -> cleanup**.

Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:

| Surface | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `references/issue-driven-workflow.md` | "Why issues over local TODO.md?" |
| `references/forge-abstraction.md` | "What `gh` command maps to what `glab` command?" |
| `references/agent-patterns.md` | "How do I wire agents to work from issues?" |
| `references/coexistence.md` | "I have git-workflow / PKH installed too — which wins?" |
| `references/github-features.md` | "How do I use Discussions, Projects, Wiki?" |
| `references/gitlab-features.md` | "How do I use Boards, Threads, CI/CD?" |
| `references/conventions.md` | "What commit/branch/merge conventions should I follow?" |
| `scripts/forge.sh` | The sourced library — all other scripts depend on it. |
| `scripts/forge-init.sh` | One-shot repo setup. |
| `scripts/forge-worktree.sh` | Issue-to-worktree-to-PR lifecycle. |
| `scripts/forge-cleanup.sh` | Auto-cleanup merged branches + worktrees. |
| `scripts/forge-status.sh` | Alignment dashboard. |
| `scripts/forge-issue.sh` | Standalone issue operations. |
| `scripts/forge-pr.sh` | Standalone PR/MR operations. |

## When to use this skill

- The user says "open an issue", "create a backlog item", "開 issue",
  "maybe later", "先記下來", or describes a bug/idea worth tracking.
- The user asks "should I open a PR?", "幫我開 PR", or finishes work on
  a branch and needs to ship it.
- The user says "clean up branches", "清理 branch", "which branches are
  done?", or has stale worktrees.
- The user wants to see the state of their issues/branches/PRs at a glance.
- A new project needs to be set up for issue-driven development.
- The user asks about configuring agents to work from GitHub/GitLab issues.

## When NOT to use this skill

- The project has no GitHub/GitLab remote — use `git-workflow` instead.
- The user explicitly prefers `project-knowledge-harness` (local TODO.md).
- Purely offline git operations with no forge interaction.
- Secret scanning or agent transcript hygiene — use `agent-history-hygiene`.

## Coexistence with other skills

### If `git-workflow` is also installed

Both skills cover branching, PRs, and worktrees. On first ambiguous
operation (e.g., "should I branch?", "open a PR"), ask the user:

> I see both `git-workflow` (git-native) and `forge-native-dev`
> (GitHub/GitLab-native) are available. Which workflow do you prefer for
> this project? Default: `forge-native-dev` for any operation involving
> the remote forge.

Once decided, remember the preference for the session. `forge-native-dev`
is the upgrade path — it covers everything `git-workflow` does plus the
forge layer.

### If `project-knowledge-harness` is also installed

PKH uses `TODO.md` + `backlog/` + `pitfalls/` as file-based project memory.
`forge-native-dev` uses Issues + Discussions + in-repo `pitfalls/`.

If `TODO.md` exists with PKH markers (`## P1` / `## P2` etc.), warn:

> This project uses `project-knowledge-harness` (local TODO.md) for backlog.
> `forge-native-dev` uses Issues instead. Using both creates duplicate
> sources of truth. Which do you prefer for this project?

**One workflow per project, not both.** The migration path is documented in
[`references/coexistence.md`](references/coexistence.md).

## Core workflow

### 1. Setup (once per project)

```bash
bash scripts/forge-init.sh --target /path/to/project --project-name "My Project"
```

This detects the forge, creates labels, configures git, and adds agent
guidance to `AGENTS.md`. Read [`references/forge-abstraction.md`](references/forge-abstraction.md)
for the full gh/glab mapping.

### 2. Capture intent as Issues

When the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea, a bug, or a feature request:

**Default to creating an Issue.** Do not ask "should I create an issue?" —
just create it with appropriate labels.

```bash
# Quick backlog item
bash scripts/forge-issue.sh backlog \
  --title "Add pagination to search" \
  --body "Results page loads all items; should paginate at 50." \
  --priority P3 --effort M

# Bug report
bash scripts/forge-issue.sh create \
  --title "Login redirect fails on Safari" \
  --body "Steps to reproduce: ..." \
  --label "type/bug" --label "priority/P2"

# Feature request
bash scripts/forge-issue.sh create \
  --title "Add dark mode toggle" \
  --body "User preference, persist in localStorage." \
  --label "type/feature" --label "backlog"
```

### 3. Work on an issue

```bash
# Start: creates branch + worktree, assigns issue, adds "in-progress" label
bash scripts/forge-worktree.sh start 42

# Agent variant (uses agent/ branch prefix)
bash scripts/forge-worktree.sh --agent start 42

# Work in the worktree
cd .worktrees/issue-42/
# ... make changes, commit conventionally ...

# Finish: pushes branch, creates PR linking to issue
bash scripts/forge-worktree.sh finish 42
```

### 4. Review and merge

The PR is a review artifact. The issue already described the intent.
PR description auto-fills with `Closes #42`.

Review happens on the PR — by humans, review agents, or both.

```bash
# Check PR status
bash scripts/forge-pr.sh status

# Merge (default: squash, delete branch)
bash scripts/forge-pr.sh merge 55
```

### 5. Clean up

After PRs merge, clean up stale branches and worktrees:

```bash
# See what's ready to clean
bash scripts/forge-cleanup.sh --dry-run

# Clean with confirmation
bash scripts/forge-cleanup.sh

# Force (no confirmation, for scripted use)
bash scripts/forge-cleanup.sh --force
```

### 6. Dashboard

See the full state at a glance:

```bash
bash scripts/forge-status.sh          # your assigned issues
bash scripts/forge-status.sh --all    # all open issues
```

## Merge strategy

**Default: squash and merge.** One issue = one PR = one commit on `main`.

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Squash and merge** | Default. Agent/vibe-coding PRs with WIP commits. Gives the cleanest `git log`. |
| **Rebase and merge** | Every commit in the PR is a meaningful, curated logical change worth preserving. |
| **Create a merge commit** | Almost never in this workflow. Only if you need branch topology in history. |

Why squash is the default:
- Agent work produces noisy WIP commits — squash collapses them into one clean commit.
- One commit per issue on `main` makes `git log --oneline` a readable changelog.
- The squash commit message carries `Closes #N`, auto-closing the issue.
- `git bisect` and `git revert` operate on meaningful units (one feature/fix).

`forge-pr.sh merge` defaults to `--squash`. Override with `--rebase` when
commits are curated, or `--merge` when you need the topology (rare).

## Role awareness

The skill detects your access level to decide what operations are available:

| Role | Detection | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Maintainer** | Has push/write access (owner, org dev with write, collaborator) | Creates labels, assigns issues, sets priority, merges PRs |
| **Contributor** | Read-only or fork-based | Opens issues/PRs, describes priority in body text, leaves labeling to maintainers |

Detection is automatic via `forge_detect_role` (queries repo permissions API).
Override with `--role maintainer` or `--role contributor` in `forge-init.sh`,
or set `FORGE_ROLE_OVERRIDE=maintainer` / `FORGE_ROLE_OVERRIDE=contributor`
in your shell.

### Maintainer behavior

- `forge-init.sh` creates labels, scaffolds issue templates
- `forge-issue.sh backlog` applies `priority/*` and `backlog` labels directly
- `forge-worktree.sh start` assigns the issue and adds `in-progress` label
- Full access to merge, close, and triage

### Contributor behavior

- `forge-init.sh` skips label creation (labels are managed by maintainers)
- `forge-issue.sh backlog` notes priority in the issue body as a suggestion,
  does not apply labels (maintainer will triage)
- Issue templates are still scaffolded (they're just files in the repo)
- PRs can be opened; merging is up to maintainers

**Note**: "maintainer" here means anyone with write access — this includes
org members, collaborators, and core contributors, not just the repo owner.
If you can push to the repo, you're a maintainer in this skill's model.

## Issue vs Discussion: content boundary

| | Issue | Discussion |
|---|---|---|
| **Nature** | Actionable, with clear done criteria | Open-ended: evaluations, trade-offs, "should we?" |
| **Lifecycle** | Open → In Progress → PR → Closed | Open → threaded conversation → may spawn Issue |
| **Signals** | "Fix X", "Add Y", "Build Z" | "Should we use X?", "Compare A vs B", "Evaluate" |
| **Body** | Concise — what to do, acceptance criteria | Detailed — analysis, pros/cons, research |
| **Closing** | Closed when the PR merges | Stays open for ongoing discussion, or answered |

**Promotion pattern**: when a Discussion matures into actionable work,
create an Issue and link back to the Discussion. The Issue body says
"Design decided in Discussion #N — proceeding with approach B."

**Keep issue bodies concise.** Detailed analysis, trade-off tables, and
research belong in Discussion threads or `backlog/` docs, linked from the
issue. An issue cluttered with research is hard to scan for "what do I
need to build?"

**Cross-referencing**: Issues, Discussions, and PRs can all reference each
other via `#N`. Use this freely — the three-way linking is the key value
of using the forge natively.

## Where things go

| Kind of information | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Actionable work (bugs, features, chores) | Issues (with priority labels) | Searchable, assignable, linkable |
| Design discussion, research, trade-offs | GitHub Discussions / GitLab issue threads | Collaborative, threaded |
| Past traps, debugging knowledge | `pitfalls/` in-repo | Grep-able by symptom, portable |
| Code review | PR/MR comments | Tied to the diff |
| Backlog visualization | GitHub Projects / GitLab Boards | Built-in to the forge |
| Release notes | Tags + auto-generated release notes | Derived from PRs |

**Pitfalls stay in-repo** even in forge-native mode. They need to be
grep-able by error message from any clone. Research and discussion go to
the forge because they benefit from collaboration features.

## Issue-as-backlog conventions

Use labels to mirror priority and type:

- `priority/P1`, `priority/P2`, `priority/P3` — priority lanes
- `type/bug`, `type/feature`, `type/chore` — work type
- `backlog` — deferred work (equivalent to PKH's `## P?`)
- `agent-task` — explicitly flagged for agent implementation
- `in-progress` — currently being worked on
- `discussion` — not actionable work, just a topic

## Agent guidance for issue-driven work

### Checking for work

When the user asks "what should I work on?" or "有什麼可以做的?":

```bash
bash scripts/forge-issue.sh list --assignee @me
```

### Progress reporting

When working on a long task, post progress comments on the issue:

```bash
bash scripts/forge-issue.sh comment 42 \
  --body "Progress: implemented the API endpoint, working on tests next."
```

### Multi-session / multi-agent work

Each agent session should work in its own worktree. Use `--agent` prefix
to distinguish agent branches from human branches:

```bash
# Agent 1 works on issue 42
bash scripts/forge-worktree.sh --agent start 42

# Agent 2 works on issue 38
bash scripts/forge-worktree.sh --agent start 38
```

### Agent configuration patterns

See [`references/agent-patterns.md`](references/agent-patterns.md) for
concrete recipes:

- GitHub: Copilot coding agent in issues, GitHub Actions triggers
- Cursor: background agents, worktree-per-issue sessions
- Claude Code: `--worktree` flag, issue-driven sessions

## Branch naming

| Who | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Human | `issue/<number>-<slug>` | `issue/42-add-oauth` |
| Agent | `agent/issue/<number>-<slug>` | `agent/issue/42-add-oauth` |

Both patterns are recognized by `forge-cleanup.sh` and `forge-status.sh`.

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/forge.sh`** — sourced library, not run directly. All other
  scripts depend on it. Exports `forge_detect`, `forge_issue_*`,
  `forge_pr_*`, `forge_label_ensure`, `forge_slugify`, `forge_whoami`,
  `forge_default_branch`.
- **`scripts/forge-init.sh [--target DIR] [--project-name NAME] [--role auto|maintainer|contributor] [--skip-labels] [--skip-templates] [--skip-git-config] [--force] [--help]`**
  — one-shot setup: labels (maintainer only), issue templates, git config,
  AGENTS.md snippet. Role auto-detected from API permissions.
- **`scripts/forge-worktree.sh <start|finish|list> [ISSUE_NUM] [--agent] [--base BRANCH] [--draft] [--help]`**
  — the core lifecycle script.
- **`scripts/forge-cleanup.sh [--dry-run] [--force] [--all] [--help]`**
  — auto-cleanup merged branches + worktrees.
- **`scripts/forge-status.sh [--json] [--assigned] [--all] [--help]`**
  — alignment dashboard.
- **`scripts/forge-issue.sh <create|list|view|close|comment|assign|label|backlog> [--help]`**
  — standalone issue operations.
- **`scripts/forge-pr.sh <create|list|view|status|merge|link> [--help]`**
  — standalone PR/MR operations.

## Gotchas

- **`gh` / `glab` must be installed and authenticated.** The skill degrades
  to error messages without them — it does not fall back to raw git for
  forge operations. Run `gh auth status` or `glab auth status` to verify.
- **Squash-merge orphans the source branch.** After a squashed PR, the
  branch's commits never appear on the base, so `git branch --merged`
  won't list it. `forge-cleanup.sh` handles this by checking PR status
  directly instead of relying on git merge state.
- **Worktree path is relative to repo root.** `FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT`
  defaults to `.worktrees`. It should be gitignored (the init script does
  this). Gitignored files (`.env`, etc.) are NOT auto-copied into
  worktrees — use a `.worktreeinclude` file (see `git-workflow`'s
  `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md`).
- **One branch per issue.** If multiple branches match `issue/42-*`, the
  scripts error. Resolve manually or use `--agent` for agent branches.
- **GitHub Discussions API requires GraphQL.** The `forge_discussion_create`
  function falls back to creating a labeled issue. Use the web UI for full
  Discussion features until the CLI catches up.
- **Label creation is idempotent but case-sensitive.** `priority/P1` and
  `Priority/P1` are treated as different labels. Stick with lowercase.
- **Issue templates are scaffolded, not enforced.** The init script copies
  templates into `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` or `.gitlab/issue_templates/`.
  Users can modify or remove them.
- **The `@me` assignee shortcut** works in `gh` but may need the actual
  username in older `glab` versions.
- **After a PR merges, always create a new branch from updated main.**
  Do not reuse the merged branch (squash-merge makes its history diverge
  from main). Do not try to reopen a merged PR (GitHub does not allow it).
  Each PR is one logical change; follow-ups are new branches and new PRs.
  See [`references/conventions.md`](references/conventions.md) for details.
- **GitHub Discussion categories cannot be created via API.** The GraphQL
  API has no `createDiscussionCategory` mutation. Default categories
  (General, Ideas, Q&A, Announcements, Polls, Show and tell) are created
  automatically when Discussions is enabled. Custom categories (e.g.
  "Design", "Research") must be created via the web UI:
  Settings → Discussions → New category.
- **`gh project link --owner @me` fails for personal repos.** Use the
  actual username (e.g. `--owner myuser`) extracted from the remote URL.
  The `forge_project_create` function handles this automatically.
