1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
221	
222	```markdown
223	# [Analysis Title]
224	
225	## Executive summary
226	[One paragraph]
227	
228	## Key findings
229	- Finding 1 with supporting data
230	- Finding 2 with supporting data
231	
232	## Recommendations
233	1. Specific actionable recommendation
234	2. Specific actionable recommendation
235	```
236	````
237	
238	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
239	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
244	
245	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
246	
247	```markdown
248	## Form processing workflow
249	
250	Progress:
251	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
252	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
253	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
254	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
255	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
256	```
257	
258	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
259	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Validation loops
264	
265	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
266	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
267	
268	```markdown
269	## Editing workflow
270	
271	1. Make your edits.
272	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
273	3. If validation fails:
274	   - Read the error message.
275	   - Fix the issues.
276	   - Run validation again.
277	4. Only proceed when validation [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es.
278	```
279	
280	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
281	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Plan-validate-execute
286	
287	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
288	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
289	
290	```markdown
291	## PDF form filling
292	
293	1. Extract form fields:
294	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
295	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
296	3. Validate:
297	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
298	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
299	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
300	5. Fill the form:
301	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
302	```
303	
304	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
305	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
306	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
307	
308	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
309	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## Bundling reusable scripts
314	
315	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
316	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
317	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
318	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
319	
320	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
321	
322	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
323	agent can call them reliably.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Quick checklist before commit
328	
329	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
330	
331	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
332	      not just a one-line summary
333	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
334	      <=1024 chars required
335	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
336	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
337	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
338	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
339	      listed at the bottom
340	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
341	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
342	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
343	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
344	      `--dry-run` support
345	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
346	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
347
`````

````text
1	# Script design for agent skills
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/using-scripts>. Read this
4	before adding anything to `scripts/` in a skill.
5	
6	The headline difference from "regular" CLI design: **the caller is an LLM that
7	reads your stderr to decide what to do next.** Optimize for that.
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [One-off commands vs bundled scripts](#one-off-commands-vs-bundled-scripts)
12	2. [Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`](#pin-versions)
13	3. [Self-contained scripts (PEP 723 etc.)](#self-contained-scripts)
14	4. [Agentic CLI design rules](#agentic-cli-design-rules)
15	5. [Error message style](#error-message-style)
16	6. [Structured output](#structured-output)
17	7. [Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes](#idempotency-dry-run-exit-codes)
18	8. [Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)](#bash-32-compatibility-macos)
19	9. [Quick script checklist](#quick-script-checklist)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## One-off commands vs bundled scripts
24	
25	If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, **don't
26	bundle a script** — reference the tool directly:
27	
28	```bash
29	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
30	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
31	```
32	
33	Bundle a script when:
34	
35	- The invocation grows past ~3 flags or needs computed arguments.
36	- You need to compose multiple tools.
37	- The logic must be tested independently.
38	- You want to give the agent a stable interface even if the underlying tool
39	  changes.
40	
41	State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md` ("Requires Node 18+", "Requires
42	`uv`"). Don't assume the agent's environment.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Pin versions
47	
48	Unpinned `uvx`, `npx`, `pipx` invocations behave inconsistently as upstreams
49	release new versions. Always pin:
50	
51	```bash
52	# Good
53	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
54	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
55	pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .
56	
57	# Bad — silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change
58	uvx ruff check .
59	npx eslint --fix .
60	```
61	
62	`@latest` is fine **if** the skill explicitly says "tracks upstream latest" and
63	the user understands that.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Self-contained scripts
68	
69	When a script needs dependencies, prefer **inline declarations** over a
70	sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with
71	one command and no setup.
72	
73	### Python — PEP 723
74	
75	```python
76	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
77	# /// script
78	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
79	# dependencies = [
80	#   "beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5",
81	# ]
82	# ///
83	"""Extract <p class="info"> from an HTML file."""
84	import sys
85	from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
86	
87	with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
88	    html = f.read()
89	print(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").select_one("p.info").get_text())
90	```
91	
92	Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html`. `uv` creates an isolated
93	environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically.
94	
95	For full reproducibility, `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py` produces
96	`scripts/extract.py.lock`.
97	
98	### Deno
99	
100	```typescript
101	#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run
102	import * as cheerio from "npm:cheerio@1.0.0";
103	// ...
104	```
105	
106	### Bun
107	
108	```typescript
109	#!/usr/bin/env bun
110	import * as cheerio from "cheerio@1.0.0";
111	// ...
112	```
113	
114	If a `node_modules/` exists anywhere up the tree, Bun's auto-install is
115	disabled. Mention this in the skill if relevant.
116	
117	### Ruby
118	
119	```ruby
120	require 'bundler/inline'
121	gemfile do
122	  source 'https://rubygems.org'
123	  gem 'nokogiri', '~> 1.16'
124	end
125	# ...
126	```
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Agentic CLI design rules
131	
132	### No interactive prompts, ever
133	
134	Agents run in non-interactive shells. A script that calls `read`, `input()`,
135	or any TTY prompt **hangs indefinitely**. There is no recovery.
136	
137	```
138	# Bad
139	$ python scripts/deploy.py
140	Target environment: _
141	
142	# Good
143	$ python scripts/deploy.py
144	Error: --env is required. Options: development, staging, production.
145	Usage: python scripts/deploy.py --env staging --tag v1.2.3
146	```
147	
148	Accept all input via flags, env vars, or stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).
149	
150	### `--help` is the primary documentation
151	
152	The agent reads `--help` to learn the script. Make it concise but complete:
153	
154	```
155	Usage: scripts/process.py [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE
156	
157	Process input data and produce a summary report.
158	
159	Options:
160	  --format FORMAT    Output format: json, csv, table (default: json)
161	  --output FILE      Write output to FILE instead of stdout
162	  --verbose          Print progress to stderr
163	  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it
164	
165	Examples:
166	  scripts/process.py data.csv
167	  scripts/process.py --format csv --output report.csv data.csv
168	
169	Exit codes:
170	  0  success
171	  1  invalid arguments
172	  2  input file not found
173	  3  processing failed
174	```
175	
176	The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Error message style
181	
182	When an agent gets an error, the message **directly shapes its next attempt**.
183	Opaque errors waste turns.
184	
185	```
186	# Bad
187	Error: invalid input
188	
189	# Good
190	Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table.
191	       Received: "xml"
192	```
193	
194	Pattern: **what was wrong + what was expected + what to try.**
195	
196	For "field not found" style errors, include the available alternatives in the
197	message — this lets the agent self-correct without re-querying the system:
198	
199	```
200	Error: Field 'signature_date' not found.
````

1	# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
2	
3	The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
4	`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
5	the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
6	**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
11	  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
12	  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
13	- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
14	  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
15	  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
16	- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
17	  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
18	  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
19	  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
20	- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
21	  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.
22	
23	## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
24	
25	Per the Material team's analysis
26	([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):
27	
28	| Change | Impact on this stack |
29	|---|---|
30	| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
31	| Theme system rewritten — nav [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
32	| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
33	| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
34	| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |
35	
36	The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
37	describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
38	publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
39	There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
40	maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
41	user-driven (solve a specific pain).
42	
43	## Material team's response — Zensical
44	
45	[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
46	MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
47	MkDocs 1.x**.
48	
49	What's known:
50	
51	- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
52	- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
53	- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
54	  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
55	- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
56	  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
57	- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.
58	
59	The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
60	due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
61	strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.
62	
63	## Why we cap explicitly
64	
65	Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
66	which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
67	accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:
68	
69	- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
70	- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
71	  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
72	- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
73	  else's defensive pin to stay correct.
74	
75	The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
76	bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
77	patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.
78	
79	## When to re-evaluate
80	
81	Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
82	following are true**:
83	
84	1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
85	   equivalent project signal of API stability).
86	2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
87	   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
88	   per-language search).
89	3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
90	   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
91	   per-page raw-markdown links).
92	4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
93	   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).
94	
95	Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
96	MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
97	them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.
98	
99	## What to avoid
100	
101	- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
102	  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
103	- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
104	  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
105	  individual users.
106	- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
107	  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
108	  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
109	- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
110	  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
111	  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.
112	
113	## Re-checking the situation
114	
115	A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:
116	
117	1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
118	   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
119	   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
120	2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
121	   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
122	3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
123	   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
124	   release date been set?
125	4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
126	   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
127	   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
128	   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.
129	
130	## Source links
131	
132	- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
133	  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
134	- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
135	- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
136	- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>
137	- MkDocs 2.0 community discussion (#4077):
138	  <https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077>
139

1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	If you are building documentation for a project that consumes one of the
4	skills in this repo (especially [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
5	or [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)),
6	this is the docs stack we recommend.
7	
8	It's the same stack this repo uses for its own docs, plus the optional
9	`mkdocstrings` layer for projects that have a Python API to document.
10	
11	## TL;DR
12	
13	```toml
14	# pyproject.toml
15	[project.optional-dependencies]
16	docs = [
17	  "mkdocs>=1.6",
18	  "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
19	  # "mkdocs-material[imaging]>=9.5",  # only with --social (cairosvg+pillow)
20	  "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.24",   # only if you have a Python API
21	  "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
22	  "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
23	  "pymdown-extensions>=10.0",
24	]
25	```
26	
27	```bash
28	# Local preview
29	uv sync --extra docs
30	uv run mkdocs serve
31	
32	# Build static site
33	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
34	
35	# Safe HTML-only preview (llmstxt stays disabled)
36	uv run mkdocs build --strict
37	```
38	
39	## Why this stack
40	
41	- **MkDocs + Material** — Markdown-first authoring, built-in search, a
42	  theme that doesn't need overrides for ~90% of projects, GitHub Pages
43	  deploy is one workflow file.
44	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — render API docs from Python docstrings via
45	  `::: package.module.symbol` directives in your Markdown. Only relevant
46	  if your project has a Python API; skip it otherwise.
47	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt`** — generates `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` so
48	  AI agents can discover and consume your docs without scraping HTML.
49	  Upstream is in maintenance mode and must be isolated from a multilingual
50	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` build; the managed helper does that. If it stops working
51	  even in the default-language [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], replace it with a post-build generator.
52	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`** — adds "Copy to LLM / Open in ChatGPT / Open
53	  in Claude" buttons on every page. Pure UX sugar; harmless if your
54	  audience doesn't use it.
55	- **Managed strict build helper** — keeps `mkdocs-static-i18n` and
56	  `mkdocs-llmstxt` out of the same plugin lifecycle. Multilingual HTML is built
57	  separately from default-language LLM artifacts, validated, and merged before
58	  `site/` is replaced.
59	
60	## Why not these?
61	
62	- **Sphinx + Furo + MyST + autodoc.** Strictly more powerful, but the
63	  setup and maintenance cost is meaningful. Recommended only if AI-facing
64	  Markdown output becomes a first-class requirement, or if your project
65	  has the kind of cross-project reference graph Sphinx is built for.
66	- **pdoc.** Single-file API doc generator. Great for "I just want HTML
67	  for my package", but no good story for guides, conventions pages, or
68	  llms.txt.
69	- **Rspress.** Best-in-class for AI-native output, but it's
70	  Node-first / frontend-product-docs-first; Python API reference is a
71	  bolt-on. Not a fit unless you're already on the Node ecosystem.
72	- **Quarto.** Excellent for notebook / tutorial / research-report
73	  workflows; not optimized for Python library documentation.
74	
75	The longer version of this analysis (with the upstream-vs-inference
76	distinction made explicit) is preserved in the reference repo
77	[`mlflow-widgets/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets/blob/main/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md).
78	
79	## Minimum `mkdocs.yml`
80

````text
1	# Bilingual / multi-language docs
2	
3	How to add a non-English language (typically Traditional Chinese, `zh-TW`) to
4	a MkDocs Material site bootstrapped by this skill, and how to keep
5	terminology consistent so future contributors — human or agent — don't
6	introduce ambiguity.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	```bash
11	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
12	uv sync --extra docs
13	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
14	```
15	
16	The Material header gains a language switcher. The managed build helper keeps
17	both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es strict, publishes all locale HTML, and produces root `llms.txt`,
18	`llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars from the default language only. Translate
19	the stub bodies when ready.
20	
21	For local HTML preview, `uv run mkdocs serve` and direct `uv run mkdocs build
22	--strict` remain safe: the config disables `llmstxt` unless the helper enables
23	it. Use the helper for every artifact that will be deployed.
24	
25	## Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure
26	
27	[Squidfunk's recommended approach](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/discussions/2346)
28	for content translation is the
29	[`mkdocs-static-i18n`](https://github.com/ultrabug/mkdocs-static-i18n) plugin.
30	We use **`docs_structure: suffix`** rather than `folder` because:
31	
32	- **Zero file moves on retrofit.** Existing `docs/index.md`,
33	  `docs/getting-started.md`, etc. stay where they are. The `folder` mode
34	  would force you to move every file into `docs/en/` first.
35	- **Relative links keep working.** Sibling files share the same directory.
36	- **Per-page opt-in to translation.** A page is only translated when
37	  `<page>.<lang>.md` exists; otherwise the plugin falls back to the default
38	  language (`fallback_to_default: true`).
39	
40	The trade-off: directory listings get crowded once you have many languages.
41	For sites that grow to 5+ languages the `folder` structure starts to win on
42	readability — but you can migrate later.
43	
44	## Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement)
45	
46	This is the rule for any non-English page in a project that uses this skill:
47	
48	> **在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞首次出現時，以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現。**
49	> 例：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」、「型別檢查 (type checking)」。
50	> 後續同段內可只用中文。
51	>
52	> **不自創翻譯。** 若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
53	> `mkdocs-static-i18n`、`pymdownx.snippets`）。
54	>
55	> **代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。**
56	
57	The reason: Chinese-language tech writing has competing translations for
58	many terms (e.g. `cache` → 快取 / 緩存 / 暫存; `repository` → 倉庫 / 儲存庫 /
59	版本庫). Keeping the English original on first mention removes the ambiguity
60	without forcing readers to guess which translation the author meant. It also
61	keeps the page grep-able for English search terms.
62	
63	`add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh` inject this rule as an admonition
64	at the top of every non-default-language stub so authors see it before they
65	start translating.
66	
67	## What `add-language.sh` does, step by step
68	
69	For users who want to apply pieces by hand or audit what the script touched:
70	
71	1. **Locates `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD.
72	2. **Detects existing i18n state.** `yq` query against `.plugins[]` checks
73	   for an `i18n:` map.
74	3. **Inserts or extends `plugins.i18n`.**
75	   - If absent: prepends a fresh i18n block before `search`, with
76	     `[default-lang, new-lang]` as the language list.
77	   - If present and the new locale isn't there: appends to
78	     `plugins[].i18n.languages`.
79	   - If the locale is already present: no-op.
80	4. **Sets `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
81	   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` warns when `theme.language` is missing).
82	5. **Removes `navigation.instant` / `navigation.instant.progress`** from
83	   `theme.features` (the language switcher's contextual link can't be
84	   rewritten by instant navigation).
85	6. **Keeps default-language `mkdocs-llmstxt` output by default.** It adds the
86	   environment guards and managed `scripts/build-docs-site.py` required to
87	   isolate llmstxt from the multilingual build. Use `--remove-llmstxt` for an
88	   explicit opt-out. Legacy `--drop-strict` is a deprecated no-op;
89	   `--keep-llmstxt` is a deprecated alias for the default behavior.
90	7. **Walks `docs/`** for `*.md` files (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`),
91	   and for each non-locale-suffixed source page, creates a sibling
92	   `*.<LANG>.md` from `assets/translation-stub.md.template`.
93	8. **Updates `.skills/preferences.yaml`** with three keys:
94	   `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages` (ordered list, default first),
95	   `keep_english_terms: true`, `i18n_structure: suffix`.
96	9. **Un-comments `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2`** in `pyproject.toml`. If the
97	   line isn't there at all, prints a hint asking you to add it manually.
98	
99	The script is idempotent: re-running with the same `--lang` is a no-op. Exit
100	`11` means the locale/stubs were added and the safe migration subset was
101	applied, but custom downstream files still need the manual actions reported by
102	`migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh --json`.
103	
104	## `theme.language` vs plugin `languages`
105	
106	These are two different things:
107	
108	- [`theme.language`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/)
109	  is **Material's UI strings** (search placeholder, "Edit this page", footer
110	  navigation hints). One value site-wide. Material ships translations for
111	  ~70 locales out of the box.
112	- `plugins.i18n.languages` is **content translation**. A list. Each entry
113	  declares a locale that has translated `*.<lang>.md` files.
114	
115	You almost always want `theme.language` set to your default content language
116	so the UI matches when readers land on a default-language page.
117	
118	## `nav_translations`
119	
120	To translate section titles in the nav (e.g. `Workflows` → `工作流程`), use
121	`mkdocs-static-i18n`'s per-language `nav_translations`:
122	
123	```yaml
124	plugins:
125	  - i18n:
126	      docs_structure: suffix
127	      languages:
128	        - locale: en
129	          name: English
130	          default: true
131	        - locale: zh-TW
132	          name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
133	          nav_translations:
134	            Workflows: 工作流程
135	            Reference: 參考資料
136	```
137	
138	`add-language.sh` does **not** populate `nav_translations` for you —
139	section names are project-specific and translating them is a deliberate
140	authorial choice. Add them by hand once you have section titles to translate.
141	
142	!!! warning "Don't apply 「中文 (English original)」 to nav labels"
143	    The terminology rule that governs body prose **does not extend to
144	    `nav_translations` values.** Nav entries are navigation chrome — short
145	    labels in a sidebar — and bilingual labels like
146	    `Reference: 參考資料 (Reference)` are too long, wrap awkwardly, and
147	    duplicate information the URL slug already preserves.
148	
149	    For nav labels: pick the most common Chinese term for each section
150	    and stick with it. Stay consistent across the whole nav. The URL
151	    slug still uses the English source name (`/zh-TW/reference/...`),
152	    so search engines and direct-link sharing are unaffected.
153	
154	    Examples:
155	
156	    | English heading | Good zh-TW label | Bad zh-TW label |
157	    |---|---|---|
158	    | `Reference` | `參考資料` | `參考資料 (Reference)` |
159	    | `Workflows` | `工作流程` | `工作流程 (Workflows)` |
160	    | `Skills` | `Skills` (keep — domain term, no canonical translation) | `技能 (Skills)` |
161	    | `Getting started` | `快速開始` | `快速開始 (Getting started)` |
162	
163	    The "keep English" exception (third row) is reserved for terms where
164	    no canonical Chinese translation exists. When in doubt, keep English
165	    — it matches the body-prose rule's spirit (don't invent) without
````

345	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + environment-guarded llmstxt,
346	  copy-to-llm, i18n-ready `docs_dir`, and pymdownx.snippets; parameterized with
347	  `{{SITE_NAME}}`, `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`. Carries `__SOCIAL_*__`
348	  marker lines that `init-docs-site.sh` expands (with `--social`) or deletes.
349	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
350	  optional-deps group. Has a `__SOCIAL_IMAGING__` marker.
351	- `assets/build-docs-site.py` — Managed two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] helper copied to the downstream
352	  project's `scripts/build-docs-site.py`. Keep its managed marker intact so the
353	  migration tool can distinguish it from a user-owned script.
354	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
355	  paths filter, uv setup, the managed strict build helper, and Pages deploy.
356	  Has a `__SOCIAL_CI__` marker for the Cairo/Pango + card-cache steps.
357	- `assets/social/` — snippets injected at the `__SOCIAL_*__` markers when
358	  `init-docs-site.sh --social` is [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed: `mkdocs-plugin.yml` (the `social`
359	  plugin block), `pyproject-dep.txt` (`mkdocs-material[imaging]`), and
360	  `ci-steps.yml` (the Cairo/Pango install + `.cache/plugin/social` cache).
361	  Pre-indented for their insertion points — keep the indentation.
362	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
363	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
364	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
365	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
366	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
367	  terminology-rule admonition.
368	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
369	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
370	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
371	
372	## Gotchas
373	
374	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
375	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
376	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
377	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
378	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
379	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
380	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
381	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
382	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
383	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
384	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
385	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
386	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
387	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
388	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
389	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
390	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
391	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
392	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
393	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
394	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
395	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
396	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
397	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
398	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
399	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
400	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
401	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
402	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
403	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
404	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
405	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
406	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
407	  `select()` form.
408	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
409	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
410	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
411	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
412	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
413	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
414	- **`pymdownx.snippets` include fragments belong in recursive `exclude_docs`.**
415	  `not_in_nav` only suppresses warnings and still publishes standalone HTML;
416	  the template excludes root and nested `_snippets/` directories.
417	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
418	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
419	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
420	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
421	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
422	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
423	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
424	  Counter-intuitive name.
425	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
426	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
427	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
428	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
429	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
430	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
431	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
432	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
433	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
434	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
435	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
436	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
437	- **A single multilingual build silently corrupts `mkdocs-llmstxt` output.**
438	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` performs a full build per locale, while llmstxt clears
439	  its page state and overwrites the same root `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` on
440	  every [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. The final locale can therefore leave nearly empty or wrong-locale
441	  output. Removing `--strict` only hides warnings; it does not repair the files.
442	  Always use `scripts/build-docs-site.py` for the deployable artifact. Root
443	  `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars intentionally contain only
444	  the default language.
445	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
446	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
447	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
448	  is just acting on it.
449	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
450	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
451	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
452	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
453	
454	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
455	
456	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, don't silently "upgrade" it; customizations may
457	not match the template. For an explicit i18n/llmstxt repair request, use
458	`migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh` audit-first. Apply only after showing its planned
459	changes and preserve every shape it reports as a manual action.
460
```

# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`

Last verified: **2026-10-30** against upstream documentation and release notes.
This replaces the April 2026 assessment. Upstream support below is not a claim
that this skill's sites have been built or migrated with Zensical.

## TL;DR

- **Keep this skill and existing MkDocs sites.** Preserve `mkdocs>=1.6,<2`,
  `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`, the lockfile, and the managed build helper.
- **English-first with optional Traditional Chinese is content i18n**, not
  just a translated interface. Continue using MkDocs for that workflow until
  a successor [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es the same output checks.
- **Zensical is a viable candidate for a scoped single-language pilot**, not
  an automatic default for every new project. Its `0.x` version alone is
  neither a reason to reject it nor evidence of production readiness.
- **Material maintenance ends on 2027-05-05** for security and critical fixes,
  per its [changelog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/changelog/).
  Staying on MkDocs is a time-bounded decision, not a promise of years of support.
- A future `zensical-site-bootstrap` should be a **separate skill**. Updating
  this skill must not silently change downstream projects' build engine.

## What changes in MkDocs 2.0

The [MkDocs announcement](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077)
links to [version 2 pre-release documentation](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/).
The Material team's [analysis, updated in October 2026](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/),
reports removal of the MkDocs 1.x plugin system, a rewritten theme interface,
and TOML configuration. It states that Material is incompatible and that no
release date has been announced. Treat these as pre-release design statements,
not a guarantee that the final design cannot change.

`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, and `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` depend on the
MkDocs plugin lifecycle. **PyMdown's snippets, superfences, and tabs are Python
Markdown extensions, not MkDocs plugins**; assess Markdown compatibility
separately rather than claiming every extension has the same failure mode.

Do not upgrade this Material-based stack to MkDocs 2.0 without a separately
validated migration. There is no need to adopt a different hosting provider:
GitHub Actions can build the static output before GitHub Pages serves it.

## What Zensical supports now

The latest release at verification was
[0.0.73 (2026-10-26)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.73).
[0.0.67 (2026-09-30)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.67)
added native `llmstxt` and a Copy as Markdown button. The old assessment that
there was no published support for these functions is obsolete.

The [plugin compatibility table](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/plugins/)
is the authority for individual settings, not the presence of a plugin name in
`mkdocs.yml`:

| Requirement | Upstream status and limits |
|---|---|
| Existing `mkdocs.yml` / Material look | Supported migration path; `theme.variant: classic` preserves the familiar appearance. Custom template overrides may need changes. |
| Search / Python API reference | Native search and `mkdocstrings` integration are documented. Install the required handler; audit companion plugins separately. |
| `llms.txt`, full output, Markdown counterparts | Native `llmstxt` since 0.0.67. Validate sections, exported content, and project Pages subpaths. Custom Python `preprocess` is ignored. |
| Copy as Markdown | `content.action.copy` works for pages with Markdown counterparts. This is not proof of parity with every `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button or custom asset. |
| UI language / alternate-language links | Documented, but not proof of suffix content translation, fallback, contextual switching, translated nav, or per-language search. |
| Arbitrary MkDocs plugins / hooks | No MkDocs plugin API; arbitrary plugins cannot run. The migration guide lists `hooks` as unsupported. |
| `gen-files` | Not supported directly; external generation is a separate workflow to evaluate. |

**Unsupported plugin configuration can be silently ignored.** A successful
build is insufficient: inspect the artifacts and user-visible behavior.
Likewise, supported plugins may have ignored settings. Check every setting
used by the target site, not just the package list.

The [migration guide](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/migration/)
does not require conversion to `zensical.toml` just to test an existing config.
It also documents CLI and template differences; replacing `mkdocs` with
`zensical` in the managed helper is not a migration strategy.

Do not treat an unverified future release date as an adoption gate. In
particular, the roadmap's November 5 Studio banner is not evidence for a
November 5, 2026 release of the SSG as version 0.1.0.

## English-first with optional Traditional Chinese

Distinguish three layers:

1. **UI localization** translates search labels and navigation controls.
2. **A language selector** links to language-specific destinations; it does
   not generate translated documents.
3. **Content i18n** maps corresponding articles, handles missing translations,
   and builds appropriate navigation and search for each locale.

For this workflow, English is the complete default source for readers and
agents. Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for articles the user wants in Traditional Chinese;
missing translations should fall back to English. Root `llms.txt`,
`llms-full.txt`, and Markdown sidecars remain default-language-only. Enabling
a locale never authorizes automatic translation.

MkDocs' `fallback_to_default: true` supports missing siblings, but an existing
"Translation pending" stub counts as a translation and masks the fallback.
**`add-language.sh --no-stubs` already enables a locale without generating
siblings.** That flag is per-invocation, not a persistent preference:
`add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for configured non-default languages.
Read [the i18n guide](i18n-guide.md#english-first-with-selective-translations)
before choosing this workflow; do not invent a persistent on-demand flag.

Zensical's [language settings](https://zensical.org/docs/setup/language/)
document UI localization and alternate links. The [roadmap](https://zensical.org/roadmap/)
still lists broader content-i18n work. Neither establishes parity with this
skill's suffix/fallback workflow. Do not replace it with a hand-built multi-site
pipeline merely to claim that language switching exists.

## Keep the caps; validate migrations separately

Material 9.7.5+ also constrains MkDocs below 2. A resolver intersects that
constraint with the project's direct requirements; the direct MkDocs dependency
is **not** resolved independently. Explicit bounds still document this skill's
own support contract and remain protective if upstream metadata changes.

Keep bounds consistent in the dependency template, optional social extra,
manual recipe, and initializer's existing-`pyproject.toml` hints. Commit a
lockfile in consuming projects and use controlled patch/minor updates with
regression tests. Bounds permit those updates; they do not refresh a lockfile
or supply security fixes automatically.

**Migrating to Zensical does not mean lifting the MkDocs cap.** Change the
builder and dependencies deliberately for each approved migration; retain the
caps wherever the MkDocs/Material stack remains in use.

## Re-evaluation and adoption gates

Review again by **January 2027**, ahead of Material's maintenance deadline,
or sooner after relevant security advisories or new content-i18n support.
This is a review recommendation, not an automatically scheduled task.

Before a pilot becomes a default or an existing site is migrated:

1. Inventory plugins, hooks, extensions, templates, and build-time generators.
   Record unsupported or unknown settings instead of accepting silent omission.
2. Build an isolated, version-locked fixture. Compare navigation, search,
   code blocks/snippets, images, anchors, and project Pages subpath links.
3. Verify `llms.txt` sections, full content, Markdown counterparts, and the
   actual Copy as Markdown behavior, not just file existence or exit status.
4. For content-i18n sites, verify English defaults, selected zh-TW counterparts,
   missing-translation fallback, same-page switching, locale navigation/search,
   correct source links, and default-language-only LLM artifacts.
5. Preserve sources and the last successful output on failure. Document rollback
   and get consent before switching an existing project or deploying anything.

A single-language pilot can validate steps 1–3 without solving i18n, but that
result does **not** make it the default for English-first bilingual projects.
Keep this skill's two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build and repair tools until an equivalent migration
has [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed all applicable gates; do not copy that MkDocs-specific machinery into
a new Zensical skill.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent transcripts and plan files in the commit that records their feature,
without leaking secrets or mutating a file while its recorder is active.

Surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `run-specstory-session.sh` | "How do I prove the recorder exited before finalization?" |
| `queue-agent-commit.sh` | "How do I queue this exact authorized commit without touching live history?" |
| `finalize-agent-commit.sh` | "How is the exact post-session snapshot sanitized and committed?" |
| `find-session.sh` | "Which transcript / plan file is my current session?" |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` | "Which exact agent files belong in the prepared index?" |
| `agent-commit-metadata.sh` | "Which provenance trailers belong in the commit?" |
| `bootstrap-project.sh` | "How do I install validation-only hooks?" |
| `scan-staged.sh` | "Is the effective staged index clean?" |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py` | "What does SpecStory redact natively?" |

## Core invariants

1. **Commit the transcript and plan with the feature they produced.** Never
   ignore `.specstory/history/` or silently drop dirty agent artifacts from the
   review trail.
2. **SpecStory state is not review history.** Ignore only
   `.specstory/.project.json` and `.specstory/statistics.json`; both are
   machine-local/regenerable.
3. **Quiescence comes before Git history movement.** An active recorder blocks
   commit, `pull --rebase`, rebase/update-base, integration, and worktree/session
   retirement. Required order:

   ```text
   recorder quiescence
     -> exact artifact + message finalization
     -> ordinary hook-enabled commit proven
     -> history/ref movement or retirement
   ```

4. **Provenance comes from the staged snapshot.** Use exact session, transcript,
   and plan selectors; never point a trailer at an unstaged artifact or guess an
   unknown model.
5. **Rotate at the provider before any Git rewrite.** Redaction prevents new
   reachability; it does not revoke a credential or erase every local copy.
6. **Never use plain `git push --force` as leak remediation.** It can destroy
   teammate work and does not remove bytes from existing clones/caches.
7. **Shipped files must be scanner-safe.** `npx skills add` installs this whole
   directory under a consumer's scan scope. Never embed a literal private-key
   header; build it at test runtime or use synthetic placeholders. Enforced by
   `tests/test_shipped_file_hygiene.py`.

## When to use

Use this skill when:

- the user asks to commit/save a SpecStory session, transcript, or plan;
- dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or another configured artifact accompanies a feature;
- `.specstory/.project.json` or `statistics.json` keeps churning;
- the user asks to install pre-commit/gitleaks for agent artifacts;
- a scanner finds a secret in an agent artifact; or
- a credential was committed or pushed—read
  [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) before any rewrite.

Do not use it when the user explicitly wants agent history excluded, or when no
agent artifacts exist. If a leak is already on shared `main`/release, do not
suggest rewriting that branch; use the remediation runbook.

## Default lifecycle: queue now, finalize after exit

Read
[`references/post-session-finalization.md`](references/post-session-finalization.md)
before running or recovering this lifecycle. It defines every state, exit code,
recovery action, and no-retry boundary.

### 1. Launch the synchronous wrapper

From the intended worktree, before starting Claude:

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
  --allow-commit claude
```

`--allow-commit` gives the **outer parent** a one-run finalizer capability. It
does not let the child infer user consent. The agent still waits for explicit
commit authorization before queueing.

Do not replace the wrapper with a Stop hook, detached watcher/daemon, or live
checkpoint. A Stop hook runs before process/recorder quiescence is proven; a
daemon separates recorder lifetime from the session; a live checkpoint commits
while the file can still change.

### 2. Work normally; stage only feature paths

Take the canonical lowercase UUID from Claude `/status`. Resolve the exact
SpecStory path and plan policy; if one UUID has multiple rendered aliases, [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
both UUID and path to disambiguate.

```bash
SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-09-01_02-14-50Z.md'
PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-change.md'

git add -- path/to/feature-a path/to/feature-b
```

Do **not** stage the live transcript or plan. The finalizer owns exact artifact
staging and sanitation after SpecStory exits.

### 3. After explicit user commit authorization, queue once

Create a UTF-8 base subject/body without lifecycle-managed trailers, then queue
with exact selectors:

```bash
MESSAGE_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agent-commit-message.txt"
printf '%s\n' \
  'feat(scope): summarize the change' \
  '' \
  'Explain why the change is needed.' > "$MESSAGE_FILE"

bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/queue-agent-commit.sh \
  --commit \
  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" \
  --plan "$PLAN" \
  --message-file "$MESSAGE_FILE"
# Use --no-plan instead of --plan only when no plan exists.
```

The queue copies only the base message into private per-worktree state. It does
not read, stage, scan, redact, or commit the live transcript.

On `status=queued`, report **"finalization queued"** and exit the agent session.
Perform no further repository/index operation—not even `git status`, a diff, a
message edit, sync, or a finalizer call.

### 4. Let the outer runner finish

New runs use protocol v2 and default to **no cloud sync**; the explicit choice
reaches native run and sync flags without changing configuration. Existing v1
requests retain their strict original schema and recovery rules, never an
implicit upgrade. Only after child exit `0` and process-group quiescence, the runner:

1. records lifecycle proof;
2. runs one exact quiet UUID sync with the selected no-cloud policy;
3. verifies the selected alias's full digest against a bounded private native
   `sync --print --silent --no-cloud-sync --no-stats` export, binding the unchanged
   native JSONL generation before/after (unsupported exports or stale aliases stop);
4. calls the finalizer with its parent-held token;
5. stages and sanitizes exact artifacts in a locked alternate index;
6. derives canonical trailers, writes private handoff drafts, and calls one
   ordinary `git commit -F` with normal hooks enabled; and
7. proves the resulting parent, tree, branch, and
   `Agent-History-Request` trailer.

Normal pre-commit execution is unsafe while a writer is active: when unstaged
changes exist, pre-commit can stash them, check out/modify staged content, then
restore the stash. That checkout/restore sequence can race a recorder and
clobber, conflict with, or reintroduce bytes. Therefore the pre-commit checker is
validation-only; the quiescent finalizer is the sole sanctioned mutator.

## Finalization outcomes

- **Success (`committed` / exit 0):** an ordinary hook-enabled commit is proven.
  Only now may rebase/update-base, integration, or retirement proceed.
- **Sanitation (`rotation_required` / exit 10):** exact index and live artifacts
  are sanitized, private full beforeimages/occurrence evidence and drafts are
  retained, and no commit was attempted. A v2 read-only `--preview-review --json`
  shows masked findings; a private versioned `--review-file` accounts for every
  finding as `reviewed_noncredential`, `credential_rotation_required`, or
  `unresolved`. Complete reviewed fixtures release only this sanitized snapshot's
  rotation gate with fresh `--allow-commit`; real credentials still require
  rotation plus `--rotation-confirmed`, and unresolved/mixed incomplete review
  blocks. Nothing restores raw bytes, adds a policy allowlist, or skips hooks.
  Legacy v1 retains rotation-only recovery and cannot acquire v2 review evidence.
- **Partial publication (`publication_unproven` / exit 8):** private evidence is
  retained but index/source publication could not be fully proven. Inspect;
  never assume rollback or replay sanitation automatically.
- **Hook/commit failure (`commit_failed` / exit 11):** HEAD is unchanged and the
  exact prepared tree plus drafts remain. Fix the hook without changing that
  snapshot, then make one explicit recovery call with fresh `--allow-commit`.
  There is no automatic retry.
- **Uncertain outcome (exit 8):** reconcile only. Never issue another commit
  automatically; prove the exact HEAD or escalate for inspection.
- **Manual handoff:** LazyGit reads per-worktree
  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`; standard Git uses per-worktree `COMMIT_EDITMSG`.
  A draft makes recovery possible but is not proof that a commit happened.

An actual rebase is identified by Git's state directories (`rebase-merge` or
`rebase-apply`), not by a stale `REBASE_HEAD` file alone. Other active operation
markers and `index.lock` also block queue/finalization.

## Bootstrap a repository

Read
[`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
before bootstrap or migration.

> **Current hook release:** `ahh-v2.0.1` is the immutable published pin used by
> the checked-in template and hook migration target. Fresh bootstrap also pins
> gitleaks v8.30.1 and installs the scoped Sourcegraph/Git-OID false-positive
> fix. Updating only the ahh tag does not rewrite an existing root
> `.gitleaks.toml`; follow the rollout steps in the reference for existing repos.

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Bootstrap installs:

- a validation-only staged-index checker plus gitleaks;
- precise nested SpecStory state ignores, keeping `history/` visible;
- generic hygiene hooks whose mutators exclude every agent/archive/install root:
  `.agents`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.opencode`, `.specify`,
  `.specstory`; and
- optionally a validation-only `prepare-commit-msg` exact-selector gate.

Security checkers retain coverage of those roots. Excluding only `.specstory`
from whitespace/EOF/formatters is insufficient: `.agents/skills/` contains
installed vendored code, and `.claude/skills/` may symlink to it.

For old `ahh-v1.1.0` or exact local-redactor layouts, the post-release migration
is transactional and fail-closed:

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

It preserves compatible sibling hooks/options, validates a candidate before
publishing, and refuses ambiguous/customized legacy commands.

## Post-leak remediation

When a scan finds a real credential, or the user says it was committed/pushed:

1. stop any reflexive force-push;
2. read [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) end-to-end;
3. rotate at the provider regardless of blast radius; and
4. only then choose the least disruptive Git action from the runbook.

## Gotchas

- `.gitignore` does not untrack existing state. Use
  `bootstrap-project.sh --untrack-specstory-state`; never broaden the ignore to
  `.specstory/`.
- SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on write but has context/rule gaps. Keep native
  redaction enabled and retain the finalizer check. Read
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  before changing placeholders or coverage.
- SpecStory 2.10 is checkout-path scoped, not branch scoped. Create the worktree
  first, then start one wrapper/session per change stream. `EnterWorktree` does
  not rebind an existing recorder.
- Exact discovery rejects incomplete JSONL, aliases, symlinks, unsafe bytes, and
  cross-worktree identity. Read
  [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  when resolution is empty or ambiguous.
- `plansDirectory` may be ignored at project scope in some Claude Code versions.
  Verify where the plan landed; user-level `"plansDirectory":
  "./.claude/plans"` is the recommended default.
- `pre-commit install` is per clone. CI is a second chance, not the last gate.
- `--install-hook` requires `core.hooksPath` genuinely unset. Empty, relative,
  global, or custom values are refused; integrate the validation-only gate in
  the configured hook directory yourself.
- `gitleaks protect` is deprecated. Use `gitleaks git --staged` or
  `gitleaks dir`.
- Rotate oversized sessions instead of raising the 2 MiB transcript allowance.

## Available scripts

- **`run-specstory-session.sh [--allow-commit] claude [-- OPTIONS...]`** — owns
  the foreground process group, preserves child/signal status, performs one
  post-exit exact sync, and optionally invokes one finalizer.
- **`queue-agent-commit.sh --commit --session-id UUID --specstory-path PATH
  (--plan PATH|--no-plan) --message-file PATH`** — writes one strict,
  metadata-only, per-worktree request; identical repeats are idempotent.
- **`finalize-agent-commit.sh --request ABSOLUTE_PATH
  (--allow-commit|--runner-token TOKEN) [--rotation-confirmed] [--review-file PATH]`**
  — validates lifecycle/snapshot proof, prepares exact sanitized artifacts and
  drafts, executes one ordinary commit, and reconciles uncertain state without
  retry. V2 `--preview-review --json` needs no authorization and never writes;
  `--prepare-only`, `--expected-revision DIGEST`, and `--reconcile-only` support a
  thin native adapter without a second commit engine.
- **`_post_session.py capabilities --json` / `inspect --request PATH --json`** —
  bounded side-effect-free protocol discovery and receipt reproof; `inspect
  --context --json` additionally requires authentic live wrapper ancestry.
  Public output contains identities/digests, never raw transcript/message values.
  Whole frozen-index text coverage is required in v2; product findings block
  without mutation, and unsupported binary/oversized coverage fails explicitly.
- **`find-session.sh (--session-id UUID|--specstory-path PATH|--newest)
  [--format specstory|claude|both] [--json]`** — exact checkout/session proof;
  `--newest` is heuristic compatibility only.
- **`stage-agent-artifacts.sh ...`** — exact or broad atomic staging.
  `--sanitize-index` sanitizes selected blobs in the locked alternate index;
  `--materialize-sanitized` safely writes those exact sanitized bytes back after
  generation checks; `--check-staged` never mutates.
- **`agent-commit-metadata.sh [--harness NAME --model NAME]
  [--format trailers|json]`** — derives canonical provenance from staged blobs.
- **`scan-staged.sh [--redact|--no-redact] [--config PATH] [--verbose]`** —
  validates the effective index; emits only bounded secret-free JSON findings
  and suppresses raw scanner output.
- **`probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`** — measures
  native coverage; exit 30 when SpecStory is absent.
- **`bootstrap-project.sh [--migrate] [--install-hook]
  [--untrack-specstory-state] [--force] [--dry-run]`** — installs/migrates the
  validation stack; remember the unpublished-v2.0.0 blocker above.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — canonical artifact directory set.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — validation-only checker, gitleaks,
  and generic hygiene with full archive/install-root mutator exclusions.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — custom rules and scoped example allowlists.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — staged-index checker/sanitizer. `--check-index`
  accepts canonical or temporary commit indexes; `--fix-index` requires an
  explicit user-owned noncanonical `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and exact `--files`.

## Reference files

- [`references/post-session-finalization.md`](references/post-session-finalization.md)

  retirement.
- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — load when exact session/path resolution is empty, ambiguous, or mismatched.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)

- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — load before changing native-redaction assumptions, sentinels, or coverage.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) — load before any
  history rewrite or force-push after a leak.

## Tests

Run from the repository root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

The suite covers exact discovery/staging, alternate-index sanitation and
materialization, validation-only migration/hooks, scanner-safe output,
runner/finalizer authorization and recovery, stale `REBASE_HEAD`, private state,
and shipped-file safety. Read [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for the full
inventory and direct commands.
