1	# Post-session finalization
2	
3	Use this runbook for the default SpecStory/Claude lifecycle, any finalizer
4	recovery, and every rebase/integration/retirement decision that follows it.
5	
6	## Protocol versions
7	
8	New wrappers create **v2** requests/journals (POSIX, Python 3.11+). V1 has a separate strict parser;
9	existing requests are never upgraded by adding fields or reconstructing missing
10	beforeimages from today's files. `--protocol-version 1` explicitly creates a
11	legacy compatibility run; it is not a migration or a review by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. V1 recovery
12	continues to require rotation confirmation after sanitation.
13	
14	V2 records durable private sanitation evidence before publishing any sanitized
15	source/index: complete post-sync source beforeimages, original and sanitized
16	blob OIDs/modes, every finding and occurrence, replayable transformation steps,
17	native source/path identities, request/root/ref/parent/input/prepared tree,
18	scanner/tool/policy identities and complete coverage. Receipt-write failure stops
19	publication; a later partial publication is `publication_unproven`, not a claim
20	that all bytes rolled back. Private raw evidence is sensitive retention data,
21	not secure erasure, and never appears in public JSON or diagnostics.
22	
23	## Hard boundary
24	
25	An active transcript recorder blocks:
26	
27	- `git commit` (including amend/fixup);
28	- `git pull --rebase`, `git rebase`, and update-base helpers;
29	- merge/cherry-pick/integration into another ref; and
30	- worktree, branch, or agent-session retirement.
31	
32	Required order:
33	
34	```text
35	recorder exits and the exact session is synced
36	  -> exact artifacts are staged/sanitized and the message is finalized
37	  -> one ordinary hook-enabled commit is proven
38	  -> only then may history/ref movement or retirement begin
39	```
40	
41	A commit draft, a queued request, a clean scan, or a manual commit command is not
42	proof of completion by itself.
43	
44	## Lifecycle diagram
45	
46	```text
47	shell parent
48	  |
49	  | run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit claude
50	  v
51	running: foreground `specstory run claude`
52	  |
53	  | child stages feature paths only
54	  | explicit user commit authorization
55	  | queue-agent-commit.sh + exact selectors
56	  v
57	pending: inert metadata-only request (no transcript read/mutation/commit)
58	  |
59	  | child reports "finalization queued" and exits; no more repo operations
60	  v
61	child_exited (must be exit 0)
62	  |
63	  | one exact UUID sync (v2 defaults no-cloud)
64	  | read-only native --print export; full digest + source-generation proof
65	  v
66	synced
67	  |
68	  | parent-held token authorizes one finalizer call
69	  | prove no writer + unchanged HEAD/ref/index tree
70	  | stage/sanitize exact artifacts in locked alternate index
71	  v
72	prepared ----------------------------+
73	  |                                    |
74	  | sanitation changed bytes           | message + provenance validation
75	  v                                    | handoff drafts
76	rotation_required                      v
77	  |                                  committing
78	  | exact per-finding review, or rotate |
79	  | fresh manual authorization          | one ordinary `git commit -F`
80	  | rotation confirmation when needed   v
81	  +----------------------------------> done (exact commit proven)
82	
83	Any uncertain commit outcome remains `committing`: reconcile only, never retry.
84	```
85	
86	No request means `done/no_request`. A nonzero/signaled child or failed exact sync
87	does not enter finalization.
88	
89	## Authorization model
90	
91	Three separate facts are required:
92	
93	1. **Launcher capability:** `run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit` lets the
94	   outer parent call the finalizer once after successful child exit and sync.
95	2. **User intent:** the child queues only after the user explicitly authorizes
96	   the commit. Launcher capability is not permission to infer that intent.
97	3. **Recovery authorization:** every manual finalizer invocation repeats
98	   `--allow-commit`. A stored request, journal, message, or draft is never commit
99	   authority.
100	
101	`queue-agent-commit.sh --commit` names the requested action; it does not execute
102	or independently authorize a commit. `--runner-token` belongs only to the outer
103	runner and must never be [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed to the child.
104	
105	## Default commands
106	
107	### 1. Start in the intended worktree
108	
109	Create the worktree before the recorder. Then launch:
110	
111	```bash
112	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
113	  --allow-commit claude
114	```
115	
116	Pass SpecStory options only after `--`, for example:
117	
118	```bash
119	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
120	  --allow-commit claude -- --resume SESSION_UUID
121	```
122	
123	The child receives only `AGENT_HISTORY_REQUEST_PATH` and
124	`AGENT_HISTORY_RUN_ID`. Neither value authorizes finalization. V2 also proves the
125	live wrapper's native process identity and child ancestry before accepting a
126	queue; copying these environment strings into another process is insufficient.
127	
128	### V2 no-cloud and exact export
129	
130	No-cloud is the default for new runs. The wrapper [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es native
131	`--no-cloud-sync --no-stats --no-usage-analytics --no-version-check` flags to run
132	and normal sync, without rewriting user/project configuration. `--cloud-sync`
133	is an explicit per-run choice, never an implicit configuration default. The
134	verification export always remains no-cloud, even for an explicitly cloud-enabled
135	normal sync. Conflicting cloud flags and config/output/redaction/timezone
136	redirects are unsupported rather than silently changing the reviewed source.
137	
138	After successful child exit and process-group quiescence, the runner performs
139	one ordinary exact UUID sync, then reads a bounded private candidate from:
140	
141	```text
142	specstory sync claude -s UUID --print --silent --no-cloud-sync --no-stats \
143	  --no-usage-analytics --no-version-check
144	```
145	
146	It compares the **entire rendered digest** with the selected alias and binds the
147	native JSONL generation before sync, before export, and after export. An explicit
148	`--resume UUID` is pinned before launch and a queue for another UUID is refused.
149	For both resumed and new sessions, native JSONL must contain this run's exact
150	`queue_ack` in a typed tool result linked to a preceding tool call. User prose,
151	an older same-root transcript, and hand-written marker files are not evidence.
152	The child must let its real recorder retain the queue result and exit; never
153	write the acknowledgement into native history yourself. A UUID, mtime, or nonce
154	substring alone proves neither freshness nor content. Unsupported
155	flags/output, changing source, or a stale selected alias stops finalization;
156	other aliases are not removed or retargeted. Installed native compatibility is
157	verified only by the isolated synthetic native regression, never by a fake
158	provider success or a real user's session.
159	
160	### 2. Prepare exact inputs inside Claude
161	
162	Take the lowercase UUID from `/status`. Resolve an exact direct child of
163	`.specstory/history/`; if the UUID has aliases, supply the path as well. Decide
164	explicitly between one exact plan and no plan.
165	
166	```bash
167	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
168	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-09-01_02-14-50Z.md'
169	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-change.md'
170	
171	git add -- path/to/feature-a path/to/feature-b
172	```
173	
174	Stage only intended non-artifact feature paths. V2 rejects any already-staged
175	artifact diff; it never silently removes one from the user's index. Do not stage
176	the live transcript or plan; do not use broad `git add -A`.
177	
178	### 3. Queue only after explicit user commit authorization
179	
180	The base message must be nonempty UTF-8 subject/body and must not already carry
181	`AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, `Agent-Plan`, or
182	`Agent-History-Request`; the finalizer owns those trailers.
183	
184	```bash
185	MESSAGE_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agent-commit-message.txt"
186	printf '%s\n' \
187	  'feat(scope): summarize the change' \
188	  '' \
189	  'Explain the reason for the change.' > "$MESSAGE_FILE"
190	
191	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/queue-agent-commit.sh \
192	  --commit \
193	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
194	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" \
195	  --plan "$PLAN" \
196	  --message-file "$MESSAGE_FILE"
197	```
198	
199	Use `--no-plan` instead of `--plan` only when no plan exists. Both protocol
200	versions require a rendered SpecStory path.
201	
202	A successful response is one bounded JSON object with `status=queued`. An
203	identical second request is idempotent; a different request conflicts and the
204	first remains authoritative.
205	
206	After success:
207	
208	1. say **"finalization queued"**;
209	2. exit the Claude session; and
210	3. perform no more repository/index operations—not status, diff, staging,
211	   message editing, sync, finalizer, rebase, integration, or retirement.
212	
213	The queue captures the attached branch, HEAD object, and staged index tree. Any
214	later branch/index change makes it stale.
215	
216	## Why finalization waits for process exit
217	
218	### Normal pre-commit is unsafe during an active writer
219	
220	When staged files also have unstaged changes, pre-commit can stash the unstaged
221	patch, check out or rewrite the staged view for hooks, and restore the patch
222	afterward. An active recorder can append between those checkout/restore steps.
223	The restore may conflict, clobber a generation, or reintroduce bytes that a hook
224	just removed. Even without a mutating hook, the recorder can change content
225	after validation but before the commit object is created.
226	
227	Therefore:
228	
229	- `check-agent-artifact-secrets` is validation-only;
230	- generic mutating hooks/formatters exclude all agent/archive/install roots;
231	- no hook sanitizes or re-stages a working-tree transcript; and
232	- the post-session finalizer is the sole sanctioned mutator.
233	
234	### Why not a Stop hook, daemon, or live checkpoint
235	
236	- A Claude Stop hook runs before child/process and recorder quiescence are
237	  proven. It cannot establish the post-exit sync boundary.
238	- A detached `specstory watch` daemon outlives the agent and breaks the parent's
239	  recorder-lifetime proof.
240	- A live checkpoint necessarily snapshots a file that can still be appended and

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use leaf `--help` for syntax, `dev help <topic>` for workflows, and
`dev help --tree` for families. See [navigation](references/command-navigation.md)
for shortcuts and Try graduation/demotion; dashboard details: `dev help tui`.
Prefer supported JSON. Read help before mutation: some actions apply immediately,
others require preview/apply. Do not preload manuals or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening needs no task. Select direct, branch or worktree deliberately; use
  explicit `--base`. Managed worktrees stay outside repositories.
- Task-free worktrees use `dev git worktree create/open`; cleanup stays reviewed.
  `dev repo list --json` supplies navigation candidates, not external preferences/history.
- `dev work start` prepares checkout/runtime; agent launch is explicit. Parallel
  writers require disjoint ownership and verified targets.
- Completion, artifacts, retirement and branch deletion are separate. Finalize
  after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when integration is unproven.
- Cached/unknown observations, runtime `done` and merged PRs never authorize
  cleanup. Resolve guards; never improvise force removal or by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] checks.
- `dev pr checkout <URL>` is task-free; `--try` creates an independent clone.
  Provisioning is explicit; merge never cleans up locally.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktrees/lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Agents/prompts: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention, exact sessions and co-commit: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Cleanup: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Hygiene/scans/redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Forks/setup/organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH/fleet: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- [Snippets](references/snippets.md).
- PR/MR pages, diffnav, gh-dash, checkout and merge: [pull requests](references/pull-requests.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array with one object for every finding that survives, no maximum:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. Keep every finding that survives. There is no maximum. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

3	Standalone, stdlib-only Python (>=3.11) tool. Keep it dependency-free: target hosts are

9	  variables are stripped (`egress.clean_env`). Never call `subprocess` directly.
10	- Never trust backend checksums; verify with our own sha256 and sizes.
11	- Every remote object must be non-empty (Baidu drops empty files).
12	- Never read, print or log backend credentials/session files.
13	- Ledger formats (`sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`) and the manifest are compatibility
14	  surfaces: bump `MANIFEST_VERSION` and handle old records when changing them.

````text
1	# ferry
2	
3	Resumable bulk transfer between hosts that cannot reach each other, relayed through cloud
4	storage (Baidu Pan, any rclone remote, a GitHub draft release, or a shared directory) — or
5	directly over ssh with rsync when the hosts can reach each other.
6	
7	```
8	source host                         relay                          destination host
9	ferry send  ── pack ─▶ stage ─ push ─▶  prefix/<key>/part-*   ─ pull ─▶ verify ─▶ dest
10	                                         prefix/<key>/manifest.json  (READY, uploaded last)
11	```
12	
13	- **Units**: one key = one tar (or one raw file) = one remote directory. Resume is per unit
14	  and per part; nothing is re-uploaded after a restart.
15	- **Integrity**: sha256 is computed while packing (single source read). The receiver checks
16	  every part, the reassembled payload and the tar member count. Backend checksums (e.g.
17	  Baidu MD5) are never trusted.
18	- **Backpressure**: staging cap on the sender, remote free-space floor and in-flight limit,
19	  so a small relay can move a much larger dataset.
20	- **Read windows**: packing (the heavy source read) can be blocked in given hours, e.g.
21	  `"Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"`; uploads continue from staging.
22	- **Direct egress by default**: proxy variables are stripped from every backend process,
23	  backend-internal proxy settings are rejected, and endpoints resolving to clash/mihomo
24	  fake-ip or routed via a tun interface fail the preflight. See *Egress* below.
25	- **Source deletion policy**: `never`, `after_remote_size` (as soon as the relay holds a
26	  byte-identical-size copy; for regenerable data) or `after_receiver_ack` (after the
27	  destination verified sha256).
28	
29	## Install
30	
31	```bash
32	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry   # CLI on PATH
33	# or as a dependency:  ferry @ git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry@v0.1.0
34	```
35	
36	Python ≥ 3.11, no runtime dependencies. Backend CLIs are used as installed:
37	[BaiduPCS-Go](https://github.com/qjfoidnh/BaiduPCS-Go), `rclone`, `gh`.
38	
39	## Job file
40	
41	```toml
42	name = "daily-archive"                        # also the default state dir name
43	# state_dir = "~/.local/state/ferry/<name>"   # ledgers, logs, lock
44	
45	[units]
46	root = "/data/shared/dataset"
47	keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"               # key = file stem / dir name
48	members = ["order/{key}", "trans/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]
49	# or: glob = "exports/*.parquet"  (each match is a unit); pack = "none" sends files as-is
50	settle = "6h"                                 # skip units with files newer than this
51	resend_changed = true                         # re-send units whose fingerprint changed
52	recheck_recent = 30                           # after the first [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], recheck newest 30 keys
53	
54	[sender]
55	stage_dir = "~/.cache/ferry/daily-archive"
56	stage_cap = "300GB"
57	read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]
58	delete_source = "after_remote_size"           # never | after_remote_size | after_receiver_ack
59	
60	[receiver]
61	dest = "/srv/archive/dataset/{key[0:4]}"      # {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}
62	# extract = true                              # unpack; each unit path is replaced whole
63	# min_free = "20GB"                           # wait while the destination is this full
64	
65	[remote]
66	adapter = "baidupcs"                          # local | baidupcs | rclone | ghrelease
67	prefix = "/ferry/daily-archive"
68	part_size = "3900MiB"                         # default per adapter
69	min_free = "200GB"
70	max_inflight = "1.5TB"
71	egress = "direct"                             # direct | any
72	# trusted_interfaces = ["Meta"]               # TUN you verified routes this backend DIRECT
73	options = { download_threads = 4 }
74	```
75	
76	Adapter options:
77	
78	| adapter | options |
79	|---|---|
80	| `local` | `root` (directory used as relay) |
81	| `baidupcs` | `binary` (default: PATH or `~/.local/bin/BaiduPCS-Go`), `upload_threads`, `download_threads` (4) |
82	| `rclone` | `remote` (`"gdrive:"`, `"s3:bucket/relay"`), `flags`, `endpoints` (route check hosts) |
83	| `ghrelease` | `repo` (`owner/name`), `tag` (draft release, created if missing; refuses a published release) |
84	| `rsync` | `host` (ssh alias; `""` = local), `root` (landing dir on that host), `ssh_options`, `flags` |
85	
86	`[remote.sides.sender]` / `[remote.sides.receiver]` override `adapter` and `options` for one
87	side. Direct mode uses this: the sender pushes with `rsync` into a landing directory on the
88	destination host, and the receiver there reads the same directory with `local`:
89	
90	```toml
91	[remote]
92	adapter = "rsync"
93	prefix = "/inbox"
94	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
95	[remote.sides.receiver]
96	adapter = "local"
97	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
98	```
99	
100	Compared with plain `rsync -a`, this adds read windows, many-small-files packing, sha256
101	verification of every unit, source-deletion policies, ledgers with throughput/ETA, and
102	change detection for long-running mirrors.
103	
104	## Backfill and increments are the same job
105	
106	A job with `delete_source = "never"` mirrors a growing, occasionally repaired source:
107	
108	- **First run = backfill**: every unit not yet sent is packed and sent.
109	- **`--follow` = increments**: new keys are picked up; units still being written are held
110	  back by `settle`.
111	- **Repairs**: each unit has a fingerprint (sorted relative paths + sizes; stat only). A
112	  changed unit is re-sent as a new revision; with `extract = true` the receiver replaces
113	  each unit path wholesale, so files deleted at the source disappear too. After the first
114	  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] only the newest `recheck_recent` keys are re-fingerprinted each round; restart the
115	  sender (or run without `--follow`) for a full recheck.
116	- **Seeding**: if the destination already holds part of the data, run
117	  `ferry inventory job.toml` on the receiver. It publishes fingerprints of what it has;
118	  the sender marks identical units as `seeded` instead of sending them.
119	
120	## Commands
121	
122	```bash
123	ferry doctor job.toml [--side receiver]   # backend login, proxy settings, routes
124	ferry plan job.toml                       # units found under the source root
125	ferry send job.toml [--follow]            # until every unit is pushed (then marks done)
126	ferry receive job.toml [--once|--follow]  # until the sender is done and the relay is empty
127	ferry inventory job.toml [--root PATH]     # receiver: publish fingerprints for seeding
128	ferry status job.toml [--side receiver] [--scan-source] [--remote] [--json]
129	```
130	
131	A second sender (or receiver) for the same job on the same host exits immediately.
132	
133	### Running unattended
134	
135	ferry has no daemon of its own: `send`/`receive --follow` is a long-running loop that
136	polls for new or changed units. Put it under a supervisor; `ferry service` prints (or,
137	with `--install`, writes and enables) one:
138	
139	```bash
140	ferry service job.toml --side receiver                 # print a systemd user unit
141	ferry service job.toml --side receiver --install       # ~/.config/systemd/user/ferry-<job>-receiver.service
142	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
143	ferry service job.toml --side sender --uninstall
144	loginctl enable-linger $USER                           # let user services run without a login
145	```
146	
147	systemd units run `--follow` with `Restart=on-failure`; cron entries run one-shot
148	(`send`, `receive --once`) and rely on the job lock to skip overlapping runs. Any other
149	supervisor (pueue, tmux, launchd) works the same way: run the printed command.
150	
151	Library use (e.g. from an orchestrator):
152	
153	```python
154	import ferry
155	job = ferry.load_job("job.toml")
156	report = ferry.preflight(job, ferry.adapter_for(job, "sender"))
157	result = ferry.send(job)            # SendResult(pushed=..., pushed_bytes=..., ...)
158	st = ferry.side_status(job, "sender", remote=True)
159	```
160	
161	## Egress
162	
163	Proxy traffic is metered, so by default ferry insists on a direct path:
164	
165	1. `http(s)_proxy`, `all_proxy`, ... are removed from every backend process environment.
166	2. Backend tools' own proxy settings (BaiduPCS-Go `proxy`) are reported.
167	3. Each backend endpoint is resolved; a `198.18.0.0/15` answer (clash/mihomo fake-ip DNS)
168	   or a route via `tun*`/`utun*`/`Meta`/`wg*`/`tailscale*` is reported.
169	
170	With `egress = "direct"` any finding fails `send`/`receive`; `egress = "any"` (or
171	`--allow-proxy` for one run) accepts them with warnings — for backends that are only
172	reachable through a proxy, e.g. Google Drive from mainland China, where the proxy's own
173	rules may still pick DIRECT for some hosts. A transparent proxy on the router is not
174	visible from the host and cannot be detected.
175	
176	## Backend notes
177	
178	See [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — e.g. Baidu silently drops empty files and exits 0 on
179	errors, single-threaded Baidu downloads are ~4x slower, GitHub assets are limited to 2 GiB.
180
````
</details></tool-use>

+## English-first with selective translations
+
+For a complete English site with selected Traditional Chinese counterparts:
+
+- Keep English as the default content and UI language.
+- Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for pages the user wants translated. Missing siblings
+  fall back to English with `fallback_to_default: true`.
+- Keep root LLM artifacts in the default language; translated pages can still
+  expose their own source links for human readers.
+- A translated interface or language selector does not translate article bodies.
+  Enabling a locale is not consent to translate, nor does it make that locale
+  private: published translations are as public as the rest of the site.
+
+The existing language helper can skip initial placeholders:
+
+```bash
+bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
+  --lang zh-TW --default-lang en --no-stubs --dry-run
+# After reviewing the changes, repeat without --dry-run.
+```
+
+**`--no-stubs` applies only to that invocation.** The helper still records the
+configured languages. Running it again without this flag creates missing
+stubs, and `add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for all configured languages
+when adding a default-language page. There is no persistent on-demand mode yet.
+Until one is added, preserve that distinction when adding English pages and
+maintaining their nav/llmstxt entries; do not delete the locale from preferences
+or claim a nonexistent flag to suppress future stubs.
+
+For a specifically requested translation of an existing page, the page helper's
+`--lang zh-TW` creates only that sibling. Translate its body after consent, not
+as an automatic consequence of enabling the locale.
+
+**A placeholder is not a missing translation.** An existing `*.zh-TW.md` with
+"Translation pending" masks English fallback. `--no-stubs` leaves existing
+files alone; review them individually and obtain approval before removing or
+replacing anything. This selective policy does not override a project's rules
+requiring complete bilingual coverage (such as this repo's published catalog).
+
 ## Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement)
 
 This is the rule for any non-English page in a project that uses this skill:

 # MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
 
-The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
-`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
-the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
-**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.
+Last verified: **2026-10-30** against upstream documentation and release notes.
+This replaces the April 2026 assessment. Upstream support below is not a claim
+that this skill's sites have been built or migrated with Zensical.
 
 ## TL;DR
 
-- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
-  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
-  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
-- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
-  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
-  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
-- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
-  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
-  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
-  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
-- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
-  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.
+- **Keep this skill and existing MkDocs sites.** Preserve `mkdocs>=1.6,<2`,
+  `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`, the lockfile, and the managed build helper.
+- **English-first with optional Traditional Chinese is content i18n**, not
+  just a translated interface. Continue using MkDocs for that workflow until
+  a successor [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es the same output checks.
+- **Zensical is a viable candidate for a scoped single-language pilot**, not
+  an automatic default for every new project. Its `0.x` version alone is
+  neither a reason to reject it nor evidence of production readiness.
+- **Material maintenance ends on 2027-05-05** for security and critical fixes,
+  per its [changelog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/changelog/).
+  Staying on MkDocs is a time-bounded decision, not a promise of years of support.
+- A future `zensical-site-bootstrap` should be a **separate skill**. Updating
+  this skill must not silently change downstream projects' build engine.
 
 ## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
 
-Per the Material team's analysis
-([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):
+The [MkDocs announcement](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077)
+links to [version 2 pre-release documentation](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/).
+The Material team's [analysis, updated in October 2026](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/),
+reports removal of the MkDocs 1.x plugin system, a rewritten theme interface,
+and TOML configuration. It states that Material is incompatible and that no
+release date has been announced. Treat these as pre-release design statements,
+not a guarantee that the final design cannot change.
 
-| Change | Impact on this stack |
+`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, and `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` depend on the
+MkDocs plugin lifecycle. **PyMdown's snippets, superfences, and tabs are Python
+Markdown extensions, not MkDocs plugins**; assess Markdown compatibility
+separately rather than claiming every extension has the same failure mode.
+
+Do not upgrade this Material-based stack to MkDocs 2.0 without a separately
+validated migration. There is no need to adopt a different hosting provider:
+GitHub Actions can build the static output before GitHub Pages serves it.
+
+## What Zensical supports now
+
+The latest release at verification was
+[0.0.73 (2026-10-26)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.73).
+[0.0.67 (2026-09-30)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.67)
+added native `llmstxt` and a Copy as Markdown button. The old assessment that
+there was no published support for these functions is obsolete.
+
+The [plugin compatibility table](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/plugins/)
+is the authority for individual settings, not the presence of a plugin name in
+`mkdocs.yml`:
+
+| Requirement | Upstream status and limits |
 |---|---|
-| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
-| Theme system rewritten — nav [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
-| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
-| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
-| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |
-
-The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
-describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
-publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
-There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
-maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
-user-driven (solve a specific pain).
-
-## Material team's response — Zensical
-
-[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
-MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
-MkDocs 1.x**.
-
-What's known:
-
-- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
-- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
-- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
-  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
-- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
-  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
-- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.
-
-The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
-due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
-strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.
-
-## Why we cap explicitly
-
-Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
-which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
-accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:
-
-- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
-- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
-  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
-- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
-  else's defensive pin to stay correct.
-
-The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
-bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
-patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.
-
-## When to re-evaluate
-
-Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
-following are true**:
-
-1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
-   equivalent project signal of API stability).
-2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
-   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
-   per-language search).
-3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
-   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
-   per-page raw-markdown links).
-4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
-   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).
-
-Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
-MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
-them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.
-
-## What to avoid
-
-- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
-  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
-- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
-  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
-  individual users.
-- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
-  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
-  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
-- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
-  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
-  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.
-
-## Re-checking the situation
-
-A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:
-
-1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
-   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
-   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
-2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
-   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
-3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
-   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
-   release date been set?
-4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
-   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
-   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
-   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.
-
-## Source links
-
-- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
-  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
-- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
-- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
-- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>
-- MkDocs 2.0 community discussion (#4077):
-  <https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077>
+| Existing `mkdocs.yml` / Material look | Supported migration path; `theme.variant: classic` preserves the familiar appearance. Custom template overrides may need changes. |
+| Search / Python API reference | Native search and `mkdocstrings` integration are documented. Install the required handler; audit companion plugins separately. |
+| `llms.txt`, full output, Markdown counterparts | Native `llmstxt` since 0.0.67. Validate sections, exported content, and project Pages subpaths. Custom Python `preprocess` is ignored. |
+| Copy as Markdown | `content.action.copy` works for pages with Markdown counterparts. This is not proof of parity with every `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button or custom asset. |
+| UI language / alternate-language links | Documented, but not proof of suffix content translation, fallback, contextual switching, translated nav, or per-language search. |
+| Arbitrary MkDocs plugins / hooks | No MkDocs plugin API; arbitrary plugins cannot run. The migration guide lists `hooks` as unsupported. |
+| `gen-files` | Not supported directly; external generation is a separate workflow to evaluate. |
+
+**Unsupported plugin configuration can be silently ignored.** A successful
+build is insufficient: inspect the artifacts and user-visible behavior.
+Likewise, supported plugins may have ignored settings. Check every setting
+used by the target site, not just the package list.
+
+The [migration guide](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/migration/)
+does not require conversion to `zensical.toml` just to test an existing config.
+It also documents CLI and template differences; replacing `mkdocs` with
+`zensical` in the managed helper is not a migration strategy.
+
+Do not treat an unverified future release date as an adoption gate. In
+particular, the roadmap's November 5 Studio banner is not evidence for a
+November 5, 2026 release of the SSG as version 0.1.0.
+
+## English-first with optional Traditional Chinese
+
+Distinguish three layers:
+
+1. **UI localization** translates search labels and navigation controls.
+2. **A language selector** links to language-specific destinations; it does
+   not generate translated documents.
+3. **Content i18n** maps corresponding articles, handles missing translations,
+   and builds appropriate navigation and search for each locale.
+
+For this workflow, English is the complete default source for readers and
+agents. Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for articles the user wants in Traditional Chinese;
+missing translations should fall back to English. Root `llms.txt`,
+`llms-full.txt`, and Markdown sidecars remain default-language-only. Enabling
+a locale never authorizes automatic translation.
+
+MkDocs' `fallback_to_default: true` supports missing siblings, but an existing
+"Translation pending" stub counts as a translation and masks the fallback.
+**`add-language.sh --no-stubs` already enables a locale without generating
+siblings.** That flag is per-invocation, not a persistent preference:
+`add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for configured non-default languages.
+Read [the i18n guide](i18n-guide.md#english-first-with-selective-translations)
+before choosing this workflow; do not invent a persistent on-demand flag.
+
+Zensical's [language settings](https://zensical.org/docs/setup/language/)
+document UI localization and alternate links. The [roadmap](https://zensical.org/roadmap/)
+still lists broader content-i18n work. Neither establishes parity with this
+skill's suffix/fallback workflow. Do not replace it with a hand-built multi-site
+pipeline merely to claim that language switching exists.
+
+## Keep the caps; validate migrations separately
+
+Material 9.7.5+ also constrains MkDocs below 2. A resolver intersects that
+constraint with the project's direct requirements; the direct MkDocs dependency
+is **not** resolved independently. Explicit bounds still document this skill's
+own support contract and remain protective if upstream metadata changes.
+
+Keep bounds consistent in the dependency template, optional social extra,
+manual recipe, and initializer's existing-`pyproject.toml` hints. Commit a
+lockfile in consuming projects and use controlled patch/minor updates with
+regression tests. Bounds permit those updates; they do not refresh a lockfile
+or supply security fixes automatically.
+
+**Migrating to Zensical does not mean lifting the MkDocs cap.** Change the
+builder and dependencies deliberately for each approved migration; retain the
+caps wherever the MkDocs/Material stack remains in use.
+
+## Re-evaluation and adoption gates
+
+Review again by **January 2027**, ahead of Material's maintenance deadline,
+or sooner after relevant security advisories or new content-i18n support.
+This is a review recommendation, not an automatically scheduled task.
+
+Before a pilot becomes a default or an existing site is migrated:
+
+1. Inventory plugins, hooks, extensions, templates, and build-time generators.
+   Record unsupported or unknown settings instead of accepting silent omission.
+2. Build an isolated, version-locked fixture. Compare navigation, search,
+   code blocks/snippets, images, anchors, and project Pages subpath links.
+3. Verify `llms.txt` sections, full content, Markdown counterparts, and the
+   actual Copy as Markdown behavior, not just file existence or exit status.
+4. For content-i18n sites, verify English defaults, selected zh-TW counterparts,
+   missing-translation fallback, same-page switching, locale navigation/search,
+   correct source links, and default-language-only LLM artifacts.
+5. Preserve sources and the last successful output on failure. Document rollback
+   and get consent before switching an existing project or deploying anything.
+
+A single-language pilot can validate steps 1–3 without solving i18n, but that
+result does **not** make it the default for English-first bilingual projects.
+Keep this skill's two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build and repair tools until an equivalent migration
+has [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed all applicable gates; do not copy that MkDocs-specific machinery into
+a new Zensical skill.

1	"""Backend adapter interface.
2	
3	Remote paths are POSIX-style strings rooted at the backend (``/ferry/cf/20200102/part-0000``).
4	Adapters must make a file visible only once it is complete (cloud uploads do this
5	naturally; the local adapter writes to a temporary name and renames).
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import posixpath
10	from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	
14	class Adapter(ABC):
15	    name: str = "?"
16	    #: Hostnames contacted by this backend; checked by the egress guard.
17	    endpoints: tuple[str, ...] = ()
18	    #: Largest single object the backend accepts (None = no known limit).
19	    max_part_size: int | None = None
20	    #: Part size used when the job does not set one.
21	    default_part_size: int | None = None
22	
23	    def __init__(self, options: dict, log: Path | None = None):
24	        self.options = options
25	        self.log = log
26	
27	    def check(self) -> list[str]:
28	        """Problems that make the backend unusable (missing binary, not logged in...)."""
29	        return []
30	
31	    def proxy_settings(self) -> list[str]:
32	        """Proxies configured inside the backend tool itself (not via environment)."""
33	        return []
34	
35	    @abstractmethod
36	    def put(self, local: Path, remote: str) -> None: ...
37	
38	    @abstractmethod
39	    def get(self, remote: str, local: Path) -> None: ...
40	
41	    @abstractmethod
42	    def stat(self, remote: str) -> int | None:
43	        """Size of a remote file, or None when it does not exist."""
44	
45	    @abstractmethod
46	    def list(self, remote_dir: str) -> list[str]:
47	        """Child names of a remote directory; directories end with '/'. [] if missing."""
48	
49	    @abstractmethod
50	    def delete(self, remote: str) -> None:
51	        """Delete a file or a whole directory; missing paths are not an error."""
52	
53	    def free_bytes(self) -> int | None:
54	        return None
55	
56	    def put_text(self, text: str, remote: str, scratch: Path) -> None:
57	        """Upload a small text object (manifests, acks) via a scratch file of the same name."""
58	        scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
59	        local = scratch / posixpath.basename(remote)
60	        local.write_text(text)
61	        try:
62	            self.put(local, remote)
63	        finally:
64	            local.unlink(missing_ok=True)
65	
66	    def get_text(self, remote: str, scratch: Path) -> str | None:
67	        if self.stat(remote) is None:
68	            return None
69	        scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
70	        local = scratch / posixpath.basename(remote)
71	        try:
72	            self.get(remote, local)
73	            return local.read_text()
74	        finally:
75	            local.unlink(missing_ok=True)
76

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	<!-- td-agent-instructions:start -->
4	<!-- td-agent-instructions:version=3 -->
5	
6	## Working with td
7	
8	td keeps task context durable across sessions. In a new context, run `td usage --new-session -q` to see current work.
9	
10	Use your judgment about how much tracking a task needs. For substantive work: `td start <id>`, record progress with `td log`, hand off with `td handoff <id>`, then `td review <id>`.
11	
12	Closing needs a review. Say who did it (default trusted mode; delegated/strict allow only the first):
13	
14	- independent session: `td approve <id> --reason "..."`
15	- a sub-agent: `td approve <id> --reviewed-by "<who>"`
16	- you: `td approve <id> --self-review --reason "..."`
17	
18	Prefer a reviewer with its own `TD_CONTEXT_ID`; never name one who did not review.
19	
20	Run `td usage` or `td <command> --help`.
21	
22	<!-- td-agent-instructions:end -->
23	
24	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
25	
26	## Project Overview
27	
28	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains local canonical skills (`skills/local/`), first-party project skills (`skills/owned/`), and cherry-picked third-party skills (`skills/vendor/`). Owned and vendor copies sync from their canonical upstream repos.
29	
30	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`owned/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	```bash
35	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
36	make sync
37	
38	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
39	make sync-check
40	
41	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
42	make kanban
43	
44	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
45	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
46	make marketplace
47	
48	# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
49	make native-marketplace-smoke
50	
51	# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
52	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
53	make lint-frontmatter
54	
55	# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
56	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
57	make validate
58	
59	# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
60	make install-hooks
61	
62	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
63	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
64	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
65	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
66	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
67	
68	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
69	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
70	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
71	
72	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
73	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
74	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
75	
76	# Start a TODO item as a td issue (td bridge; no-op without td, TODO.md unchanged)
77	./scripts/start-todo.sh --title "<substring>"
78	
79	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
80	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
81	
82	# Create a new local skill
83	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
84	
85	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
86	uv sync --extra docs
87	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
88	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
89	```
90	
91	## Source categories and upstream sync
92	
93	- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
94	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
95	- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.
96	
97	`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
98	`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
99	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
100	with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
101	cannot serve as a distributable copy.
102	
103	An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
104	contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
105	After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
106	Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).
107	
108	## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)
109	
110	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
111	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
112	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
113	
114	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
115	
116	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
117	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
118	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
119	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
120	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
121	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
122	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
123	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
124	
125	Active series in this repo:
126	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
127	
128	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
129	
130	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
131	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
132	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
133	
134	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
135	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
136	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
137	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
138	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
139	  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
140	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
141	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
142	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
143	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
144	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
145	
146	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
147	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
148	
149	## Marketplace Catalog
150	
151	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
152	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
153	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
154	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
155	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
156	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
157	for the full mechanism.
158	
159	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
160	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
161	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
162	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
163	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
164	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
165	
166	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
167	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
168	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
169	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
170	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
171	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
172	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
173	within-group caveat in
174	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
175	
176	## SKILL.md Format
177	
178	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
179	
180	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
181	
182	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
183	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
184	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
185	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
186	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
187	
188	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
189	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
190	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
191	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
192	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
193	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
194	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
195	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
196	
197	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
198	
199	```bash
200	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
201	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
202	
203	# …or remove them afterward
204	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
205	```
206	
207	## Project Memory Workflow
208	
209	<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance -->
210	### Issue-driven workflow (GitHub)
211	
212	This project uses GitHub Issues as the canonical backlog and GitHub
213	Discussions for evaluative/research topics. The `forge-native-dev` skill
214	provides the scripts below.
215	
216	| Information | Lives in | Why |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| Actionable work (bugs, features, chores) | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) | Searchable, assignable, cross-linkable |
219	| Evaluations, "should we?", research | [Discussions](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/discussions) | Threaded, collaborative |
220	| Research docs, trade-off analysis | `backlog/` | In-repo, diffable, reviewed in PRs |
221	| Past traps, debugging knowledge | `pitfalls/` | Grep-able by symptom, portable |
222	| Backlog visualization | [Project board](https://github.com/users/daviddwlee84/projects/11) | Built-in to the forge |
223	| Historical record | `TODO.md` `## Done` section | In git |
224	
225	**Capture intent as Issues** — when the user describes a bug, idea, or
226	"maybe later" item, create an Issue with appropriate labels. Do not ask
227	"should I create an issue?" — default to creating one.
228	
229	**Work lifecycle:**
230	1. Start: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start <issue-number>`
231	2. Work in the worktree, commit conventionally
232	3. Finish: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh finish <issue-number>`
233	4. After merge: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-cleanup.sh`
234	
235	**Check for work:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-issue.sh list --assignee @me`
236	
237	**Dashboard:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-status.sh`
238	
239	**PRs are review gates, not proposals.** The issue describes intent; the
240	PR is the diff to review. Default merge strategy: **squash and merge**.
241	<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance (end) -->
242	
243	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
244	
245	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
246	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
247	own conventions). It has four subareas:
248	
249	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
250	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
251	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
252	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
253	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
254	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
255	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
256	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
257	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
258	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
259	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
260	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
261	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
262	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
263	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
264	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
265	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
266	  status / license / last_verified`).
267	
268	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
269	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
270	
271	| Status | Meaning |
272	|---|---|
273	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
274	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
275	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
276	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
277	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
278	
279	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
280	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
281	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
282	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
283	
284	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
285	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
286	
287	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
288	
289	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
290	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
291	
292	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
293	2. The root cause
294	3. The workaround
295	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
296	
297	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
298	the explanation they do not know yet.
299
````

6	## Working with td
7	
8	td keeps task context durable across sessions. In a new context, run `td usage --new-session -q` to see current work.
9	
10	Use your judgment about how much tracking a task needs. For substantive work: `td start <id>`, record progress with `td log`, hand off with `td handoff <id>`, then `td review <id>`.
11	
12	Closing needs a review. Say who did it (default trusted mode; delegated/strict allow only the first):
13	
14	- independent session: `td approve <id> --reason "..."`
15	- a sub-agent: `td approve <id> --reviewed-by "<who>"`
16	- you: `td approve <id> --self-review --reason "..."`
17	
18	Prefer a reviewer with its own `TD_CONTEXT_ID`; never name one who did not review.
19	
20	Run `td usage` or `td <command> --help`.
21	
22	<!-- td-agent-instructions:end -->

24	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

26	## Project Overview
27	
28	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains local canonical skills (`skills/local/`), first-party project skills (`skills/owned/`), and cherry-picked third-party skills (`skills/vendor/`). Owned and vendor copies sync from their canonical upstream repos.
29	
30	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`owned/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	```bash
35	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
36	make sync
37	
38	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
39	make sync-check
40	
41	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
42	make kanban
43	
44	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
45	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
46	make marketplace
47	
48	# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
49	make native-marketplace-smoke
50	
51	# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
52	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
53	make lint-frontmatter
54	
55	# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
56	# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
57	make validate
58	
59	# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
60	make install-hooks
61	
62	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
63	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
64	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
65	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
66	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
67	
68	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
69	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
70	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
71	
72	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
73	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
74	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
75	
76	# Start a TODO item as a td issue (td bridge; no-op without td, TODO.md unchanged)
77	./scripts/start-todo.sh --title "<substring>"
78	
79	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
80	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
81	
82	# Create a new local skill
83	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
84	
85	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
86	uv sync --extra docs
87	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
88	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
89	```

241	<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance (end) -->
242	
243	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
244	
245	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
246	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
247	own conventions). It has four subareas:
248	
249	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
250	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
251	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
252	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
253	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
254	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
255	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
256	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
257	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
258	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
259	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
260	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
261	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
262	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
263	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
264	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
265	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
266	  status / license / last_verified`).
267	
268	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
269	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
270	
271	| Status | Meaning |
272	|---|---|
273	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
274	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
275	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
276	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
277	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
278	
279	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
280	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
281	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
282	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
283	
284	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
285	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
286	
287	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
288	
289	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
290	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
291	
292	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
293	2. The root cause
294	3. The workaround
295	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
296	
297	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
298	the explanation they do not know yet.

126	+## English-first with selective translations
127	+
128	+For a complete English site with selected Traditional Chinese counterparts:
129	+
130	+- Keep English as the default content and UI language.
131	+- Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for pages the user wants translated. Missing siblings
132	+  fall back to English with `fallback_to_default: true`.
133	+- Keep root LLM artifacts in the default language; translated pages can still
134	+  expose their own source links for human readers.
135	+- A translated interface or language selector does not translate article bodies.
136	+  Enabling a locale is not consent to translate, nor does it make that locale
137	+  private: published translations are as public as the rest of the site.
138	+
139	+The existing language helper can skip initial placeholders:
140	+
141	+```bash
142	+bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
143	+  --lang zh-TW --default-lang en --no-stubs --dry-run
144	+# After reviewing the changes, repeat without --dry-run.
145	+```
146	+
147	+**`--no-stubs` applies only to that invocation.** The helper still records the
148	+configured languages. Running it again without this flag creates missing
149	+stubs, and `add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for all configured languages
150	+when adding a default-language page. There is no persistent on-demand mode yet.
151	+Until one is added, preserve that distinction when adding English pages and
152	+maintaining their nav/llmstxt entries; do not delete the locale from preferences
153	+or claim a nonexistent flag to suppress future stubs.
154	+
155	+For a specifically requested translation of an existing page, the page helper's
156	+`--lang zh-TW` creates only that sibling. Translate its body after consent, not
157	+as an automatic consequence of enabling the locale.
158	+
159	+**A placeholder is not a missing translation.** An existing `*.zh-TW.md` with
160	+"Translation pending" masks English fallback. `--no-stubs` leaves existing
161	+files alone; review them individually and obtain approval before removing or
162	+replacing anything. This selective policy does not override a project's rules
163	+requiring complete bilingual coverage (such as this repo's published catalog).
164	+
