173	 # MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
174	 
175	-The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
176	-`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
177	-the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
178	-**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.
179	+Last verified: **2026-10-30** against upstream documentation and release notes.
180	+This replaces the April 2026 assessment. Upstream support below is not a claim
181	+that this skill's sites have been built or migrated with Zensical.
182	 
183	 ## TL;DR
184	 
185	-- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
186	-  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
187	-  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
188	-- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
189	-  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
190	-  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
191	-- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
192	-  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
193	-  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
194	-  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
195	-- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
196	-  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.
197	+- **Keep this skill and existing MkDocs sites.** Preserve `mkdocs>=1.6,<2`,
198	+  `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`, the lockfile, and the managed build helper.
199	+- **English-first with optional Traditional Chinese is content i18n**, not
200	+  just a translated interface. Continue using MkDocs for that workflow until
201	+  a successor [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es the same output checks.
202	+- **Zensical is a viable candidate for a scoped single-language pilot**, not
203	+  an automatic default for every new project. Its `0.x` version alone is
204	+  neither a reason to reject it nor evidence of production readiness.
205	+- **Material maintenance ends on 2027-05-05** for security and critical fixes,
206	+  per its [changelog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/changelog/).
207	+  Staying on MkDocs is a time-bounded decision, not a promise of years of support.
208	+- A future `zensical-site-bootstrap` should be a **separate skill**. Updating
209	+  this skill must not silently change downstream projects' build engine.
210	 
211	 ## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
212	 
213	-Per the Material team's analysis
214	-([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):
215	+The [MkDocs announcement](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077)
216	+links to [version 2 pre-release documentation](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/).
217	+The Material team's [analysis, updated in October 2026](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/),
218	+reports removal of the MkDocs 1.x plugin system, a rewritten theme interface,
219	+and TOML configuration. It states that Material is incompatible and that no
220	+release date has been announced. Treat these as pre-release design statements,
221	+not a guarantee that the final design cannot change.
222	 
223	-| Change | Impact on this stack |
224	+`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, and `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` depend on the
225	+MkDocs plugin lifecycle. **PyMdown's snippets, superfences, and tabs are Python
226	+Markdown extensions, not MkDocs plugins**; assess Markdown compatibility
227	+separately rather than claiming every extension has the same failure mode.
228	+
229	+Do not upgrade this Material-based stack to MkDocs 2.0 without a separately
230	+validated migration. There is no need to adopt a different hosting provider:
231	+GitHub Actions can build the static output before GitHub Pages serves it.
232	+
233	+## What Zensical supports now
234	+
235	+The latest release at verification was
236	+[0.0.73 (2026-10-26)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.73).
237	+[0.0.67 (2026-09-30)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.67)
238	+added native `llmstxt` and a Copy as Markdown button. The old assessment that
239	+there was no published support for these functions is obsolete.
240	+
241	+The [plugin compatibility table](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/plugins/)
242	+is the authority for individual settings, not the presence of a plugin name in
243	+`mkdocs.yml`:
244	+
245	+| Requirement | Upstream status and limits |
246	 |---|---|
247	-| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
248	-| Theme system rewritten — nav [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
249	-| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
250	-| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
251	-| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |
252	-
253	-The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
254	-describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
255	-publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
256	-There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
257	-maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
258	-user-driven (solve a specific pain).
259	-
260	-## Material team's response — Zensical
261	-
262	-[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
263	-MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
264	-MkDocs 1.x**.
265	-
266	-What's known:
267	-
268	-- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
269	-- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
270	-- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
271	-  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
272	-- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
273	-  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
274	-- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.
275	-
276	-The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
277	-due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
278	-strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.
279	-
280	-## Why we cap explicitly
281	-
282	-Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
283	-which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
284	-accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:
285	-
286	-- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
287	-- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
288	-  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
289	-- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
290	-  else's defensive pin to stay correct.
291	-
292	-The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
293	-bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
294	-patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.
295	-
296	-## When to re-evaluate
297	-
298	-Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
299	-following are true**:
300	-
301	-1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
302	-   equivalent project signal of API stability).
303	-2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
304	-   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
305	-   per-language search).
306	-3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
307	-   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
308	-   per-page raw-markdown links).
309	-4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
310	-   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).
311	-
312	-Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
313	-MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
314	-them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.
315	-
316	-## What to avoid
317	-
318	-- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
319	-  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
320	-- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
321	-  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
322	-  individual users.
323	-- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
324	-  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
325	-  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
326	-- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
327	-  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
328	-  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.
329	-
330	-## Re-checking the situation
331	-
332	-A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:
333	-
334	-1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
335	-   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
336	-   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
337	-2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
338	-   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
339	-3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
340	-   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
341	-   release date been set?
342	-4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
343	-   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
344	-   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
345	-   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.
346	-
347	-## Source links
348	-
349	-- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
350	-  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
351	-- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
352	-- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
353	-- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>
354	-- MkDocs 2.0 community discussion (#4077):
355	-  <https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077>
356	+| Existing `mkdocs.yml` / Material look | Supported migration path; `theme.variant: classic` preserves the familiar appearance. Custom template overrides may need changes. |
357	+| Search / Python API reference | Native search and `mkdocstrings` integration are documented. Install the required handler; audit companion plugins separately. |
358	+| `llms.txt`, full output, Markdown counterparts | Native `llmstxt` since 0.0.67. Validate sections, exported content, and project Pages subpaths. Custom Python `preprocess` is ignored. |
359	+| Copy as Markdown | `content.action.copy` works for pages with Markdown counterparts. This is not proof of parity with every `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button or custom asset. |
360	+| UI language / alternate-language links | Documented, but not proof of suffix content translation, fallback, contextual switching, translated nav, or per-language search. |
361	+| Arbitrary MkDocs plugins / hooks | No MkDocs plugin API; arbitrary plugins cannot run. The migration guide lists `hooks` as unsupported. |
362	+| `gen-files` | Not supported directly; external generation is a separate workflow to evaluate. |
363	+
364	+**Unsupported plugin configuration can be silently ignored.** A successful
365	+build is insufficient: inspect the artifacts and user-visible behavior.
366	+Likewise, supported plugins may have ignored settings. Check every setting
367	+used by the target site, not just the package list.
368	+
369	+The [migration guide](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/migration/)
370	+does not require conversion to `zensical.toml` just to test an existing config.
371	+It also documents CLI and template differences; replacing `mkdocs` with
372	+`zensical` in the managed helper is not a migration strategy.
373	+
374	+Do not treat an unverified future release date as an adoption gate. In
375	+particular, the roadmap's November 5 Studio banner is not evidence for a
376	+November 5, 2026 release of the SSG as version 0.1.0.
377	+
378	+## English-first with optional Traditional Chinese
379	+
380	+Distinguish three layers:
381	+
382	+1. **UI localization** translates search labels and navigation controls.
383	+2. **A language selector** links to language-specific destinations; it does
384	+   not generate translated documents.
385	+3. **Content i18n** maps corresponding articles, handles missing translations,
386	+   and builds appropriate navigation and search for each locale.
387	+
388	+For this workflow, English is the complete default source for readers and
389	+agents. Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for articles the user wants in Traditional Chinese;
390	+missing translations should fall back to English. Root `llms.txt`,
391	+`llms-full.txt`, and Markdown sidecars remain default-language-only. Enabling
392	+a locale never authorizes automatic translation.
393	+
394	+MkDocs' `fallback_to_default: true` supports missing siblings, but an existing
395	+"Translation pending" stub counts as a translation and masks the fallback.
396	+**`add-language.sh --no-stubs` already enables a locale without generating
397	+siblings.** That flag is per-invocation, not a persistent preference:
398	+`add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for configured non-default languages.
399	+Read [the i18n guide](i18n-guide.md#english-first-with-selective-translations)
400	+before choosing this workflow; do not invent a persistent on-demand flag.
401	+
402	+Zensical's [language settings](https://zensical.org/docs/setup/language/)
403	+document UI localization and alternate links. The [roadmap](https://zensical.org/roadmap/)
404	+still lists broader content-i18n work. Neither establishes parity with this
405	+skill's suffix/fallback workflow. Do not replace it with a hand-built multi-site
406	+pipeline merely to claim that language switching exists.
407	+
408	+## Keep the caps; validate migrations separately
409	+
410	+Material 9.7.5+ also constrains MkDocs below 2. A resolver intersects that
411	+constraint with the project's direct requirements; the direct MkDocs dependency
412	+is **not** resolved independently. Explicit bounds still document this skill's
413	+own support contract and remain protective if upstream metadata changes.
414	+
415	+Keep bounds consistent in the dependency template, optional social extra,
416	+manual recipe, and initializer's existing-`pyproject.toml` hints. Commit a

```text
1	# Deployment exclusion cheatsheet
2	
3	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are repo metadata for maintainers,
4	not files to ship to users. Make sure they are excluded from whatever
5	packaging or deployment mechanism the host project uses.
6	
7	The bundled `scripts/init.sh` does NOT modify ignore files automatically
8	(too high blast radius). It prints the lines you should add. Reference
9	table:
10	
11	| Mechanism | File | Lines to add |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| chezmoi | `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` | `TODO.md`<br>`backlog/**`<br>`pitfalls/**` |
14	| Python (setuptools) | `MANIFEST.in` | `exclude TODO.md`<br>`recursive-exclude backlog *`<br>`recursive-exclude pitfalls *` |
15	| npm | `package.json` `files` allowlist OR `.npmignore` | `TODO.md`<br>`backlog/`<br>`pitfalls/` |
16	| Docker | `.dockerignore` | `TODO.md`<br>`backlog/`<br>`pitfalls/` |
17	| Generic | confirm `.gitignore` does NOT ignore them | (they should be tracked) |
18	
19	For Python wheels, also confirm your `pyproject.toml` `[tool.setuptools]`
20	`packages` / `include` configuration does not pick up these directories.
21
```
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	---
2	name: python-project-best-practice
3	description: 'Modern Python project conventions for the agentic-coding era: uv + src layout, Tyro CLIs with shell completion, marimo notebooks that run as scripts, loguru, and ruff/type/pytest gates behind a Justfile, plus an AGENTS.md contract agents can drive. Use when starting a new Python project or package, scaffolding a pyproject.toml, choosing a CLI/test/lint/logging stack, making a tool installable with `uv tool install`, or modernizing a legacy setup.py / requirements.txt / poetry / conda repo.'
4	---
5	
6	# Python Project Best Practice
7	
8	An opinionated baseline for Python projects that both people and agents work
9	in. Two entry points: scaffold a new project (Workflow A), or score and
10	modernize an existing one (Workflow B). The same conventions drive both.
11	
12	The bias throughout: **every operation has one canonical, discoverable,
13	non-interactive command**. That is what makes a project workable by an agent,
14	and it happens to be what makes it pleasant for humans.
15	
16	## When to use
17	
18	- "Start a new Python project / package / CLI tool"
19	- "Set up pyproject.toml", "which should I use, uv or poetry / pip-tools?"
20	- "How do I make this installable so someone can just run it?"
21	- "Modernize this repo" — setup.py, requirements.txt, poetry, conda, flat layout
22	- Choosing between ruff/black, mypy/ty, extras/dependency-groups, just/taskipy
23	- Adding a CLI, notebooks, an HTTP surface, or a Rust extension to a Python repo
24	
25	## When NOT to use
26	
27	These skills own their territory. Delegate rather than restate:
28	
29	| Topic | Skill |
30	|---|---|
31	| `--help` / `--dry-run` / `--print-config` / exit-code design and verification | `verifiable-surfaces` |
32	| marimo dual-mode notebooks, sweeps, tracking | `marimo-batch-mlflow`; format rules in `marimo-notebook`; widgets in `anywidget` |
33	| Production FastAPI internals | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
34	| Docs site, GitHub Pages, llms.txt | `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` |
35	| Releasing a compiled Go/Rust binary | `cli-release-distribution` (Python distribution stays here) |
36	| pre-commit setup, secret remediation | `agent-history-hygiene` |
37	| TDD discipline itself | `engineering-fundamentals/tdd` |
38	| Building an MCP server | `mcp-builder` (read `references/api-and-services.md` first — usually you want a subcommand) |
39	
40	Also not for: a one-file script (use a PEP 723 header and stop), or a
41	maintenance-only repo where a migration buys nothing.
42	
43	## Authoritative sources
44	
45	Fetch the page rather than guessing — this toolchain moves fast, and several
46	of these projects change CLI surface between minor versions.
47	
48	| Thing | Where |
49	|---|---|
50	| uv | <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/> · CLI reference <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/> |
51	| ruff rules | <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/> |
52	| ty | <https://github.com/astral-sh/ty> (0.0.x — check the version before quoting behavior) |
53	| Tyro | <https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/> · completion <https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/> |
54	| loguru | <https://loguru.readthedocs.io/> |
55	| pydantic-settings | <https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/> |
56	| PyO3 / maturin | <https://pyo3.rs/> · <https://www.maturin.rs/> |
57	| Python versions / EOL | <https://devguide.python.org/versions/> (3.10 EOL Oct 2026; default floor `>=3.11`) |
58	| Packaging specs | <https://packaging.python.org/> · PEP 735 (dependency groups), PEP 723 (script deps) |
59	
60	## The canonical layout
61	
62	```
63	pyproject.toml          [project] + [dependency-groups] + tool config. One file.
64	uv.lock                 committed. Pins YOUR dev env, never your users'.
65	.python-version         dev interpreter (uv python pin). Not the same as requires-python.
66	Justfile                every supported operation. `just --list` is the surface.
67	AGENTS.md               the agent contract. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it.
68	README.md               getting started for humans: uv sync, just check.
69	.envrc / .env.example   direnv activation; the tracked contract for .env (which is ignored).
70	
71	src/my_tool/            src layout: tests import the INSTALLED package
72	  core.py               domain logic. stdlib logging. no side effects at import.
73	  _log.py               loguru setup. called by entry points only.
74	  settings.py           pydantic-settings: defaults < .env < environment.
75	  cli/                  one frozen dataclass per subcommand; run() -> exit code
76	  py.typed              without this your annotations are invisible to consumers
77	tests/                  mirrors src/ module for module
78	scripts/                repo helpers, NOT importable from the package
79	notebooks/              marimo notebooks. import the package; nothing imports them.
80	.agents/skills/my-tool/ the package's own skill, shipped with the code
81	.github/workflows/ci.yml  runs the same gate as `just check`
82	```
83	
84	Two arrows to keep straight: `notebooks/` and `scripts/` may import the
85	package; the package imports neither.
86	
87	## Decision: which profile?
88	
89	Start at the smallest row that fits and add later — profiles are additive, so
90	"agentic later" costs nothing now.
91	
92	| Profile | Use when | Adds | Read |
93	|---|---|---|---|
94	| `minimal` | a library nobody runs from a shell yet | package, tests, Justfile, CI, AGENTS.md | `uv-and-pyproject`, `quality-gates` |
95	| `cli` **(default)** | almost everything | Tyro CLI, loguru, pydantic-settings, `[project.scripts]` | + `tyro-cli`, `logging-and-config` |
96	| `lib` | others will import it | publishing metadata, `py.typed` | + `uv-and-pyproject` §Distribution |
97	| `api` | it serves HTTP | FastAPI app, `/docs`, `/openapi.json` | + `api-and-services` |
98	| `ml` | experiments and notebooks | marimo notebook that is also a CLI | + `notebooks-and-widgets` |
99	| `rust` | a profiled, CPU-bound hot loop | maturin backend, PyO3 crate, `.pyi` stubs | + `rust-pyo3` |
100	
101	Companion skills to recommend, by profile, are in
102	[`references/agent-interface.md`](references/agent-interface.md) and in the
103	scaffolder's `recommended_skills[]`.
104	
105	## Workflow A — new project from zero
````

- **`gen-files`** is unsupported. The page suggests generating files separately and tracking them in version control; its `uvx` example requires `mkdocs.yml` and does not work with `zensical.toml`.

- **Arbitrary MkDocs plugins:** Zensical does not run arbitrary plugins or provide the MkDocs plugin API.  
  > “Zensical does not currently run arbitrary MkDocs plugins or expose the MkDocs plugin API.”

- **Ignored configurations:** Settings marked ignored for supported plugins are silently ignored without validation or warnings. Configuration for plugins absent from the supported list is also silently ignored, and those plugins are not imported or run. Unknown settings for supported plugins instead cause a configuration error.

````text
1	# Bilingual / multi-language docs
2	
3	How to add a non-English language (typically Traditional Chinese, `zh-TW`) to
4	a MkDocs Material site bootstrapped by this skill, and how to keep
5	terminology consistent so future contributors — human or agent — don't
6	introduce ambiguity.
7	
8	## TL;DR
9	
10	```bash
11	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
12	uv sync --extra docs
13	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
14	```
15	
16	The Material header gains a language switcher. The managed build helper keeps
17	both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es strict, publishes all locale HTML, and produces root `llms.txt`,
18	`llms-full.txt`, and `.md` sidecars from the default language only. Translate
19	the stub bodies when ready.
20	
21	For local HTML preview, `uv run mkdocs serve` and direct `uv run mkdocs build
22	--strict` remain safe: the config disables `llmstxt` unless the helper enables
23	it. Use the helper for every artifact that will be deployed.
24	
25	## Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure
26	
27	[Squidfunk's recommended approach](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/discussions/2346)
28	for content translation is the
29	[`mkdocs-static-i18n`](https://github.com/ultrabug/mkdocs-static-i18n) plugin.
30	We use **`docs_structure: suffix`** rather than `folder` because:
31	
32	- **Zero file moves on retrofit.** Existing `docs/index.md`,
33	  `docs/getting-started.md`, etc. stay where they are. The `folder` mode
34	  would force you to move every file into `docs/en/` first.
35	- **Relative links keep working.** Sibling files share the same directory.
36	- **Per-page opt-in to translation.** A page is only translated when
37	  `<page>.<lang>.md` exists; otherwise the plugin falls back to the default
38	  language (`fallback_to_default: true`).
39	
40	The trade-off: directory listings get crowded once you have many languages.
41	For sites that grow to 5+ languages the `folder` structure starts to win on
42	readability — but you can migrate later.
43	
44	## English-first with selective translations
45	
46	For a complete English site with selected Traditional Chinese counterparts:
47	
48	- Keep English as the default content and UI language.
49	- Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for pages the user wants translated. Missing siblings
50	  fall back to English with `fallback_to_default: true`.
51	- Keep root LLM artifacts in the default language; translated pages can still
52	  expose their own source links for human readers.
53	- A translated interface or language selector does not translate article bodies.
54	  Enabling a locale is not consent to translate, nor does it make that locale
55	  private: published translations are as public as the rest of the site.
56	
57	The existing language helper can skip initial placeholders:
58	
59	```bash
60	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
61	  --lang zh-TW --default-lang en --no-stubs --dry-run
62	# After reviewing the changes, repeat without --dry-run.
63	```
64	
65	**`--no-stubs` applies only to that invocation.** The helper still records the
66	configured languages. Running it again without this flag creates missing
67	stubs, and `add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for all configured languages
68	when adding a default-language page. There is no persistent on-demand mode yet.
69	Until one is added, preserve that distinction when adding English pages and
70	maintaining their nav/llmstxt entries; do not delete the locale from preferences
71	or claim a nonexistent flag to suppress future stubs.
72	
73	For a specifically requested translation of an existing page, the page helper's
74	`--lang zh-TW` creates only that sibling. Translate its body after consent, not
75	as an automatic consequence of enabling the locale.
76	
77	**A placeholder is not a missing translation.** An existing `*.zh-TW.md` with
78	"Translation pending" masks English fallback. `--no-stubs` leaves existing
79	files alone; review them individually and obtain approval before removing or
80	replacing anything. This selective policy does not override a project's rules
81	requiring complete bilingual coverage (such as this repo's published catalog).
82	
83	## Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement)
84	
85	This is the rule for any non-English page in a project that uses this skill:
86	
87	> **在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞首次出現時，以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現。**
88	> 例：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」、「型別檢查 (type checking)」。
89	> 後續同段內可只用中文。
90	>
91	> **不自創翻譯。** 若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
92	> `mkdocs-static-i18n`、`pymdownx.snippets`）。
93	>
94	> **代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。**
95	
96	The reason: Chinese-language tech writing has competing translations for
97	many terms (e.g. `cache` → 快取 / 緩存 / 暫存; `repository` → 倉庫 / 儲存庫 /
98	版本庫). Keeping the English original on first mention removes the ambiguity
99	without forcing readers to guess which translation the author meant. It also
100	keeps the page grep-able for English search terms.
101	
102	`add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh` inject this rule as an admonition
103	at the top of every non-default-language stub so authors see it before they
104	start translating.
105	
106	## What `add-language.sh` does, step by step
107	
108	For users who want to apply pieces by hand or audit what the script touched:
109	
110	1. **Locates `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD.
111	2. **Detects existing i18n state.** `yq` query against `.plugins[]` checks
112	   for an `i18n:` map.
113	3. **Inserts or extends `plugins.i18n`.**
114	   - If absent: prepends a fresh i18n block before `search`, with
115	     `[default-lang, new-lang]` as the language list.
116	   - If present and the new locale isn't there: appends to
117	     `plugins[].i18n.languages`.
118	   - If the locale is already present: no-op.
119	4. **Sets `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
120	   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` warns when `theme.language` is missing).
121	5. **Removes `navigation.instant` / `navigation.instant.progress`** from
122	   `theme.features` (the language switcher's contextual link can't be
123	   rewritten by instant navigation).
124	6. **Keeps default-language `mkdocs-llmstxt` output by default.** It adds the
125	   environment guards and managed `scripts/build-docs-site.py` required to
126	   isolate llmstxt from the multilingual build. Use `--remove-llmstxt` for an
127	   explicit opt-out. Legacy `--drop-strict` is a deprecated no-op;
128	   `--keep-llmstxt` is a deprecated alias for the default behavior.
129	7. **Walks `docs/`** for `*.md` files (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`),
130	   and for each non-locale-suffixed source page, creates a sibling
131	   `*.<LANG>.md` from `assets/translation-stub.md.template`.
132	8. **Updates `.skills/preferences.yaml`** with three keys:
133	   `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages` (ordered list, default first),
134	   `keep_english_terms: true`, `i18n_structure: suffix`.
135	9. **Un-comments `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2`** in `pyproject.toml`. If the
136	   line isn't there at all, prints a hint asking you to add it manually.
137	
138	The script is idempotent: re-running with the same `--lang` is a no-op. Exit
139	`11` means the locale/stubs were added and the safe migration subset was
140	applied, but custom downstream files still need the manual actions reported by
141	`migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh --json`.
142	
143	## `theme.language` vs plugin `languages`
144	
145	These are two different things:
146	
147	- [`theme.language`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/)
148	  is **Material's UI strings** (search placeholder, "Edit this page", footer
149	  navigation hints). One value site-wide. Material ships translations for
150	  ~70 locales out of the box.
151	- `plugins.i18n.languages` is **content translation**. A list. Each entry
152	  declares a locale that has translated `*.<lang>.md` files.
153	
154	You almost always want `theme.language` set to your default content language
155	so the UI matches when readers land on a default-language page.
156	
157	## `nav_translations`
158	
159	To translate section titles in the nav (e.g. `Workflows` → `工作流程`), use
160	`mkdocs-static-i18n`'s per-language `nav_translations`:
161	
162	```yaml
163	plugins:
164	  - i18n:
165	      docs_structure: suffix
166	      languages:
167	        - locale: en
168	          name: English
169	          default: true
170	        - locale: zh-TW
171	          name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
172	          nav_translations:
173	            Workflows: 工作流程
174	            Reference: 參考資料
175	```
176	
177	`add-language.sh` does **not** populate `nav_translations` for you —
178	section names are project-specific and translating them is a deliberate
179	authorial choice. Add them by hand once you have section titles to translate.
180	
181	!!! warning "Don't apply 「中文 (English original)」 to nav labels"
182	    The terminology rule that governs body prose **does not extend to
183	    `nav_translations` values.** Nav entries are navigation chrome — short
184	    labels in a sidebar — and bilingual labels like
185	    `Reference: 參考資料 (Reference)` are too long, wrap awkwardly, and
186	    duplicate information the URL slug already preserves.
187	
188	    For nav labels: pick the most common Chinese term for each section
189	    and stick with it. Stay consistent across the whole nav. The URL
190	    slug still uses the English source name (`/zh-TW/reference/...`),
191	    so search engines and direct-link sharing are unaffected.
192	
193	    Examples:
194	
195	    | English heading | Good zh-TW label | Bad zh-TW label |
196	    |---|---|---|
197	    | `Reference` | `參考資料` | `參考資料 (Reference)` |
198	    | `Workflows` | `工作流程` | `工作流程 (Workflows)` |
199	    | `Skills` | `Skills` (keep — domain term, no canonical translation) | `技能 (Skills)` |
200	    | `Getting started` | `快速開始` | `快速開始 (Getting started)` |
201	
202	    The "keep English" exception (third row) is reserved for terms where
203	    no canonical Chinese translation exists. When in doubt, keep English
204	    — it matches the body-prose rule's spirit (don't invent) without
205	    duplicating into the label.
206	
207	## Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`
208	
209	### Why one multilingual build is unsafe
210	
211	This is not merely a strict-mode compatibility warning, and
212	`reconfigure_material` is not the root cause:
213	
214	1. `mkdocs-static-i18n` performs a full MkDocs build for each locale.
215	2. `mkdocs-llmstxt` resets its collected page state for each build.
216	3. Every locale writes the same root `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` paths.
217	
218	The last locale therefore overwrites the valid default-language output. With
219	explicit `sections:` paths, translated source URIs no longer match and the
220	last files may contain only a heading. With globs, the files may look large but
221	contain the wrong locale. Strict mode exposes `Page URI ... not found`
222	warnings; a non-strict build silently ships the corrupted files. Removing
223	`--strict`, changing plugin order, toggling `reconfigure_material`, or using
224	globs does not solve the lifecycle collision.
225	
226	### Canonical two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build
227	
228	Run:
229	
230	```bash
231	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
232	```
233	
234	For a multilingual site with llmstxt enabled, the helper:
235	
236	1. Builds a temporary default-language-only source tree with i18n,
237	   copy-to-llm, and social disabled and llmstxt enabled.
238	2. Verifies `llms.txt`, the configured full output, every expected section,
239	   and generated `.md` sidecars.
240	3. Builds the full multilingual source tree with i18n/copy/social enabled and
241	   llmstxt disabled.
242	4. Merges the verified default-language LLM artifacts, rejects non-default
243	   locale paths, and only then replaces the final `site/` directory.
244	
245	Both [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es are strict. The helper has no non-strict escape hatch. A failed
246	[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] leaves the previous `site/` untouched; use `--keep-temp` only when you
247	need to inspect the staged trees.
248	
249	The corresponding `mkdocs.yml` guards are:
250	
251	```yaml
252	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
253	
254	plugins:
255	  - i18n:
256	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_I18N_ENABLED, true]
257	      # ...
258	  - llmstxt:
259	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
260	      # ...
261	  - copy-to-llm:
262	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
263	      # ...
264	  - social:
265	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
266	      # ... only when social cards were enabled
267	```
268	
269	The default `false` for llmstxt is deliberate: direct `mkdocs serve` and
270	`mkdocs build --strict` are HTML-only and cannot accidentally overwrite the
271	canonical LLM artifact. CI and deploy workflows must invoke the helper.
272	
273	### Output and copy-to-LLM contract
274	
275	- Root `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, and raw `.md` sidecars represent the
276	  **default language only**. This skill does not generate per-locale llms files.
277	- Keep Material's `content.action.edit` feature and a valid `repo_url` /
278	  `edit_uri`. The copy-to-LLM assets use the page's GitHub edit URL to derive
279	  the correct raw source, including a translated `*.zh-TW.md` sibling, instead
280	  of guessing from the locale site URL.
281	- `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button labels remain English-only on non-English pages.
282	  This is cosmetic and does not affect the source selected by the button.
283	
284	To opt out of LLM artifacts entirely:
285	
286	```bash
287	bash scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --remove-llmstxt
288	```
289	
290	Do not use `validation.links.not_found: info` or remove strict merely to make a
291	red build green. Fix source links and use a full deployed URL derived from
292	`site_url`, such as `https://owner.github.io/project/llms.txt`. A leading
293	`/llms.txt` is wrong for GitHub project Pages because it drops the repository
294	subpath.
295	
296	- **The translation-stub admonition is zh-TW-specific.** The terminology
297	  rule it injects is written for Traditional Chinese and uses the
298	  「中文 (English original)」 format. If you add `--lang ja` or another
299	  language, the admonition still says "Terminology rule (ja pages)" but the
300	  body is in Chinese. Either edit
301	  `assets/translation-stub.md.template` to be language-neutral first, or
302	  hand-edit the stubs after creation.
303	
304	## Removing a language
305	
306	To remove `zh-TW` later:
307	
308	1. Delete the `zh-TW` entry from `plugins[].i18n.languages` in `mkdocs.yml`.
309	2. (Optional) Delete every `*.zh-TW.md` file under `docs/`.
310	3. Update `.skills/preferences.yaml`:
311	   ```bash
312	   bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
313	     --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en"]'
314	   ```
315	4. If you only had two languages and want to fully remove the plugin, also
316	   delete the `i18n:` block and re-comment `mkdocs-static-i18n` in
317	   `pyproject.toml`.
318	
319	## Reset path
320	
321	If you want to fully back out of all the i18n decisions and start over:
322	
323	```bash
324	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
325	# Then manually revert mkdocs.yml / pyproject.toml as above, and
326	# re-run init-docs-site.sh or add-language.sh from scratch.
327	```
328	
329	The `--reset` clears the recorded decision; the agent will re-interview on
330	the next invocation.
331	
332	## Future work — `i18n_structure: folder`
333	
334	The `i18n_structure` preference key exists, but `add-language.sh` currently
335	only implements `suffix`. If we add `folder` later, the migration path will
336	be: walk `docs/`, move every default-language file into `docs/<default>/`,
337	move every `*.<lang>.md` into `docs/<lang>/<base>.md`, rewrite relative
338	links. Non-trivial — punted unless someone actually needs it.

1	# Skills management
2	
3	`dev agent skill manage` opens an independent wizard. REPOS and SKILLS offer the same
4	workflow through Ctrl+O; it does not add another dashboard tab.
5	
6	```bash
7	dev agent skill manage
8	dev agent skill manage --repo api
9	dev agent skill manage --all
10	dev agent skill list --all --check --json
11	```
12	
13	Choose project, global, project plus global, or multiple repositories. The
14	repository picker includes checkouts with `skills-lock.json`, even when installed
15	skill folders are missing or ignored by Git. Global skills are processed once.
16	Use Space to select, Ctrl+A to select/clear visible items, and type to filter.
17	
18	## Check and update
19	
20	Checking explicitly contacts Git sources, groups identical source/ref pairs,
21	and compares upstream content with the lock. It does not run `skills`, npm, Node
22	or project code. Dated results are cached in `skill-checks-v1.json`; changing the
23	lock invalidates them. `update_checked_at` in skill-list JSON identifies the last
24	comparison. A cached result is evidence from that time, not a live remote query.
25	
26	Update checks first, then preselects confirmed updates for review. Missing
27	installations, unsupported locks, failed checks and locally modified skill
28	contents are reported separately. The preview names each checkout, scope,
29	selected skill and command. Confirmation is required before execution.
30	
31	Native management mutations require a globally installed `skills` executable compatible
32	with the tested 1.5.23–1.5.25 contracts (supported 1.x versions from 1.5.23).
33	`dev self doctor` reports the dependency; install or upgrade it with
34	`npm install -g skills`. dev does not install dependencies automatically or fall
35	back to npx. Listing and checking continue to work when the dependency is absent.
36	
37	Commands run serially under dev's existing provider mutation lease. Lock,
38	installation and provider changes since preview reject the affected operation.
39	Results distinguish completed, failed, skipped, stale, canceled and unverified
40	items. A zero provider exit code alone is insufficient: dev rereads installations
41	and the resulting lock. Private JSON receipts live under
42	`<state_dir>/skills/runs/`. Raw Git and external installers remain outside dev's
43	coordination; native updates are not frozen artifact-transfer plans.
44	
45	## Single-project native operations
46	
47	The advanced choices appear for one project without global scope:
48	
49	| Choice | Native command | Behavior |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| Restore from lock | `skills experimental_install` | Re-resolves recorded sources/ref into `.agents/skills`; may update the lock. Useful when `.agents` is gitignored or absent. It does not guarantee the old content hash. |
52	| Sync dependency skills | `skills experimental_sync --yes --agent …` | Reads skills from existing `node_modules` and installs for explicitly selected project agents. It does not install npm dependencies. |
53	
54	The wizard checks native command support, project destination changes and local
55	content conflicts. Dependency skills with colliding names require individual
56	attention. Both operations retain native output and verify installed results;
57	neither is included in cross-repository batches in this version.
58	
59	`dev agent skill install` and `dev agent skill sync` still manage dev's bundled skill. The
60	existing single-skill `dev agent skill update <skill> --project|--global` command remains
61	available for automation. Explicit transfer preparation keeps its separate pinned
62	provider and verified-payload contract.
63	
64	
65	Provider source contracts: [update](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/v1.5.25/src/update.ts), [restore](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/v1.5.25/src/install.ts), [dependency sync](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/v1.5.25/src/sync.ts).
66	
67	## Bundled dev-cli skill lifecycle
68	
69	The bundled `dev-cli` skill follows the installed binary separately from skills
70	managed by the external `skills` provider:
71	
72	`dev --skill`, `dev agent skill print`, and the installed `SKILL.md` share one compact
73	entrypoint. It routes ordinary tasks to command `--help` and `dev help <topic>`;
74	the full reference tree remains bundled for advanced operations on demand.
75	Reading the installed skill does not require printing it again or loading every
76	reference. Use the checks below when investigating version or content drift.
77	
78	```bash
79	dev agent skill install                 # install or explicitly replace bundled files
80	dev agent skill install --check         # local content comparison; nonzero on drift/absence
81	dev agent skill install --if-installed  # refresh only an existing installation
82	dev agent skill uninstall --dry-run     # preview exact owned files and matching links
83	dev agent skill uninstall              # confirm and remove those files and links
84	```
85	
86	`dev self doctor` and `dev self upgrade --check` report whether the default installation
87	matches the running binary, without changing it. After a successful `dev self upgrade`,
88	the **new executable** refreshes an already installed
89	`~/.agents/skills/dev-cli`. Homebrew and Scoop use their stable installation paths;
90	other `dev` copies on PATH are not selected. An absent skill stays absent. A
91	normal upgrade also repairs an existing skill when the binary is already current.
92	Skill refresh failure is reported separately after the binary update succeeds.
93	
94	For standalone binaries, `dev self upgrade` uses the exact release's platform asset
95	when present and verifies `SHA256SUMS`. If the platform is absent, it offers a
96	native Go source build of that release tag (Termux also needs Clang). This fallback
97	is available since v0.2.35; older binaries need a one-time native source installation.
98	Source builds prefer the release's checksummed compact source archive, excluding
99	conversation history. Older releases use Go's configured module verification and
100	can require a larger download. Both use two workers and the installed toolchain,
101	and validate the candidate version before replacement.
102	Download/checksum failures never trigger compilation. `--check` never builds;
103	`--yes` accepts the displayed upgrade path. On Termux, prepare dependencies with

105	
106	Installation records content hashes in `.dev-cli-install.json`. Automatic refresh
107	refuses recorded local edits, restores missing files, and removes unchanged

113	
114	Uninstall previews and revalidates the recorded files plus agent symlinks still

120	
121	Custom `--dir` installations require `skill install --dir PATH` to refresh and
122	`skill uninstall --dir PATH` to remove. Direct package-manager upgrades and
123	upgrades initiated by binaries older than v0.2.23 do not run the new refresh hook;

2	# new-skill.sh — Scaffold a new agent skill in the npx-skills-compatible layout.
3	#
4	# Three placement scopes (auto-detected by default, override with --local /
5	# --project / --global):
6	#
7	#   LOCAL    Publishing-repo workflow (this very repo). Canonical content lives
8	#            under <repo>/skills/local/<name>/ (or skills/vendor/<name>/ with
9	#            --vendor), and discovery symlinks are added at
10	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name> and <repo>/.claude/skills/<name>
11	#            -> ../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>.
12	#
13	#   PROJECT  Generic per-project install. Canonical content at
14	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/ (universal agents like Cursor /
15	#            Codex / OpenCode / Warp pick this up directly), plus a relative
16	#            symlink at <repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>
17	#            (and other already-present non-universal agent dirs).
18	#
19	#   GLOBAL   System-wide install. Canonical content at ~/.agents/skills/<name>/
20	#            plus a relative symlink at ~/.claude/skills/<name> ->
21	#            ../../.agents/skills/<name> (and any other detected agent dir).
22	#
23	# Auto-detection precedence (when no scope flag given):
24	#   1. publishing repo (vendor.yaml, skills/local/, or
25	#      skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json found walking up) -> LOCAL
26	#   2. inside a git repo (.git found walking up)                 -> PROJECT
27	#   3. otherwise                                                 -> GLOBAL
28	#
29	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS — no mapfile, no ${var,,},
30	# no [[ -v var ]]).
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
35	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
36	ASSETS_DIR="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
37	
38	usage() {
39	  cat <<'EOF'
40	Usage: new-skill.sh [OPTIONS] <skill-name>
41	
42	Scaffold a new agent skill with the standard layout (SKILL.md, references/,
43	scripts/, assets/) seeded from skill-author's templates, then place it where
44	the active scope says it belongs and add discovery symlinks for non-universal
45	agents.
46	
47	Scope (mutually exclusive — auto-detected if omitted):
48	  --local            Force LOCAL mode (this publishing repo's skills/local/).
49	                     Requires a vendor.yaml / skills/local/ / skills/.claude-plugin
50	                     anchor walking up from --root or CWD.
51	  --project          Force PROJECT mode (<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/).
52	                     Requires a git repo root (.git) walking up.
53	  --global           Force GLOBAL mode (~/.agents/skills/<name>/).
54	
55	Other options:
56	  --vendor           In LOCAL mode, place under skills/vendor/<name>/ instead of
57	                     skills/local/. (Rare — vendored skills normally come via
58	                     vendor.yaml + scripts/sync-vendor.sh.)
59	  --root DIR         Override repo / project root discovery.
60	  --no-symlinks      Skip the agent-dir discovery symlinks (just write the
61	                     canonical dir). Useful for CI / packaging tests.
62	  --dry-run          Print what would be created without writing.
63	  --force            Overwrite if the target canonical directory already exists.
64	                     Existing symlinks are always replaced.
65	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
66	
67	Examples:
68	  bash new-skill.sh my-skill                # auto-detect scope
69	  bash new-skill.sh --project my-skill      # force project (.agents/skills)

2	
3	Standalone, stdlib-only Python (>=3.11) tool. Keep it dependency-free: target hosts are
4	often old (CentOS 7 via uv-managed Python), without root, with restricted egress.
5	
6	- Checks: `just check` (ruff + pytest). Tests that touch real clouds are marked

9	  variables are stripped (`egress.clean_env`). Never call `subprocess` directly.
10	- Never trust backend checksums; verify with our own sha256 and sizes.
11	- Every remote object must be non-empty (Baidu drops empty files).
12	- Never read, print or log backend credentials/session files.
13	- Ledger formats (`sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`) and the manifest are compatibility
14	  surfaces: bump `MANIFEST_VERSION` and handle old records when changing them.
15	- Record backend traps in `pitfalls/` (titled by symptom); future work in `TODO.md`.
16	- Do not commit or push without an explicit request.

3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills

7	## Layout

12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md

16	│       └── assets/

19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **Skills maintained in this repo go in `skills/local/`.** For a skill maintained
23	  alongside another first-party project, scaffold with `--project --root <project>`
24	  there and import its distribution copy into `skills/owned/` using the shared

29	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
30	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
31	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
32	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
33	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The

37	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
38	
39	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
40	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
41	precedence (when no flag given):
42	
43	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
44	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
45	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
46	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
47	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
48	   discovery symlinks for you.
49	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
50	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
51	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
52	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
53	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
54	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
55	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
56	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
57	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
58	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.

60	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root

65	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both

69	for the historical bug this convention prevents.

75	1. **First [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.

77	   useful.

79	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
80	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
81	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
82	
83	## Scripts naming and mirroring
84	
85	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
86	root. The pattern:
87	
88	| Canonical location | Mirror |
89	|---|---|
90	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
91	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
92	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
93	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |

98	
99	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
100	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
101	automated check for this — be careful.
102	
103	## Documentation
104	
105	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
106	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
107	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
108	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
109	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
110	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
111	
112	When you add a new local skill, also add:
113	
114	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
115	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
116	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
117	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
118	
119	## Project memory
120	
121	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
122	
123	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
124	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
125	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
126	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
127	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
128	
129	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
130	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
131	
132	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
133	
134	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
135	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
136	
137	## Bash compatibility
138	
139	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
140	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
141	escape hatches.
142	
143	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
144	
145	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
146	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
147	repo**. Notable specifics:
148	
149	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
150	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
151	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
152	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
153	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
154	  parsing-heavy helpers.
155	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
156	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
157	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
158

1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	If you are building documentation for a project that consumes one of the
4	skills in this repo (especially [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
5	or [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)),
6	this is the docs stack we recommend.
7	
8	It's the same stack this repo uses for its own docs, plus the optional
9	`mkdocstrings` layer for projects that have a Python API to document. Keep it
10	for existing plugin-dependent sites and English-first docs with optional
11	Traditional Chinese. For new single-language projects, evaluate Zensical in an
12	isolated pilot rather than silently changing engines; read
13	[the dated compatibility assessment](mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md) first.
14	
15	For selective translation, read
16	[the i18n guide](i18n-guide.md#english-first-with-selective-translations):
17	`add-language.sh --no-stubs` skips initial translation placeholders, but does
18	not persist an on-demand policy for future page-helper invocations.
19	
20	## TL;DR
21	
22	```toml
23	# pyproject.toml
24	[project.optional-dependencies]
25	docs = [
26	  "mkdocs>=1.6,<2",
27	  "mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10",
28	  # "mkdocs-material[imaging]>=9.5,<10",  # only with --social (cairosvg+pillow)
29	  "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.24",   # only if you have a Python API
30	  "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
31	  "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
32	  "pymdown-extensions>=10.0",
33	]
34	```
35	
36	```bash
37	# Local preview
38	uv sync --extra docs
39	uv run mkdocs serve
40	
41	# Build static site
42	uv run python scripts/build-docs-site.py
43	
44	# Safe HTML-only preview (llmstxt stays disabled)
45	uv run mkdocs build --strict
46	```
47	
48	## Why this stack
49	
50	- **MkDocs + Material** — Markdown-first authoring, built-in search, a
51	  theme that doesn't need overrides for ~90% of projects, GitHub Pages
52	  deploy is one workflow file.
53	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — render API docs from Python docstrings via
54	  `::: package.module.symbol` directives in your Markdown. Only relevant
55	  if your project has a Python API; skip it otherwise.
56	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt`** — generates `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` so
57	  AI agents can discover and consume your docs without scraping HTML.
58	  Upstream is in maintenance mode and must be isolated from a multilingual
59	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` build; the managed helper does that. If it stops working
60	  even in the default-language [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], replace it with a post-build generator.
61	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`** — adds "Copy to LLM / Open in ChatGPT / Open
62	  in Claude" buttons on every page. Pure UX sugar; harmless if your
63	  audience doesn't use it.
64	- **Managed strict build helper** — keeps `mkdocs-static-i18n` and
65	  `mkdocs-llmstxt` out of the same plugin lifecycle. Multilingual HTML is built
66	  separately from default-language LLM artifacts, validated, and merged before
67	  `site/` is replaced.
68	
69	## Why not these?
70	
71	- **Sphinx + Furo + MyST + autodoc.** Strictly more powerful, but the
72	  setup and maintenance cost is meaningful. Recommended only if AI-facing
73	  Markdown output becomes a first-class requirement, or if your project
74	  has the kind of cross-project reference graph Sphinx is built for.
75	- **pdoc.** Single-file API doc generator. Great for "I just want HTML
76	  for my package", but no good story for guides, conventions pages, or
77	  llms.txt.
78	- **Rspress.** Best-in-class for AI-native output, but it's
79	  Node-first / frontend-product-docs-first; Python API reference is a
80	  bolt-on. Not a fit unless you're already on the Node ecosystem.
81	- **Quarto.** Excellent for notebook / tutorial / research-report
82	  workflows; not optimized for Python library documentation.
83	
84	The longer version of this analysis (with the upstream-vs-inference
85	distinction made explicit) is preserved in the reference repo
86	[`mlflow-widgets/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets/blob/main/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md).
87	
88	## Minimum `mkdocs.yml`
89	
90	```yaml
91	site_name: Your Project
92	site_description: One sentence about your project.
93	site_url: https://yourname.github.io/your-project/
94	repo_url: https://github.com/yourname/your-project
95	edit_uri: edit/main/docs/
96	docs_dir: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
97	
98	theme:
99	  name: material
100	  features:
101	    - navigation.instant
102	    - navigation.sections
103	    - navigation.indexes
104	    - search.suggest
105	    - content.code.copy
106	    - content.action.edit
107	    - toc.follow
108	
109	plugins:
110	  - search
111	  # Optional (opt-in via `init-docs-site.sh --social`): OG/Twitter preview
112	  # cards. Needs system cairo/pango + mkdocs-material[imaging]. Omit for a
113	  # dependency-free build.
114	  # - social:
115	  #     enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_SOCIAL_ENABLED, true]
116	  #     cards_layout_options:
117	  #       background_color: "#3f51b5"
118	  #       # font_family: Noto Sans TC   # set a CJK font if titles are CJK
119	  - mkdocstrings:        # remove this block if no Python API
120	      handlers:
121	        python:
122	          paths: [src]
123	          options:
124	            show_source: true
125	            show_root_heading: true
126	            members_order: source
127	            docstring_style: google
128	            merge_init_into_class: true
129	  - llmstxt:
130	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_LLMSTXT_ENABLED, false]
131	      full_output: llms-full.txt
132	      sections:
133	        Guides: [index.md, getting-started.md]
134	        API Reference: [reference/*.md]
135	  - copy-to-llm:
136	      enabled: !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_COPY_TO_LLM_ENABLED, true]
137	      repo_url: "https://yourname.github.io/your-project"
138	
139	markdown_extensions:
140	  - admonition
141	  - tables
142	  - toc:
143	      permalink: true
144	  - pymdownx.superfences
145	  - pymdownx.highlight
146	  - pymdownx.snippets:
147	      base_path:
148	        - .
149	        - !ENV [MKDOCS_SITE_BOOTSTRAP_DOCS_DIR, docs]
150	      check_paths: true
151	
152	nav:
153	  - Home: index.md
154	  - Getting Started: getting-started.md
155	  - API Reference:
156	      - Overview: reference/index.md
157	```
158	
159	## GitHub Pages workflow
160	
161	`.github/workflows/docs.yml`:
162	
163	```yaml
164	name: Docs
165	
166	on:
167	  push:
168	    branches: [main]
169	    paths:
170	      - 'docs/**'
171	      - 'mkdocs.yml'
172	      - 'pyproject.toml'
173	      - 'scripts/build-docs-site.py'
174	      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
175	  workflow_dispatch:
176	
177	permissions:
178	  contents: read
179	  pages: write
180	  id-token: write
````

1	# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`
2	
3	Last verified: **2026-10-30** against upstream documentation and release notes.
4	This replaces the April 2026 assessment. Upstream support below is not a claim
5	that this skill's sites have been built or migrated with Zensical.
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	- **Keep this skill and existing MkDocs sites.** Preserve `mkdocs>=1.6,<2`,
10	  `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`, the lockfile, and the managed build helper.
11	- **English-first with optional Traditional Chinese is content i18n**, not
12	  just a translated interface. Continue using MkDocs for that workflow until
13	  a successor [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es the same output checks.
14	- **Zensical is a viable candidate for a scoped single-language pilot**, not
15	  an automatic default for every new project. Its `0.x` version alone is
16	  neither a reason to reject it nor evidence of production readiness.
17	- **Material maintenance ends on 2027-05-05** for security and critical fixes,
18	  per its [changelog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/changelog/).
19	  Staying on MkDocs is a time-bounded decision, not a promise of years of support.
20	- A future `zensical-site-bootstrap` should be a **separate skill**. Updating
21	  this skill must not silently change downstream projects' build engine.
22	
23	## What changes in MkDocs 2.0
24	
25	The [MkDocs announcement](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077)
26	links to [version 2 pre-release documentation](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/).
27	The Material team's [analysis, updated in October 2026](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/),
28	reports removal of the MkDocs 1.x plugin system, a rewritten theme interface,
29	and TOML configuration. It states that Material is incompatible and that no
30	release date has been announced. Treat these as pre-release design statements,
31	not a guarantee that the final design cannot change.
32	
33	`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, and `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` depend on the
34	MkDocs plugin lifecycle. **PyMdown's snippets, superfences, and tabs are Python
35	Markdown extensions, not MkDocs plugins**; assess Markdown compatibility
36	separately rather than claiming every extension has the same failure mode.
37	
38	Do not upgrade this Material-based stack to MkDocs 2.0 without a separately
39	validated migration. There is no need to adopt a different hosting provider:
40	GitHub Actions can build the static output before GitHub Pages serves it.
41	
42	## What Zensical supports now
43	
44	The latest release at verification was
45	[0.0.73 (2026-10-26)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.73).
46	[0.0.67 (2026-09-30)](https://github.com/zensical/zensical/releases/tag/v0.0.67)
47	added native `llmstxt` and a Copy as Markdown button. The old assessment that
48	there was no published support for these functions is obsolete.
49	
50	The [plugin compatibility table](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/plugins/)
51	is the authority for individual settings, not the presence of a plugin name in
52	`mkdocs.yml`:
53	
54	| Requirement | Upstream status and limits |
55	|---|---|
56	| Existing `mkdocs.yml` / Material look | Supported migration path; `theme.variant: classic` preserves the familiar appearance. Custom template overrides may need changes. |
57	| Search / Python API reference | Native search and `mkdocstrings` integration are documented. Install the required handler; audit companion plugins separately. |
58	| `llms.txt`, full output, Markdown counterparts | Native `llmstxt` since 0.0.67. Validate sections, exported content, and project Pages subpaths. Custom Python `preprocess` is ignored. |
59	| Copy as Markdown | `content.action.copy` works for pages with Markdown counterparts. This is not proof of parity with every `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button or custom asset. |
60	| UI language / alternate-language links | Documented, but not proof of suffix content translation, fallback, contextual switching, translated nav, or per-language search. |
61	| Arbitrary MkDocs plugins / hooks | No MkDocs plugin API; arbitrary plugins cannot run. The migration guide lists `hooks` as unsupported. |
62	| `gen-files` | Not supported directly; external generation is a separate workflow to evaluate. |
63	
64	**Unsupported plugin configuration can be silently ignored.** A successful
65	build is insufficient: inspect the artifacts and user-visible behavior.
66	Likewise, supported plugins may have ignored settings. Check every setting
67	used by the target site, not just the package list.
68	
69	The [migration guide](https://zensical.org/docs/compatibility/mkdocs/migration/)
70	does not require conversion to `zensical.toml` just to test an existing config.
71	It also documents CLI and template differences; replacing `mkdocs` with
72	`zensical` in the managed helper is not a migration strategy.
73	
74	Do not treat an unverified future release date as an adoption gate. In
75	particular, the roadmap's November 5 Studio banner is not evidence for a
76	November 5, 2026 release of the SSG as version 0.1.0.
77	
78	## English-first with optional Traditional Chinese
79	
80	Distinguish three layers:
81	
82	1. **UI localization** translates search labels and navigation controls.
83	2. **A language selector** links to language-specific destinations; it does
84	   not generate translated documents.
85	3. **Content i18n** maps corresponding articles, handles missing translations,
86	   and builds appropriate navigation and search for each locale.
87	
88	For this workflow, English is the complete default source for readers and
89	agents. Add `*.zh-TW.md` only for articles the user wants in Traditional Chinese;
90	missing translations should fall back to English. Root `llms.txt`,
91	`llms-full.txt`, and Markdown sidecars remain default-language-only. Enabling
92	a locale never authorizes automatic translation.
93	
94	MkDocs' `fallback_to_default: true` supports missing siblings, but an existing
95	"Translation pending" stub counts as a translation and masks the fallback.
96	**`add-language.sh --no-stubs` already enables a locale without generating
97	siblings.** That flag is per-invocation, not a persistent preference:
98	`add-docs-page.sh` still creates stubs for configured non-default languages.
99	Read [the i18n guide](i18n-guide.md#english-first-with-selective-translations)
100	before choosing this workflow; do not invent a persistent on-demand flag.
101	
102	Zensical's [language settings](https://zensical.org/docs/setup/language/)
103	document UI localization and alternate links. The [roadmap](https://zensical.org/roadmap/)
104	still lists broader content-i18n work. Neither establishes parity with this
105	skill's suffix/fallback workflow. Do not replace it with a hand-built multi-site
106	pipeline merely to claim that language switching exists.
107	
108	## Keep the caps; validate migrations separately
109	
110	Material 9.7.5+ also constrains MkDocs below 2. A resolver intersects that
111	constraint with the project's direct requirements; the direct MkDocs dependency
112	is **not** resolved independently. Explicit bounds still document this skill's
113	own support contract and remain protective if upstream metadata changes.
114	
115	Keep bounds consistent in the dependency template, optional social extra,
116	manual recipe, and initializer's existing-`pyproject.toml` hints. Commit a
117	lockfile in consuming projects and use controlled patch/minor updates with
118	regression tests. Bounds permit those updates; they do not refresh a lockfile
119	or supply security fixes automatically.
120	
121	**Migrating to Zensical does not mean lifting the MkDocs cap.** Change the
122	builder and dependencies deliberately for each approved migration; retain the
123	caps wherever the MkDocs/Material stack remains in use.
124	
125	## Re-evaluation and adoption gates
126	
127	Review again by **January 2027**, ahead of Material's maintenance deadline,
128	or sooner after relevant security advisories or new content-i18n support.
129	This is a review recommendation, not an automatically scheduled task.
130	
131	Before a pilot becomes a default or an existing site is migrated:
132	
133	1. Inventory plugins, hooks, extensions, templates, and build-time generators.
134	   Record unsupported or unknown settings instead of accepting silent omission.
135	2. Build an isolated, version-locked fixture. Compare navigation, search,
136	   code blocks/snippets, images, anchors, and project Pages subpath links.
137	3. Verify `llms.txt` sections, full content, Markdown counterparts, and the
138	   actual Copy as Markdown behavior, not just file existence or exit status.
139	4. For content-i18n sites, verify English defaults, selected zh-TW counterparts,
140	   missing-translation fallback, same-page switching, locale navigation/search,
141	   correct source links, and default-language-only LLM artifacts.
142	5. Preserve sources and the last successful output on failure. Document rollback
143	   and get consent before switching an existing project or deploying anything.
144	
145	A single-language pilot can validate steps 1–3 without solving i18n, but that
146	result does **not** make it the default for English-first bilingual projects.
147	Keep this skill's two-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] build and repair tools until an equivalent migration
148	has [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed all applicable gates; do not copy that MkDocs-specific machinery into
149	a new Zensical skill.
150
