````text
1	# ferry
2	
3	Resumable bulk transfer between hosts that cannot reach each other, relayed through cloud
4	storage (Baidu Pan, any rclone remote, a GitHub draft release, or a shared directory) — or
5	directly over ssh with rsync when the hosts can reach each other.
6	
7	```
8	source host                         relay                          destination host
9	ferry send  ── pack ─▶ stage ─ push ─▶  prefix/<key>/part-*   ─ pull ─▶ verify ─▶ dest
10	                                         prefix/<key>/manifest.json  (READY, uploaded last)
11	```
12	
13	- **Units**: one key = one tar (or one raw file) = one remote directory. Resume is per unit
14	  and per part; nothing is re-uploaded after a restart.
15	- **Integrity**: sha256 is computed while packing (single source read). The receiver checks
16	  every part, the reassembled payload and the tar member count. Backend checksums (e.g.
17	  Baidu MD5) are never trusted.
18	- **Backpressure**: staging cap on the sender, remote free-space floor and in-flight limit,
19	  so a small relay can move a much larger dataset.
20	- **Read windows**: packing (the heavy source read) can be blocked in given hours, e.g.
21	  `"Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"`; uploads continue from staging.
22	- **Direct egress by default**: proxy variables are stripped from every backend process,
23	  backend-internal proxy settings are rejected, and endpoints resolving to clash/mihomo
24	  fake-ip or routed via a tun interface fail the preflight. See *Egress* below.
25	- **Source deletion policy**: `never`, `after_remote_size` (as soon as the relay holds a
26	  byte-identical-size copy; for regenerable data) or `after_receiver_ack` (after the
27	  destination verified sha256).
28	
29	## Install
30	
31	```bash
32	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry   # CLI on PATH
33	# or as a dependency:  ferry @ git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry@v0.1.0
34	```
35	
36	Python ≥ 3.11, no runtime dependencies. Backend CLIs are used as installed:
37	[BaiduPCS-Go](https://github.com/qjfoidnh/BaiduPCS-Go), `rclone`, `gh`.
38	
39	## Job file
40	
41	```toml
42	name = "daily-archive"                        # also the default state dir name
43	# state_dir = "~/.local/state/ferry/<name>"   # ledgers, logs, lock
44	
45	[units]
46	root = "/data/shared/dataset"
47	keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"               # key = file stem / dir name
48	members = ["order/{key}", "trans/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]
49	# or: glob = "exports/*.parquet"  (each match is a unit); pack = "none" sends files as-is
50	settle = "6h"                                 # skip units with files newer than this
51	resend_changed = true                         # re-send units whose fingerprint changed
52	recheck_recent = 30                           # after the first [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], recheck newest 30 keys
53	
54	[sender]
55	stage_dir = "~/.cache/ferry/daily-archive"
56	stage_cap = "300GB"
57	read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]
58	delete_source = "after_remote_size"           # never | after_remote_size | after_receiver_ack
59	
60	[receiver]
61	dest = "/srv/archive/dataset/{key[0:4]}"      # {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}
62	# extract = true                              # unpack; each unit path is replaced whole
63	# min_free = "20GB"                           # wait while the destination is this full
64	
65	[remote]
66	adapter = "baidupcs"                          # local | baidupcs | rclone | ghrelease
67	prefix = "/ferry/daily-archive"
68	part_size = "3900MiB"                         # default per adapter
69	min_free = "200GB"
70	max_inflight = "1.5TB"
71	egress = "direct"                             # direct | any
72	# trusted_interfaces = ["Meta"]               # TUN you verified routes this backend DIRECT
73	options = { download_threads = 4 }
74	```
75	
76	Adapter options:
77	
78	| adapter | options |
79	|---|---|
80	| `local` | `root` (directory used as relay) |
81	| `baidupcs` | `binary` (default: PATH or `~/.local/bin/BaiduPCS-Go`), `upload_threads`, `download_threads` (4) |
82	| `rclone` | `remote` (`"gdrive:"`, `"s3:bucket/relay"`), `flags`, `endpoints` (route check hosts) |
83	| `ghrelease` | `repo` (`owner/name`), `tag` (draft release, created if missing; refuses a published release) |
84	| `rsync` | `host` (ssh alias; `""` = local), `root` (landing dir on that host), `ssh_options`, `flags` |
85	
86	`[remote.sides.sender]` / `[remote.sides.receiver]` override `adapter` and `options` for one
87	side. Direct mode uses this: the sender pushes with `rsync` into a landing directory on the
88	destination host, and the receiver there reads the same directory with `local`:
89	
90	```toml
91	[remote]
92	adapter = "rsync"
93	prefix = "/inbox"
94	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
95	[remote.sides.receiver]
96	adapter = "local"
97	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
98	```
99	
100	Compared with plain `rsync -a`, this adds read windows, many-small-files packing, sha256
101	verification of every unit, source-deletion policies, ledgers with throughput/ETA, and
102	change detection for long-running mirrors.
103	
104	## Backfill and increments are the same job
105	
106	A job with `delete_source = "never"` mirrors a growing, occasionally repaired source:
107	
108	- **First run = backfill**: every unit not yet sent is packed and sent.
109	- **`--follow` = increments**: new keys are picked up; units still being written are held
110	  back by `settle`.
111	- **Repairs**: each unit has a fingerprint (sorted relative paths + sizes; stat only). A
112	  changed unit is re-sent as a new revision; with `extract = true` the receiver replaces
113	  each unit path wholesale, so files deleted at the source disappear too. After the first
114	  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] only the newest `recheck_recent` keys are re-fingerprinted each round; restart the
115	  sender (or run without `--follow`) for a full recheck.
116	- **Seeding**: if the destination already holds part of the data, run
117	  `ferry inventory job.toml` on the receiver. It publishes fingerprints of what it has;
118	  the sender marks identical units as `seeded` instead of sending them.
119	
120	## Commands
121	
122	```bash
123	ferry doctor job.toml [--side receiver]   # backend login, proxy settings, routes
124	ferry plan job.toml                       # units found under the source root
125	ferry send job.toml [--follow]            # until every unit is pushed (then marks done)
126	ferry receive job.toml [--once|--follow]  # until the sender is done and the relay is empty
127	ferry inventory job.toml [--root PATH]     # receiver: publish fingerprints for seeding
128	ferry status job.toml [--side receiver] [--scan-source] [--remote] [--json]
129	```
130	
131	A second sender (or receiver) for the same job on the same host exits immediately.
132	
133	### Running unattended
134	
135	ferry has no daemon of its own: `send`/`receive --follow` is a long-running loop that
136	polls for new or changed units. Put it under a supervisor; `ferry service` prints (or,
137	with `--install`, writes and enables) one:
138	
139	```bash
140	ferry service job.toml --side receiver                 # print a systemd user unit
141	ferry service job.toml --side receiver --install       # ~/.config/systemd/user/ferry-<job>-receiver.service
142	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
143	ferry service job.toml --side sender --uninstall
144	loginctl enable-linger $USER                           # let user services run without a login
145	```
146	
147	systemd units run `--follow` with `Restart=on-failure`; cron entries run one-shot
148	(`send`, `receive --once`) and rely on the job lock to skip overlapping runs. Any other
149	supervisor (pueue, tmux, launchd) works the same way: run the printed command.
150	
151	Library use (e.g. from an orchestrator):
152	
153	```python
154	import ferry
155	job = ferry.load_job("job.toml")
156	report = ferry.preflight(job, ferry.adapter_for(job, "sender"))
157	result = ferry.send(job)            # SendResult(pushed=..., pushed_bytes=..., ...)
158	st = ferry.side_status(job, "sender", remote=True)
159	```
160	
161	## Egress
162	
163	Proxy traffic is metered, so by default ferry insists on a direct path:
164	
165	1. `http(s)_proxy`, `all_proxy`, ... are removed from every backend process environment.
166	2. Backend tools' own proxy settings (BaiduPCS-Go `proxy`) are reported.
167	3. Each backend endpoint is resolved; a `198.18.0.0/15` answer (clash/mihomo fake-ip DNS)
168	   or a route via `tun*`/`utun*`/`Meta`/`wg*`/`tailscale*` is reported.
169	
170	With `egress = "direct"` any finding fails `send`/`receive`; `egress = "any"` (or
171	`--allow-proxy` for one run) accepts them with warnings — for backends that are only
172	reachable through a proxy, e.g. Google Drive from mainland China, where the proxy's own
173	rules may still pick DIRECT for some hosts. A transparent proxy on the router is not
174	visible from the host and cannot be detected.
175	
176	## Backend notes
177	
178	See [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — e.g. Baidu silently drops empty files and exits 0 on
179	errors, single-threaded Baidu downloads are ~4x slower, GitHub assets are limited to 2 GiB.
180
````
</details></tool-use>

3	Standalone, stdlib-only Python (>=3.11) tool. Keep it dependency-free: target hosts are

6	- Checks: `just check` (ruff + pytest). Tests that touch real clouds are marked
7	  `network` and skipped by default (`uv run pytest -m network`).
8	- Every backend command must go through `ferry.proc.run`/`run_transfer` so proxy
9	  variables are stripped (`egress.clean_env`). Never call `subprocess` directly.
10	- Never trust backend checksums; verify with our own sha256 and sizes.
11	- Every remote object must be non-empty (Baidu drops empty files).
12	- Never read, print or log backend credentials/session files.
13	- Ledger formats (`sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`) and the manifest are compatibility

````text
1	# ferry
2	
3	Resumable bulk transfer between hosts that cannot reach each other, relayed through cloud
4	storage (Baidu Pan, any rclone remote, a GitHub draft release, or a shared directory) — or
5	directly over ssh with rsync when the hosts can reach each other.
6	
7	```
8	source host                         relay                          destination host
9	ferry send  ── pack ─▶ stage ─ push ─▶  prefix/<key>/part-*   ─ pull ─▶ verify ─▶ dest
10	                                         prefix/<key>/manifest.json  (READY, uploaded last)
11	```
12	
13	- **Units**: one key = one tar (or one raw file) = one remote directory. Resume is per unit
14	  and per part; nothing is re-uploaded after a restart.
15	- **Integrity**: sha256 is computed while packing (single source read). The receiver checks
16	  every part, the reassembled payload and the tar member count. Backend checksums (e.g.
17	  Baidu MD5) are never trusted.
18	- **Backpressure**: staging cap on the sender, remote free-space floor and in-flight limit,
19	  so a small relay can move a much larger dataset.
20	- **Read windows**: packing (the heavy source read) can be blocked in given hours, e.g.
21	  `"Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"`; uploads continue from staging.
22	- **Direct egress by default**: proxy variables are stripped from every backend process,
23	  backend-internal proxy settings are rejected, and endpoints resolving to clash/mihomo
24	  fake-ip or routed via a tun interface fail the preflight. See *Egress* below.
25	- **Source deletion policy**: `never`, `after_remote_size` (as soon as the relay holds a
26	  byte-identical-size copy; for regenerable data) or `after_receiver_ack` (after the
27	  destination verified sha256).
28	
29	## Install
30	
31	```bash
32	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry   # CLI on PATH
33	# or as a dependency:  ferry @ git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry@v0.1.0
34	```
35	
36	Python ≥ 3.11, no runtime dependencies. Backend CLIs are used as installed:
37	[BaiduPCS-Go](https://github.com/qjfoidnh/BaiduPCS-Go), `rclone`, `gh`.
38	
39	## Job file
40	
41	```toml
42	name = "daily-archive"                        # also the default state dir name
43	# state_dir = "~/.local/state/ferry/<name>"   # ledgers, logs, lock
44	
45	[units]
46	root = "/data/shared/dataset"
47	keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"               # key = file stem / dir name
48	members = ["order/{key}", "trans/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]
49	# or: glob = "exports/*.parquet"  (each match is a unit); pack = "none" sends files as-is
50	settle = "6h"                                 # skip units with files newer than this
51	resend_changed = true                         # re-send units whose fingerprint changed
52	recheck_recent = 30                           # after the first [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], recheck newest 30 keys
53	
54	[sender]
55	stage_dir = "~/.cache/ferry/daily-archive"
56	stage_cap = "300GB"
57	read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]
58	delete_source = "after_remote_size"           # never | after_remote_size | after_receiver_ack
59	
60	[receiver]
61	dest = "/srv/archive/dataset/{key[0:4]}"      # {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}
62	# extract = true                              # unpack; each unit path is replaced whole
63	# min_free = "20GB"                           # wait while the destination is this full
64	
65	[remote]
66	adapter = "baidupcs"                          # local | baidupcs | rclone | ghrelease
67	prefix = "/ferry/daily-archive"
68	part_size = "3900MiB"                         # default per adapter
69	min_free = "200GB"
70	max_inflight = "1.5TB"
71	egress = "direct"                             # direct | any
72	# trusted_interfaces = ["Meta"]               # TUN you verified routes this backend DIRECT
73	options = { download_threads = 4 }
74	```
75	
76	Adapter options:
77	
78	| adapter | options |
79	|---|---|
80	| `local` | `root` (directory used as relay) |
81	| `baidupcs` | `binary` (default: PATH or `~/.local/bin/BaiduPCS-Go`), `upload_threads`, `download_threads` (4) |
82	| `rclone` | `remote` (`"gdrive:"`, `"s3:bucket/relay"`), `flags`, `endpoints` (route check hosts) |
83	| `ghrelease` | `repo` (`owner/name`), `tag` (draft release, created if missing; refuses a published release) |
84	| `rsync` | `host` (ssh alias; `""` = local), `root` (landing dir on that host), `ssh_options`, `flags` |
85	
86	`[remote.sides.sender]` / `[remote.sides.receiver]` override `adapter` and `options` for one
87	side. Direct mode uses this: the sender pushes with `rsync` into a landing directory on the
88	destination host, and the receiver there reads the same directory with `local`:
89	
90	```toml
91	[remote]
92	adapter = "rsync"
93	prefix = "/inbox"
94	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
95	[remote.sides.receiver]
96	adapter = "local"
97	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
98	```
99	
100	Compared with plain `rsync -a`, this adds read windows, many-small-files packing, sha256
101	verification of every unit, source-deletion policies, ledgers with throughput/ETA, and
102	change detection for long-running mirrors.
103	
104	## Backfill and increments are the same job
105	
106	A job with `delete_source = "never"` mirrors a growing, occasionally repaired source:
107	
108	- **First run = backfill**: every unit not yet sent is packed and sent.
109	- **`--follow` = increments**: new keys are picked up; units still being written are held
110	  back by `settle`.
111	- **Repairs**: each unit has a fingerprint (sorted relative paths + sizes; stat only). A
112	  changed unit is re-sent as a new revision; with `extract = true` the receiver replaces
113	  each unit path wholesale, so files deleted at the source disappear too. After the first
114	  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] only the newest `recheck_recent` keys are re-fingerprinted each round; restart the
115	  sender (or run without `--follow`) for a full recheck.
116	- **Seeding**: if the destination already holds part of the data, run
117	  `ferry inventory job.toml` on the receiver. It publishes fingerprints of what it has;
118	  the sender marks identical units as `seeded` instead of sending them.
119	
120	## Commands
121	
122	```bash
123	ferry doctor job.toml [--side receiver]   # backend login, proxy settings, routes
124	ferry plan job.toml                       # units found under the source root
125	ferry send job.toml [--follow]            # until every unit is pushed (then marks done)
126	ferry receive job.toml [--once|--follow]  # until the sender is done and the relay is empty
127	ferry inventory job.toml [--root PATH]     # receiver: publish fingerprints for seeding
128	ferry status job.toml [--side receiver] [--scan-source] [--remote] [--json]
129	```
130	
131	A second sender (or receiver) for the same job on the same host exits immediately.
132	
133	### Running unattended
134	
135	ferry has no daemon of its own: `send`/`receive --follow` is a long-running loop that
136	polls for new or changed units. Put it under a supervisor; `ferry service` prints (or,
137	with `--install`, writes and enables) one:
138	
139	```bash
140	ferry service job.toml --side receiver                 # print a systemd user unit
141	ferry service job.toml --side receiver --install       # ~/.config/systemd/user/ferry-<job>-receiver.service
142	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
143	ferry service job.toml --side sender --uninstall
144	loginctl enable-linger $USER                           # let user services run without a login
145	```
146	
147	systemd units run `--follow` with `Restart=on-failure`; cron entries run one-shot
148	(`send`, `receive --once`) and rely on the job lock to skip overlapping runs. Any other
149	supervisor (pueue, tmux, launchd) works the same way: run the printed command.
150	
151	Library use (e.g. from an orchestrator):
152	
153	```python
154	import ferry
155	job = ferry.load_job("job.toml")
156	report = ferry.preflight(job, ferry.adapter_for(job, "sender"))
157	result = ferry.send(job)            # SendResult(pushed=..., pushed_bytes=..., ...)
158	st = ferry.side_status(job, "sender", remote=True)
159	```
160	
161	## Egress
162	
163	Proxy traffic is metered, so by default ferry insists on a direct path:
164	
165	1. `http(s)_proxy`, `all_proxy`, ... are removed from every backend process environment.
166	2. Backend tools' own proxy settings (BaiduPCS-Go `proxy`) are reported.
167	3. Each backend endpoint is resolved; a `198.18.0.0/15` answer (clash/mihomo fake-ip DNS)
168	   or a route via `tun*`/`utun*`/`Meta`/`wg*`/`tailscale*` is reported.
169	
170	With `egress = "direct"` any finding fails `send`/`receive`; `egress = "any"` (or
171	`--allow-proxy` for one run) accepts them with warnings — for backends that are only
172	reachable through a proxy, e.g. Google Drive from mainland China, where the proxy's own
173	rules may still pick DIRECT for some hosts. A transparent proxy on the router is not
174	visible from the host and cannot be detected.
175	
176	## Backend notes
177	
178	See [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — e.g. Baidu silently drops empty files and exits 0 on
179	errors, single-threaded Baidu downloads are ~4x slower, GitHub assets are limited to 2 GiB.
180
````
</details></tool-use>

64	def _print(args, data: dict, text: str) -> None:

68	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
69	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
70	    try:

74	            lines = [f"adapter: {report.adapter}  egress policy: {report.egress_policy}"]
75	            lines += [f"  route {r['host']} -> {r['address']} via {r['interface']}"
76	                      + (f"  !! {r['problem']}" if r["problem"] else "") for r in report.routes]
77	            lines += [f"  problem: {x}" for x in report.problems]
78	            shown = {f"{r['host']}: {r['problem']}" for r in report.routes if r["problem"]}
79	            lines += [f"  egress: {x}" for x in report.egress_findings if x not in shown]
80	            if report.proxy_env_stripped:
81	                lines.append("  proxy env (removed for child processes): "
82	                             + ", ".join(report.proxy_env_stripped))
83	            lines.append("OK" if report.ok else "NOT OK")
84	            _print(args, report.to_dict(), "\n".join(lines))
85	            return 0 if report.ok else 2
86	        if args.command == "plan":
87	            units = enumerate_units(job.units)
88	            data = {"units": [{"key": u.key, "members": list(u.members)} for u in units]}
89	            _print(args, data, "\n".join(f"{u.key}  {len(u.members)} member(s)" for u in units)
90	                   + f"\n{len(units)} units")
91	            return 0
92	        if args.command == "inventory":
93	            from .inventory import build_inventory, publish_inventory
94	            inv = build_inventory(job, args.root)
95	            if not args.no_upload:
96	                publish_inventory(job, inv)
97	            _print(args, inv if args.json else {}, f"{len(inv['keys'])} units fingerprinted "
98	                   f"under {inv['root']}" + ("" if args.no_upload else "; published to relay"))
99	            return 0

103	                (svc.uninstall_systemd if args.kind == "systemd" else svc.uninstall_cron)(
104	                    job, args.side)
105	                print(f"removed {args.kind} entry for {job.name}/{args.side}")
106	                return 0
107	            if args.kind == "systemd":
108	                if args.install:

110	                    print(f"installed and started {path}")

130	            _print(args, st.to_dict(), text)

1	"""Job specification (TOML) and unit enumeration.
2	
3	A *unit* is the smallest resumable piece of work: one key, one tar (or one raw file),
4	one remote directory. Units are enumerated either from ``keys_from`` + ``members``
5	templates (several paths per key, e.g. one trading day across kinds) or from ``glob``
6	(each match is its own unit).
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import os
11	import re
12	import tomllib
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	from .sizes import parse_size
17	from .windows import Window
18	
19	DELETE_POLICIES = ("never", "after_remote_size", "after_receiver_ack")
20	EGRESS_POLICIES = ("direct", "any")
21	_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}")
22	
23	
24	class JobError(ValueError):
25	    [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
26	
27	
28	@dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class Unit:
30	    key: str
31	    root: Path
32	    members: tuple[str, ...]  # paths relative to root that exist
33	
34	
35	@dataclass(frozen=True)
36	class UnitsSpec:
37	    root: Path
38	    keys_from: str | None = None
39	    members: tuple[str, ...] = ()
40	    glob: str | None = None
41	    pack: str = "tar"  # "tar" | "none" (single regular file, sent byte for byte)
42	    #: Skip units whose newest file is younger than this (still being written).
43	    settle_seconds: float = 0
44	    #: Re-send a unit when its fingerprint changed since it was pushed.
45	    resend_changed: bool = True
46	    #: After the first [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], only the newest N keys are re-fingerprinted each round.
47	    recheck_recent: int | None = None
48	
49	
50	@dataclass(frozen=True)
51	class SenderSpec:
52	    stage_dir: Path
53	    stage_cap: int | None = None
54	    read_blocked: tuple[Window, ...] = ()
55	    delete_source: str = "never"
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class ReceiverSpec:
60	    dest: str  # template; {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}
61	    extract: bool = False
62	    #: Wait instead of receiving while the destination has less free space than this
63	    #: plus about twice the unit size (download + reassembly/extract).
64	    min_free: int = 0
65	
66	
67	@dataclass(frozen=True)
68	class RemoteSpec:
69	    adapter: str
70	    prefix: str
71	    part_size: int | None = None
72	    min_free: int = 0
73	    max_inflight: int | None = None
74	    egress: str = "direct"
75	    #: Interfaces the operator verified as direct (e.g. a TUN whose rules send this
76	    #: backend DIRECT); routes through them are not egress findings.
77	    trusted_interfaces: tuple[str, ...] = ()
78	    options: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
79	    #: Per-side adapter overrides, e.g. the receiver reads an rsync target as "local".
80	    sides: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
81	
82	    def for_side(self, side: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
83	        override = self.sides.get(side, {})
84	        return override.get("adapter", self.adapter), dict(override.get("options", self.options))
85	
86	
87	@dataclass(frozen=True)
88	class Job:
89	    name: str
90	    path: Path | None
91	    state_dir: Path
92	    units: UnitsSpec
93	    sender: SenderSpec
94	    receiver: ReceiverSpec | None
95	    remote: RemoteSpec
96	
97	
98	def _duration(value: str | int | float) -> float:
99	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
100	        return float(value)
101	    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([smhd]?)\s*", value)
102	    if not m:
103	        raise JobError(f"invalid duration {value!r}; use e.g. '30m', '6h', '2d'")
104	    return float(m.group(1)) * {"": 1, "s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400}[m.group(2)]
105	
106	
107	def _path(value: str) -> Path:
108	    return Path(os.path.expandvars(os.path.expanduser(value)))
109	
110	
111	def load_job(path: str | Path) -> Job:
112	    path = Path(path)
113	    with path.open("rb") as f:
114	        return job_from_dict(tomllib.load(f), path)
115	
116	
117	def job_from_dict(data: dict, path: Path | None = None) -> Job:
118	    try:
119	        name = data["name"]
120	        if not _KEY.fullmatch(name):
121	            raise JobError(f"job name {name!r} must be [A-Za-z0-9._-]")
122	        u, s, r = data["units"], data.get("sender", {}), data["remote"]
123	        units = UnitsSpec(root=_path(u["root"]), keys_from=u.get("keys_from"),
124	                          members=tuple(u.get("members", ())), glob=u.get("glob"),
125	                          pack=u.get("pack", "tar"),
126	                          settle_seconds=_duration(u.get("settle", 0)),
127	                          resend_changed=bool(u.get("resend_changed", True)),
128	                          recheck_recent=u.get("recheck_recent"))
129	        if bool(units.keys_from) == bool(units.glob):
130	            raise JobError("units needs exactly one of keys_from (+members) or glob")
131	        if units.keys_from and not units.members:
132	            raise JobError("units.keys_from requires units.members templates")
133	        if units.pack not in ("tar", "none"):
134	            raise JobError("units.pack must be 'tar' or 'none'")
135	        state_dir = _path(data.get("state_dir", f"~/.local/state/ferry/{name}"))
136	        sender = SenderSpec(
137	            stage_dir=_path(s.get("stage_dir", str(state_dir / "stage"))),
138	            stage_cap=parse_size(s.get("stage_cap")),
139	            read_blocked=tuple(Window.parse(w) for w in s.get("read_blocked", ())),
140	            delete_source=s.get("delete_source", "never"))
141	        if sender.delete_source not in DELETE_POLICIES:
142	            raise JobError(f"sender.delete_source must be one of {DELETE_POLICIES}")
143	        receiver = None
144	        if "receiver" in data:
145	            rc = data["receiver"]
146	            receiver = ReceiverSpec(dest=rc["dest"], extract=bool(rc.get("extract", False)),
147	                                    min_free=parse_size(rc.get("min_free", 0)) or 0)
148	        remote = RemoteSpec(adapter=r["adapter"], prefix=r["prefix"].rstrip("/"),
149	                            part_size=parse_size(r.get("part_size")),
150	                            min_free=parse_size(r.get("min_free", 0)) or 0,
151	                            max_inflight=parse_size(r.get("max_inflight")),
152	                            egress=r.get("egress", "direct"),
153	                            trusted_interfaces=tuple(r.get("trusted_interfaces", ())),
154	                            options=dict(r.get("options", {})),
155	                            sides=dict(r.get("sides", {})))
156	        if set(remote.sides) - {"sender", "receiver"}:
157	            raise JobError("remote.sides keys must be 'sender' or 'receiver'")
158	        if remote.egress not in EGRESS_POLICIES:
159	            raise JobError(f"remote.egress must be one of {EGRESS_POLICIES}")
160	    except KeyError as e:
161	        raise JobError(f"missing required job field {e}") from None
162	    return Job(name, path, state_dir, units, sender, receiver, remote)

165	def enumerate_units(spec: UnitsSpec) -> list[Unit]:
166	    """All units currently present under the source root, sorted by key."""
167	    root = spec.root
168	    units: dict[str, Unit] = {}
169	    if spec.keys_from:
170	        for match in root.glob(spec.keys_from):
171	            key = match.stem if match.is_file() else match.name
172	            if not _KEY.fullmatch(key):
173	                raise JobError(f"derived key {key!r} is not a safe name")
174	            members = tuple(m for m in (t.format(key=key) for t in spec.members)
175	                            if (root / m).exists())
176	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, members)
177	    else:
178	        for match in root.glob(spec.glob or ""):
179	            # Remote names starting with "_" are reserved for protocol files.
180	            key = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", match.name).lstrip("._-")
181	            if key in units:
182	                raise JobError(f"two glob matches map to key {key!r}")
183	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, (str(match.relative_to(root)),))

26	def files_of(unit: Unit) -> list[tuple[str, os.stat_result]]:
27	    out = []
28	    for rel in unit.members:
29	        top = unit.root / rel
30	        if top.is_file():
31	            out.append((rel, top.stat()))
32	            continue
33	        for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(top):
34	            dirnames.sort()
35	            for name in filenames:
36	                path = Path(dirpath) / name
37	                out.append((str(path.relative_to(unit.root)), path.stat()))
38	    out.sort()
39	    return out
40	
41	
42	def fingerprint(unit: Unit) -> Fingerprint:
43	    h = hashlib.sha256()
44	    total = 0
45	    newest = 0.0
46	    entries = files_of(unit)
47	    for rel, st in entries:
48	        h.update(f"{rel}\t{st.st_size}\n".encode())
49	        total += st.st_size
50	        newest = max(newest, st.st_mtime)
51	    return Fingerprint(h.hexdigest(), len(entries), total, newest)
52

```markdown
# Ferry

Ferry moves bulk data between hosts that cannot reach each other, using cloud
storage or a shared directory as a relay. When SSH connectivity is available,
it can instead push into a landing directory with rsync.

It is a standalone Python 3.11+ CLI with no runtime Python dependencies.
Cloud and SSH adapters use separately installed backend tools.

## How transfers work

A job groups source paths into **units**. Each unit becomes a tar archive or one
raw file, split into parts if needed. The sender stages and uploads those parts,
then uploads `manifest.json` last to mark the unit ready. The receiver downloads,
checks sizes and SHA-256 hashes, places the result, and removes the relay payload.

- Resume uses per-host ledgers, sender staging, and verified receiver parts.
- Read windows and space limits help control source load and relay occupancy.
- Follow mode discovers new units and detects some source changes.
- Source deletion is optional; start with `delete_source = "never"`.

**The relay is temporary transport, not a backup.** Use a dedicated relay prefix
and destination, retain source data, and verify your recovery process before
considering automatic source deletion.

## Start here

1. [Getting started](getting-started.md): install and try an isolated local relay.
2. [Configuration](configuration.md): define units, limits, and backend adapters.
3. [Operations](operations.md): inspect progress, resume, and run unattended.

Browse the [source repository](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry) and its
[example jobs](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/tree/main/examples).

```

# Getting started

## Install

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed and Python 3.11+ available:

```sh
uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry
ferry --help
```

Ensure uv's tool executable directory is on your `PATH`. The local adapter needs
no other tools or cloud account. Other adapters require their backend CLI and
separately configured authentication; never paste credential or session files
into a job, diagnostic report, or issue.

## Try an isolated local relay

Run these commands in one POSIX shell. They create a fresh temporary directory
containing a non-empty sample file, job state, staging, relay, and destination.
No existing dataset or cloud service is involved.

```sh
demo=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ferry-demo.XXXXXX)
mkdir -p "$demo/source" "$demo/relay" "$demo/destination"
printf 'Hello from Ferry\n' > "$demo/source/hello.txt"

cat > "$demo/job.toml" <<EOF
name = "local-demo"
state_dir = "$demo/state"

[units]
root = "$demo/source"
glob = "*.txt"
pack = "none"

[sender]
stage_dir = "$demo/stage"
delete_source = "never"

[receiver]
dest = "$demo/destination"
extract = false

[remote]
adapter = "local"
prefix = "/local-demo"
egress = "direct"
options = { root = "$demo/relay" }
EOF

ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml"
ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
ferry plan "$demo/job.toml"
ferry send "$demo/job.toml"
ferry receive "$demo/job.toml" --once
ferry status "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
cmp "$demo/source/hello.txt" "$demo/destination/hello.txt"
printf 'Demo directory: %s\n' "$demo"
```

Both doctor checks should report `OK`, and plan should list one unit. After
receiving, status should report one completed unit; `cmp` exits successfully
without output when the files match. The source remains intact. Verified relay
payloads are removed, though protocol files can remain.

Keep the printed directory if you want to inspect or repeat the job. Re-running
with the same state resumes recorded work; it does not force a fresh copy.
There is deliberately no automatic cleanup command here.

## Move to two hosts

Use matching job names, unit definitions, and relay prefixes on both hosts,
with host-appropriate source, staging, state, and destination paths. Each host
keeps its own persistent state. Start with a small disposable dataset and
`delete_source = "never"`; run doctor for each side before sending.

Choose a backend in [Configuration](configuration.md), then read
[Operations](operations.md) before enabling follow mode or source deletion.

# Configuration

A job is a TOML file [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed to each CLI command. Start with the complete
[local quickstart](getting-started.md), then change one setting at a time.
Use absolute filesystem paths for predictable behavior under supervisors.

## Job identity and units

`name` identifies the job; use letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens,
starting with a letter or digit. `state_dir` defaults to
`~/.local/state/ferry/<name>`. Keep it persistent and separate from source data.
Use a dedicated remote prefix for each job, not a shared production directory.

`[units]` requires `root` and exactly one selection method:

- `glob = "exports/*.parquet"`: each match is a unit, keyed from its basename.
  Avoid matches whose names collapse to the same key.
- `keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"` plus
  `members = ["data/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]`: derive each key from a file
  stem or directory name, then collect existing paths from the templates.
  Missing member paths are omitted; inspect `ferry plan` before sending.

`pack = "tar"` is the default. `pack = "none"` requires exactly one regular file
per unit. Empty raw payloads are rejected; use tar when transporting empty files.
Keep unit paths non-overlapping, especially when extracting or deleting sources.

| Optional unit setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `settle = "6h"` | Skip units whose newest file is younger than this; default is no delay. |
| `resend_changed = true` | Default; resend changed fingerprints when source deletion is `never`. |
| `recheck_recent = 30` | In follow mode, limit repeat checks to the last 30 sorted keys; unset checks all. |

Fingerprints use relative paths and file sizes, **not content hashes**. Same-size
edits can go unnoticed. Restarting the sender performs a full fingerprint scan,
not a full content comparison. Settling is a heuristic, not a filesystem snapshot.

## Sender and receiver

| Section / setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `sender.stage_dir` | Local staging; defaults to `<state_dir>/stage`. |
| `sender.stage_cap = "50GB"` | Pause new packing when staged data reaches the cap; not a hard disk quota. |
| `sender.read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]` | Block starting new packing during these windows; uploads continue. |
| `sender.delete_source = "never"` | Default; retain sources. See [deletion policies](operations.md#source-deletion). |
| `receiver.dest` | Required for receiving; supports `{key}` and slices such as `{key[0:4]}`. |
| `receiver.extract = false` | Default; keep tar archives. Raw files are placed under their payload filenames. |
| `receiver.min_free = "20GB"` | Require this floor plus about twice the payload size before receiving. |

With `extract = true`, tar member paths are extracted beneath `dest`; affected
unit paths are replaced wholesale. Use a dedicated destination, not directories
containing unrelated files. Leave room beyond the staging cap for a whole unit.

## Relay and adapter selection

`[remote]` requires `adapter` and `prefix`. Sizes accept strings such as `50GB`
or `3900MiB`. Optional `part_size` controls splitting; defaults depend on the
adapter. `min_free` is enforced only when the adapter can report free space.
`max_inflight` limits outstanding payload bytes tracked for the job; allow at
least the largest whole unit, or sending can wait indefinitely.

| Adapter | Main `options` | Requirements and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local` | `root` | Existing directory; no backend CLI. Both sides must see the same relay contents. |
| `baidupcs` | `binary`, `upload_threads`, `download_threads` | Authenticated BaiduPCS-Go; default parts are 3900 MiB, download threads 4. |
| `rclone` | `remote`, `flags`, `endpoints` | Configured rclone remote, e.g. `gdrive:`. Set endpoint hostnames if inference fails. |
| `ghrelease` | `repo`, `tag` | Authenticated `gh`; creates a missing draft release and refuses a published one. Default parts 1900 MiB, each strictly below 2 GiB. |
| `rsync` | `host`, `root`, `ssh_options`, `flags` | rsync and, for a remote host, working noninteractive SSH; empty `host` means local. |

Ferry requires non-empty remote objects and uses its own SHA-256 verification,
not backend checksums. Backend quotas and permissions still apply.

`[remote.sides.sender]` and `[remote.sides.receiver]` can override `adapter` and
`options`. An overridden options table **replaces**, rather than merges with,
the base options. For direct SSH delivery, send via rsync and receive locally:

```toml
[remote]
adapter = "rsync"
prefix = "/inbox"
options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }

[remote.sides.receiver]
adapter = "local"
options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
```

This is a fragment, not a complete job. The receiver runs on `nas` and reads the
same landing directory. `egress = "direct"` is the default; see
[egress controls](operations.md#egress) before accepting proxy routes.

## Example jobs

Adapt paths and review policies before using these public repository examples:

- [Incremental mirror](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/mirror-incremental.toml): retains sources and extracts at the destination.
- [Baidu archive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/daily-archive-baidu.toml): **deletes sources after remote size checks**; change to `never` for a pilot.
- [Google Drive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/gdrive-via-proxy.toml): explicitly accepts non-direct egress.
- [GitHub draft release](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/github-draft-release.toml): raw-file units; replace the repository placeholder.

````markdown
# Operations

## Inspect before transferring

```sh
ferry doctor job.toml
ferry doctor job.toml --side receiver
ferry plan job.toml
ferry status job.toml
ferry status job.toml --side receiver --json
ferry status job.toml --scan-source --remote
```

Doctor checks the selected backend and egress; it can contact remote services
and, for rsync, create a missing landing directory. It is not a generic dry-run
or proof that every later backend operation will succeed. Plan enumerates source
units and members; it does not simulate transfer, settling, or source deletion.

Status normally reads local ledgers. `--scan-source` adds source enumeration;
`--remote` queries the backend for relay information. Sender and receiver have
separate state, so inspect each on its own host. Commands accept `--json`, but
service output remains supervisor text rather than a general JSON report.

## Run and resume

```sh
ferry send job.toml
ferry receive job.toml --once
```

Send processes eligible work and marks the sender done. Receive with `--once`
makes one [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]; without it, receive waits until the sender is done and the relay
is empty. For continuous operation, run `send --follow` and `receive --follow`
in separate processes, adding `--poll 60` to control idle polling in seconds.

To resume, restart the same command with the same job, state, staging, and relay
prefix. Do not delete ledgers, staged manifests, or destination partial files to
"fix" an interrupted transfer. Uploaded parts with matching remote sizes can be
reused; downloaded parts are checked by SHA-256 before reuse. One sender and one
receiver may run per job on a host; a second instance of either side fails fast.

Inspect `<state_dir>/sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`, and side logs when progress
stalls. Check read windows, settling, staging space, remote limits, destination
free space, and preflight errors. Keep credentials and session files out of reports.

## Integrity and destination safety

The sender hashes the packed payload and its parts. The receiver checks sizes,
part and whole-payload SHA-256 hashes, and tar member counts before recording
verification. It then removes that unit's relay data. With extraction enabled,
existing unit paths are replaced, including removal of files absent in the new copy.

Change detection is weaker than transfer verification: its path-and-size
fingerprints miss same-size edits. `ferry inventory job.toml --no-upload --json`
previews fingerprints of an existing destination tree; omit `--no-upload` only
when you intend to publish them to the relay for sender-side skipping. Use
`--root PATH` for a source-shaped tree when `receiver.dest` contains a key template.
Inventory seeding is not a content-hash audit or evidence of a fresh transfer.

## Source deletion

- `never` is the default and the recommended starting point.
- `after_remote_size` deletes source members after upload size checks, **before
  destination SHA-256 verification**. Use only for independently recoverable data.
- `after_receiver_ack` waits for the receiver's verification acknowledgement.
  Keep the sender running or restart it to consume acknowledgements; one-shot
  sending can wait for the receiver rather than exiting immediately.

Keep source units immutable throughout transfer and acknowledgement handling:
settling does not lock files, and deletion acts on source paths. Use trusted,
job-specific relay storage; do not fabricate acknowledgements or reuse old
protocol state for a different dataset. Neither deletion policy replaces backups.

## Egress

Backend subprocesses always have proxy environment variables stripped, including
when `egress = "any"`. The default `direct` policy rejects detected backend proxy
settings, fake-IP DNS in `198.18.0.0/15`, and routes through recognized tunnel
interfaces. Backend-internal proxy configuration and host routing still matter.

Set `remote.egress = "any"`, or [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `--allow-proxy` to doctor/send/receive, only
when accepting those egress findings is intentional. This does not restore proxy
environment variables or fix missing authentication. `trusted_interfaces` exempts
interfaces you have independently verified route this backend directly. Host
checks cannot detect every transparent upstream proxy; verify cost-sensitive paths.

## Unattended operation

Preview a supervisor definition before installing anything:

```sh
ferry service job.toml --side receiver
ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
```

Systemd user units run follow mode with `Restart=on-failure`; cron uses one-shot
commands and job locks prevent overlap. `--install` writes and enables the selected
service, so it can start transfers immediately; `--uninstall` removes it. Systemd
may need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` to survive logout. On other supervisors,
including launchd, use the corresponding send/receive command explicitly. Test
manually with source retention before enabling any unattended destructive policy.

````markdown
# Zensical says "No issues found" but llms.txt contains only headings

## Symptom

With Zensical 0.0.73, `zensical build --strict` prints:

```text
Build started
No issues found
Build finished in 0.45s
```

But `llms.txt` contains only the site and section headings, and root source
pages have no exported Markdown counterparts or Copy as Markdown buttons.

## Root cause

The native llmstxt section used only `Documentation = ["**/*.md"]`.
In the tested release, that pattern did not select `docs/index.md` or other
root-level pages. A strict build does not reject an empty matched section.

## Workaround

Cover both root and nested source paths:

```toml
[project.plugins.llmstxt.sections]
Documentation = ["*.md", "**/*.md"]
```

Explicit source paths are also appropriate for a curated section.

## Prevention

Compare the llms index with the intended source inventory; validate exported
Markdown, full output, and copy-button URLs. A successful build and the mere
existence of `llms.txt` are not sufficient. Recheck these patterns when updating
Zensical rather than assuming another tool's glob semantics apply.

````

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""Initialize an English Zensical site without installing or publishing anything."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import tomllib
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

ASSETS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"
VERSION = "0.0.73"


def safe_path(root, relative):
    path = root
    for part in Path(relative).parts:
        path /= part
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError(f"refusing symlink: {path}")
    return path


def initialize(args):
    target = Path(args.target_dir).expanduser()
    if target.is_symlink() or not target.is_dir():
        raise ValueError("--target-dir must be an existing non-symlink directory")
    root = target.resolve()
    url = urlsplit(args.site_url)
    if (url.scheme not in {"https", "http"} or not url.netloc or url.username
            or url.[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]word or url.query or url.fragment or not args.site_url.endswith("/")):
        raise ValueError("--site-url must be an HTTP(S) URL ending in /, without credentials/query/fragment")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", args.repo_slug):
        raise ValueError("--repo-slug must be owner/repo")
    if not args.site_name.strip() or "\n" in args.site_name:
        raise ValueError("--site-name must be a nonempty single line")
    for name in ("mkdocs.yml", "mkdocs.yaml", "zensical.toml"):
        path = safe_path(root, name)
        if path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"existing {name}; maintain it explicitly instead of bootstrapping over it")

    docs = safe_path(root, "docs")
    if docs.exists() and not docs.is_dir():
        raise ValueError("docs exists but is not a directory")
    existing = list(docs.rglob("*")) if docs.exists() else []
    if any(path.is_symlink() for path in existing):
        raise ValueError("docs contains symlinks; select a real, curated source tree first")
    if existing and args.existing != "keep":
        raise ValueError("docs is nonempty; review its publishable contents, then use --existing keep")
    if existing and not (docs / "index.md").is_file():
        raise ValueError("existing docs needs an index.md; no content will be generated over it")

    values = {
        "SITE_NAME": json.dumps(args.site_name, ensure_ascii=False),
        "SITE_URL": json.dumps(args.site_url),
        "REPO_URL": json.dumps(f"https://github.com/{args.repo_slug}"),
    }
    config = re.sub(r"\{\{([A-Z_]+)\}\}", lambda match: values[match[1]],
                    (ASSETS / "zensical.toml.template").read_text())
    tomllib.loads(config)
    files = {
        "zensical.toml": config,
        "scripts/check-docs-site.py": (ASSETS / "check-docs-site.py").read_text(),
    }
    if not existing:
        files["docs/index.md"] = (ASSETS / "index.md.template").read_text().replace(
            "{{SITE_NAME}}", args.site_name)
    if args.ci:
        files[".github/workflows/docs-check.yml"] = (ASSETS / "docs-check.yml").read_text()

    pyproject = safe_path(root, "pyproject.toml")
    if pyproject.exists():
        tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text())
    else:
        files["pyproject.toml"] = (
            f'[dependency-groups]\ndocs = ["zensical=={VERSION}"]\n'
            '\n[tool.uv]\npackage = false\n'
        )
    for relative in files:
        destination = safe_path(root, relative)
        if destination.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"would overwrite {relative}; resolve the conflict first")
        if any(parent.exists() and not parent.is_dir()
               for parent in destination.parents if parent != root.parent):
            raise ValueError(f"non-directory parent for {relative}")

    ignore = safe_path(root, ".gitignore")
    original_ignore = ignore.read_text() if ignore.exists() else ""
    ignored = original_ignore.splitlines()
    additions = [line for line in ("/site/", "/.cache/", "/.venv/") if line not in ignored]
    updated_ignore = original_ignore
    if additions:
        if updated_ignore and not updated_ignore.endswith("\n"):
            updated_ignore += "\n"
        updated_ignore += "\n".join(additions) + "\n"

    if not args.dry_run:
        for relative, content in files.items():
            destination = root / relative
            destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with destination.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
                stream.write(content)
        if additions:
            ignore.write_text(updated_ignore, encoding="utf-8")

    return {
        "status": "planned" if args.dry_run else "created",
        "target": str(root),
        "files": list(files),
        "preserved_existing_docs": bool(existing),
        "gitignore_additions": additions,
        "next_steps": [
            f"uv add --group docs 'zensical=={VERSION}'" if pyproject.exists()
            and "pyproject.toml" not in files else "uv lock",
            "uv sync --locked --only-group docs",
            "uv run --no-sync zensical build --strict",
            "uv run --no-sync python scripts/check-docs-site.py",
        ],
        "deployed": False,
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--target-dir", required=True, help="Existing project root (never inferred from CWD)")
    parser.add_argument("--site-name", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--site-url", required=True, help="Future site base URL including /project/ and trailing /")
    parser.add_argument("--repo-slug", required=True, help="GitHub owner/repo")
    parser.add_argument("--existing", choices=["keep"], help="Preserve an explicitly reviewed existing docs tree")
    parser.add_argument("--ci", action="store_true", help="Add build-only Actions workflow; never deploy")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Report exact planned files without writing")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = initialize(args)
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(json.dumps({"status": "blocked", "deployed": False}))
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

1	# Ferry
2	
3	Ferry moves bulk data between hosts that cannot reach each other, using cloud
4	storage or a shared directory as a relay. When SSH connectivity is available,
5	it can instead push into a landing directory with rsync.
6	
7	It is a standalone Python 3.11+ CLI with no runtime Python dependencies.
8	Cloud and SSH adapters use separately installed backend tools.
9	
10	## How transfers work
11	
12	A job groups source paths into **units**. Each unit becomes a tar archive or one
13	raw file, split into parts if needed. The sender stages and uploads those parts,
14	then uploads `manifest.json` last to mark the unit ready. The receiver downloads,
15	checks sizes and SHA-256 hashes, places the result, and removes the relay payload.
16	
17	- Resume uses per-host ledgers, sender staging, and verified receiver parts.
18	- Read windows and space limits help control source load and relay occupancy.
19	- Follow mode discovers new units and detects some source changes.
20	- Source deletion is optional; start with `delete_source = "never"`.
21	
22	**The relay is temporary transport, not a backup.** Use a dedicated relay prefix
23	and destination, retain source data, and verify your recovery process before
24	considering automatic source deletion.
25	
26	## Start here
27	
28	1. [Getting started](getting-started.md): install and try an isolated local relay.
29	2. [Configuration](configuration.md): define units, limits, and backend adapters.
30	3. [Operations](operations.md): inspect progress, resume, and run unattended.
31	
32	Browse the [source repository](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry) and its
33	[example jobs](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/tree/main/examples).
34
```

85	        members, filename = 1, source.name
86	    writer.close()
87	    if writer.size == 0:
88	        shutil.rmtree(tmp)
89	        raise ValueError(f"unit {unit.key} produced an empty payload")

91	                        filename=filename, size=writer.size, sha256=writer.total.hexdigest(),
92	                        parts=tuple(writer.parts), members=members, ack_required=ack_required,
93	                        source_host=socket.gethostname(), created_at=utcnow(),
94	                        paths=tuple(unit.members), fingerprint=fingerprint, revision=revision)
95	    (tmp / "manifest.json").write_text(manifest.to_json())
96	    shutil.rmtree(final, ignore_errors=True)
97	    tmp.rename(final)
98	    return manifest

101	def _walk(path: Path):
102	    """Deterministic (sorted) traversal including directories, so tar output is stable."""
103	    yield path
104	    if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():
105	        for child in sorted(path.iterdir()):
106	            yield from _walk(child)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check the English all-pages artifact contract; never build or publish the site."""

import argparse
from html.parser import HTMLParser
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import tomllib
from urllib.parse import unquote, urljoin, urlsplit


class Page(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self, text):
        super().__init__()
        self.copy_urls = []
        self.links = []
        self.feed(text)

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        if "data-md-copy-url" in attrs:
            self.copy_urls.append(attrs["data-md-copy-url"])
        if tag == "a" and attrs.get("href"):
            self.links.append(attrs["href"])
        if tag == "img" and attrs.get("src"):
            self.links.append(attrs["src"])


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def check(root):
    project = tomllib.loads((root / "zensical.toml").read_text())["project"]
    require(project.get("docs_dir", "docs") == "docs" and project.get("site_dir", "site") == "site",
            "this checker expects docs/ and site/; review it before changing output layout")
    require(project.get("theme", {}).get("language") == "en", "this pilot validates English content only")
    require(not project.get("hooks"), "MkDocs hooks are not supported by this pilot")
    plugins = project.get("plugins", {})
    require(not (set(plugins) - {"search", "llmstxt"}),
            "additional plugins need an explicit compatibility and artifact review")
    require(plugins.get("llmstxt", {}).get("full_output") == "llms-full.txt",
            "expected llmstxt.full_output = llms-full.txt")
    base = project["site_url"]
    require(base.endswith("/"), "site_url must end in /")
    origin = urlsplit(base)
    docs, site = root / "docs", root / "site"
    for directory in (docs, site):
        require(directory.is_dir() and not directory.is_symlink(), f"missing or symlinked {directory.name}/")
        require(not any(path.is_symlink() for path in directory.rglob("*")),
                f"{directory.name}/ contains symlinks")
    sources = sorted(docs.rglob("*.md"))
    require(sources and (docs / "index.md") in sources, "expected docs/index.md and Markdown pages")

    def local_file(url):
        parsed = urlsplit(url)
        require((parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) == (origin.scheme, origin.netloc),
                f"artifact URL uses a different origin: {url}")
        require(parsed.path.startswith(origin.path), f"artifact URL drops the project subpath: {url}")
        relative = unquote(parsed.path[len(origin.path):])
        path = (site / relative).resolve()
        require(path.is_relative_to(site.resolve()), f"artifact URL escapes site/: {url}")
        if parsed.path.endswith("/"):
            path /= "index.html"
        require(path.is_file(), f"missing artifact for {url}")
        return path

    index = (site / "llms.txt").read_text()
    full = (site / "llms-full.txt").read_text()
    links = re.findall(r"^\s*-\s+\[.*?\]\(<?([^)>\s]+)>?\)", index, re.MULTILINE)
    exported = [local_file(link) for link in links]
    require(len(exported) == len(set(exported)), "duplicate pages in llms.txt")
    expected = set()
    for source in sources:
        relative = source.relative_to(docs)
        directory = relative.parent if relative.name == "index.md" else relative.with_suffix("")
        markdown = site / directory / "index.md"
        html = site / directory / "index.html"
        expected.add(markdown.resolve())
        require(markdown.is_file() and html.is_file(), f"missing HTML/Markdown pair for {relative}")
        content = markdown.read_text().strip()
        require(content and content in full, f"full output omits content from {relative}")
        page = Page(html.read_text())
        html_url = urljoin(base, html.relative_to(site).as_posix())
        require(page.copy_urls, f"missing Copy as Markdown button for {relative}")
        for url in page.copy_urls:
            require(local_file(urljoin(html_url, url)) == markdown.resolve(),
                    f"copy button selects the wrong source for {relative}")
        for href in page.links:
            if href.startswith("#"):
                continue
            url = urljoin(html_url, href)
            parsed = urlsplit(url)
            if (parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) == (origin.scheme, origin.netloc):
                local_file(url)
    require(set(exported) == expected, "llms.txt does not cover exactly the intended Markdown pages")
    search = json.loads((site / "search.json").read_text())
    require(bool(search), "empty search index")
    return {"status": "ok", "pages": len(sources), "llm_pages": len(exported), "deployed": False}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--target-dir", default=".", help="Project root containing zensical.toml")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = check(Path(args.target_dir).resolve())
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "deployed": False}))
        return 1
    print(json.dumps(result))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Isolated bootstrap safety tests and a pinned real-builder smoke test."""

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import tomllib
import unittest

SKILL = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INIT = SKILL / "scripts" / "init-docs-site.py"


class BootstrapTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temporary.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)

    def initialize(self, *args):
        return subprocess.run([
            sys.executable, "-I", str(INIT), "--target-dir", str(self.root),
            "--site-name", 'Example "Docs"', "--site-url", "https://example.test/project/",
            "--repo-slug", "owner/repo", *args,
        ], capture_output=True, text=True)

    def snapshot(self):
        return {str(p.relative_to(self.root)): p.read_bytes()
                for p in self.root.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink()}

    def test_dry_run_writes_nothing(self):
        result = self.initialize("--ci", "--dry-run")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout)["status"], "planned")
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), {})

    def test_fresh_site_and_build_only_ci(self):
        result = self.initialize("--ci")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        config = tomllib.loads((self.root / "zensical.toml").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(config["project"]["site_name"], 'Example "Docs"')
        self.assertEqual(config["project"]["theme"]["language"], "en")
        deps = tomllib.loads((self.root / "pyproject.toml").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependency-groups"]["docs"], ["zensical==0.0.73"])
        workflow = (self.root / ".github/workflows/docs-check.yml").read_text()
        self.assertIn("pull_request:", workflow)
        self.assertIn("--locked --only-group docs", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("pages: write", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("actions/deploy-pages", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn(".github/workflows/docs.yml", self.snapshot())
        before = self.snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(self.initialize().returncode, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)

    def test_existing_docs_require_opt_in_and_preserve_dependencies(self):
        (self.root / "docs").mkdir()
        (self.root / "docs/index.md").write_text("# User content\n")
        (self.root / "pyproject.toml").write_text('[project]\nname="app"\nversion="0.1.0"\ndependencies=[]\n')
        (self.root / ".gitignore").write_text("custom-file")
        original = self.snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(self.initialize().returncode, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), original)
        result = self.initialize("--existing", "keep")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        for name in ("docs/index.md", "pyproject.toml"):
            self.assertEqual(self.snapshot()[name], original[name])
        self.assertTrue((self.root / ".gitignore").read_text().startswith("custom-file\n"))
        self.assertIn("uv add --group docs", json.loads(result.stdout)["next_steps"][0])

    def test_config_or_output_conflict_fails_before_writes(self):
        for name in ("mkdocs.yml", "mkdocs.yaml", "scripts/check-docs-site.py",
                     ".github/workflows/docs-check.yml"):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                path = self.root / name
                path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                path.write_text("user owned\n")
                before = self.snapshot()
                self.assertEqual(self.initialize("--ci").returncode, 2)
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), before)
                path.unlink()

    def test_symlinks_fail_closed(self):
        for name in ("docs", "scripts", ".gitignore", "pyproject.toml"):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                path = self.root / name
                path.symlink_to(self.root / "missing")
                self.assertEqual(self.initialize().returncode, 2)
                self.assertFalse((self.root / "zensical.toml").exists())
                path.unlink()

    def test_docs_symlink_is_not_followed(self):
        (self.root / "docs").mkdir()
        (self.root / "docs/index.md").symlink_to(self.root / "missing")
        self.assertEqual(self.initialize("--existing", "keep").returncode, 2)
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "zensical.toml").exists())

    def test_invalid_url_fails_without_writes(self):
        for url in ("https://example.test/project", "https://user:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@example.test/", "file:///tmp/"):
            with self.subTest(url=url):
                self.assertEqual(self.initialize("--site-url", url).returncode, 2)
                self.assertEqual(self.snapshot(), {})

    @unittest.skipUnless(os.environ.get("ZENSICAL_INTEGRATION") == "1", "set ZENSICAL_INTEGRATION=1 for real builds")
    def test_real_build_and_artifact_failures(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.initialize().returncode, 0)
        (self.root / "docs/guides").mkdir()
        (self.root / "docs/guides/setup.md").write_text(
            "# Nested setup\n\nNested export marker.\n\n[Home](../index.md)\n")

        checker = [sys.executable, "-I", str(self.root / "scripts/check-docs-site.py"),
                   "--target-dir", str(self.root)]
        result = subprocess.run(checker, capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout)["llm_pages"], 2)
        llms = self.root / "site/llms.txt"
        original = llms.read_text()
        llms.write_text("# Empty\n")
        self.assertNotEqual(subprocess.run(checker, capture_output=True).returncode, 0)
        llms.write_text(original)
        llms.write_text(original.replace("https://example.test/project/", "https://example.test/"))
        self.assertNotEqual(subprocess.run(checker, capture_output=True).returncode, 0)
        llms.write_text(original)
        markdown = self.root / "site/guides/setup/index.md"
        markdown.unlink()
        self.assertNotEqual(subprocess.run(checker, capture_output=True).returncode, 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

````markdown
---
name: zensical-site-bootstrap
description: 'Bootstrap and maintain English Zensical documentation with locked uv docs dependencies, native llms.txt and Copy as Markdown, safe existing-content handling, and build-only GitHub Actions. Use when explicitly setting up Zensical, dogfooding a new docs site, checking LLM exports, or maintaining a Zensical project. # Zensical site bootstrap

Build an English documentation site without adding application runtime
dependencies or publishing anything. This is a single-language pilot, separate
from `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`; existing MkDocs projects retain their old workflow.

Requires Python 3.11+ and `uv`. The tested builder is **Zensical 0.0.73**.

## When to use

- The user explicitly chooses Zensical for a new documentation site.
- A project is dogfooding Zensical before installing the published skill.
- A Zensical build succeeds but llms exports or Copy as Markdown are missing.
- The user wants to add pages or verify an existing Zensical site's artifacts.

## When not to use

- The user only asks for one Markdown document: do not scaffold a site.
- Existing MkDocs configuration, arbitrary plugins, hooks, or content-i18n
  requirements need migration analysis, not this initializer.
- English plus selected zh-TW, fallback, or contextual language switching is
  required now: prefer the existing MkDocs skill until that contract is tested.
- A generic request to "set up docs" is not permission to replace an existing
  engine. Inspect it and establish the desired scope first.

## Workflow

### 1. Confirm scope and inspect the project

Read project instructions, README, existing docs, `pyproject.toml`, task runner,
CI, `.gitignore`, and any recorded docs preferences. Keep the application's
runtime dependency contract. Do not reuse the MkDocs preference namespace or
change an explicit opt-out without the user's request.

Confirm an **English-only** initial site and which files are publishable. Do not
point `docs_dir` at the repository root or copy `backlog/`, agent history,
credentials, or runtime state into the site. A public repository is not consent
to enable Pages. Do not translate content automatically.

Read `references/pilot-and-migration.md` when comparing engines, planning later
translations, or replacing a local dogfood source with an installed skill.

### 2. Preview, then initialize

Use this skill's actual installed directory for the script path. Pass the
project root explicitly; never infer it from the agent's current directory.

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/init-docs-site.py" \
  --target-dir /path/to/project \
  --site-name 'My Project' \
  --repo-slug owner/project \
  --site-url https://owner.github.io/project/ \
  --ci --dry-run
```

After reviewing the plan and obtaining consent, repeat without `--dry-run`.
`--ci` adds a **build-only** workflow; omitting it creates no workflow.
For a reviewed nonempty `docs/`, add `--existing keep`. It requires an existing
`docs/index.md` and preserves the whole tree; it does not reorganize content.

The initializer refuses existing MkDocs/Zensical config, symlinks, and collisions
with generated paths. There is no `--force` mode. Re-running on a configured
project stops without changes: switch to maintenance instead.

### 3. Add development-only dependencies and build

Existing `pyproject.toml` is left untouched; follow the initializer's JSON
`next_steps` after reviewing the proposed dependency group:

```bash
uv add --group docs 'zensical==0.0.73'
uv sync --locked --only-group docs
uv run --no-sync zensical build --strict
uv run --no-sync python scripts/check-docs-site.py
```

A docs-only project without a prior `pyproject.toml` receives a virtual uv
project with a docs group; run `uv lock` first instead of `uv add`.
Keep `uv.lock` under version control. Inspect its diff: do not silently upgrade
unrelated dependencies or replace an existing package index.

`--only-group docs` is suitable for CI. For local work that also needs the
application/dev dependencies, use `uv sync --locked --group docs` instead.
Do not put Zensical in `[project].dependencies` merely to make a build work.

The project-local checker verifies root and nested pages, full text, Markdown
counterparts, Copy as Markdown targets, project-subpath links, and a nonempty
search artifact. Fix failures instead of dropping strict mode. Its contract is
all `docs/**/*.md` pages; custom exclusions, output layouts, or plugins require
reviewing and adapting the checker as part of the same change.

### 4. Maintain project-owned documentation

Add English `.md` pages under `docs/` and keep relative links correct. The
initial config uses automatic navigation and llmstxt globs for root and nested
pages; no separate page helper is needed. If the user wants an explicit `nav`,
maintain it alongside the pages. Do not create locale-suffixed placeholders.

Preserve the README as a useful repository entrypoint. Link it to `docs/index.md`
until a site is actually published; a future `site_url` is not a live website.
Add commands to the project's existing Makefile/Justfile rather than replacing
its task runner. Run its normal checks as well as the documentation checks.

For preview:

```bash
uv run --no-sync zensical serve
```

In a browser, test navigation, search, and Copy as Markdown, including a nested
page. Check the clipboard content, not only that a button exists. Building the
site is not proof of interactive behavior.

### 5. Publish only after separate approval

The bundled workflow has no Pages permissions, deployment job, or public
preview. Do not enable Pages, dispatch deployment, or push changes merely
because initialization succeeded.

When explicitly asked to publish, read the current official
[Pages guide](https://zensical.org/docs/publish-your-site/). Adapt its artifact
flow to the existing locked docs group and checker. Keep PRs build-only; deploy
only approved default-branch events. Scope `pages: write` and `id-token: write`
to the deploy job, preserve project-subpath URLs, and confirm repo visibility.

## Available scripts

- `scripts/init-docs-site.py` — stdlib-only, no install/network/deploy operations.
  Flags: `--target-dir`, `--site-name`, `--site-url`, `--repo-slug`,
  `--existing keep`, `--ci`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  JSON stdout; diagnostics on stderr. Exit 0 success/preview, 2 blocked input.
- Project-local `scripts/check-docs-site.py` — copied from the asset below.
  Flags: `--target-dir` (defaults to CWD), `--help`. JSON stdout, diagnostics on
  stderr; exit 0 validated, 1 failed. It does not rebuild or publish anything.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/zensical.toml.template` — English theme, native copy/llmstxt, root and
  nested Markdown selection; no custom MkDocs plugin lifecycle.
- `assets/index.md.template` — starter page only for an empty docs tree.
- `assets/docs-check.yml` — locked build and artifact checks, no deployment.
- `assets/check-docs-site.py` — project-owned output-contract checker.

## Reference files

- `references/pilot-and-migration.md` — read before dogfooding, upgrading the
  builder, switching to a distributed skill, or considering multilingual docs.

## Gotchas

- **`**/*.md` alone can silently omit root pages.** The tested native llmstxt
  implementation needs `*.md` as well. Strict build can [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] with empty exports.
- **UI translation is not content i18n.** An alternate-language selector does
  not create translated pages or implement missing-translation fallback.
- **Zensical does not execute arbitrary MkDocs plugins.** Unsupported settings
  may be ignored; this pilot's checker allows only search and llmstxt plugins.
- **Upstream `zensical new` includes a deployment workflow with unpinned install.**
  Do not run it blindly inside a real project; this skill uses reviewed,
  build-only templates instead.
- **Installing/updating a skill does not migrate generated project files.**
  Keep the docs, config, checker and CI self-contained. Compare explicit changes
  after an update; never rerun initialization with an imagined force flag.
- **A local preview cannot prove GitHub Pages configuration.** Report local
  validation separately from installation, remote CI, and publication.

## Scope and ownership

This skill starts with English, static navigation/search, code blocks, native
LLM exports and Copy as Markdown. It does not promise API-generator integration,
MkDocs plugin compatibility, bilingual content/fallback, or versioned publishing.

This consumer command intentionally tracks the published CLI. For reproducible

The initial pin is Zensical **0.0.73**, not a permanent guarantee. Test:
