154	queued or runtime-done is not READY. Native Windows co-commit remains unsupported.
155	
156	## Choose the containment base
157	
158	`dev work retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
159	linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
160	branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
161	`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
162	Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
163	a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
164	Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch.
165	
166	Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
167	fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
168	prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] --base <branch>` guidance.
169	After `dev work done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the
170	external coordinator carry X forward as `dev work retire --base X <task>`. If a shell
171	handoff cannot carry the override, dev prints the external command instead.
172	
173	Optional `--delete-branch` still runs ordinary `git branch -d`, whose own merged
174	check uses the branch's upstream or HEAD, not `--base`. Against a non-HEAD base,
175	branch deletion can therefore fail after the worktree was removed; the branch
176	and DONE task remain, and the result reports partial completion.
177	
178	## Pull-request flow
179	
180	```bash
181	dev work done <task> --pr
182	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
183	git fetch origin
184	dev work done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
185	dev work retire --base origin/main <task> --delete-branch
186	```
187	
188	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent. It requires an explicit operator
189	attestation:
190	
191	```bash
192	dev work done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
193	```
194	
195	This proves only that the named squash commit is in the base; the operator is
196	asserting that it represents the feature. Equal trees after a squash are not
197	ancestry proof and do not waive retirement's containment checks.
198	
199	## Safety policy
200	
201	Retirement always refuses when:
202	
203	- the caller cwd is the target or below it;
204	- the caller Herdr workspace/pane or tmux pane covers the target;
205	- a workspace contains panes outside the target;
206	- an agent is `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting`;
207	- runtime enumeration fails;
208	- the checkout is dirty, on the wrong branch, or not contained in its base;
209	- relevant artifact proof is pending, failed, unknown or no longer reachable.
210	
211	`unknown` or empty agent status requires `--close-unknown` from outside the
212	target. Runtime enumeration failure requires external `--assume-no-runtime`.
213	Neither flag by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es caller containment or active-agent states.
214	
215	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools can by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] dev.
216	Never run them from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee covers
217	only dev-mediated paths. Existing CLI expert acknowledgements remain compatible,
218	but flow intentionally omits them. Task-backed and exact unmanaged path
219	retirement use taskflow, with contained removal required for the latter. Some
220	record-only/salvage `sweep` actions remain isolated compatibility paths.
221	
222	## What self-deletion looks like
223	
224	A real Codex session deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another
225	checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because Unix processes can
226	hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked. SpecStory then recreated the
227	same path with only `.specstory/` content.
228	
229	The resulting shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:

1	# Worktree ownership
2	
3	For ordinary clone/worktree acquisition, submodule initialization is core Git acquisition, before provisioning/runtime, and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not skip it; `--submodules=none` does. Gitlink children are independent submodule clones, not nested managed linked worktrees. Read `submodules.md` for selection and explicit disposal rules.
4	
5	Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
6	a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.
7	
8	## The rule
9	
10	| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev work retire` |
13	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
14	| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
15	| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |
16	
17	Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
18	history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
19	ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
20	coordination override—not a default.
21	
22	`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
23	existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
24	new process from the target worktree root.
25	
26	## Create managed work or surface an existing checkout
27	
28	Task tracking is optional. `dev git worktree create <branch> --base <ref>`
29	creates/provisions/opens a checkout without a task record. Existing Git work
30	survives closing its runtime without adoption. Use `dev work start` only when
31	the recorded start/park/resume lifecycle is wanted.
32	
33	For task-free merged cleanup, run from the canonical checkout and outside the
34	target runtime: `dev work sweep --merged-worktrees --base main --delete-branches`
35	reports the exact contained candidates; after review, add `--apply` to confirm
36	each removal. An open PR, agent `done`, or td issue closure is not containment.
37	Dirty products and unsettled artifacts remain blockers. A transcript path is
38	not a discard allowlist; inspect its exact final changes after the writer exits.
39	Squash integration may require a separate manual decision.
40	
41	Prefer `dev work start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>'` for new
42	managed work: it creates/selects the checkout, provisions it, opens the runtime,
43	and records task intent. For an already registered external worktree that only
44	needs runtime visibility:
45	
46	```bash
47	dev git worktree open <branch> --repo <repo> --runtime herdr --no-focus
48	```
49	
50	This opens or reuses the exact checkout without switching/attaching, launching an
51	agent, provisioning, or adopting a task. Dirty files and the index stay untouched.
52	It reports branch, actual path and backend/handle immediately, followed by the
53	observed runtime opened/reused surface; this is not Git worktree creation. With
54	runtime `none`, no runtime opens and no shell `cd` handoff is emitted. Without
55	`--no-focus`, normal activation or shell navigation is unchanged. Runtime errors
56	remain errors; do not turn a failed open into a success report.
57	
58	When handing work back, report the repository, branch, actual checkout path and
59	runtime handle/result immediately. Adoption is a separate lifecycle decision,
60	not a visibility switch. See `runtime-herdr.md` for reuse/fallback boundaries.
61	
62	## PR/MR trial checkouts
63	
64	`dev pr checkout <URL>` selects an exact existing checkout without resetting
65	local work, or fetches the verified request head into a task-free worktree.
66	Do not match a fork's branch by name alone. Multiple clone/checkout matches
67	require an explicit selection. Existing SSH fetch transport remains native;
68	`--source-remote` resolves ambiguous base remotes.
69	
70	PR acquisition does not run ordinary provisioning or submodule initialization
71	by default. Only explicit `--provision` authorizes project setup under existing
72	trust rules. Without a local repository, `--try` creates an independent
73	catalog-backed dated clone; `--clone [--path PATH]` creates a project clone and
74	worktree. Neither implicitly forks or creates task intent. `--dry-run` is
75	read-only and `--no-open`/`--json` suppress runtime opening. Merge and optional
76	base synchronization never replace retirement/cleanup proof. Read
77	[pull requests](pull-requests.md) for exact-head merge guards and unknown receipts.
78	
79	## Why dev creates the checkout
80	
81	`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
82	`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
83	on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
84	A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
85	target.
86	
87	Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
88	server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.
89	
90	Herdr's native **New worktree** action is still valid for an external,
91	unmanaged checkout. When the canonical repository is under a configured scan
92	root, Git registration lets dev discover the checkout without scanning
93	`~/.herdr/worktrees`; dev does not auto-adopt, relocate, or provision it. Run
94	`dev git worktree provision <path>` if it needs the project environment and `dev work adopt`
95	followed by `dev work adopt --apply` only when it should enter the durable task
96	lifecycle. For one exact checkout, `dev repo flow [repo]` offers plan-first
97	metadata-only Adopt and clean branch-preserving Remove Checkout. It never removes
98	the canonical checkout or a harness/conflicting/locked/prunable/task-claimed row,
99	and it does not prune repository-wide stale registrations.
100	
101	## Paths
102	
103	Default:
104	
105	```text
106	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
107	```
108	
109	Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
110	`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
111	variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.
112	
113	Always [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `--base` for unattended creation so the intended starting point is
114	explicit. `dev work start` and `dev git worktree create` otherwise resolve the repository's
115	default branch; they do not use whichever feature happens to be checked out.
116	
117	## Provisioning
118	
119	A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev git worktree create` and `dev work start` build and apply
120	an inspectable plan:
121	
122	```bash
123	dev git worktree plan
124	dev git worktree plan --write
125	dev git worktree provision --dry-run
126	```
127	
128	Effective settings come from global config or committed repo
129	`.dev-cli/config.toml` (legacy `.dev.toml` remains readable):
130	
131	```toml
132	[worktree]
133	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
134	link = []
135	post_create = "auto"
136	strategy = "reinstall"
137	```
138	
139	An executable `post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml` requires approval of its
140	exact content hash with `dev self config trust <repo> --yes`. Legacy `.dev.toml`
141	retains its compatibility behavior.
142	
143	Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
144	copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
145	must remain the same regular file from validation through open; source swaps and
146	symlinked destination parents are refused. Existing destinations are reported
147	as skipped, never falsely as copied, and file contents are never logged.
148	
149	This is local provisioning only. Off-machine `dev fleet files` deliberately uses
150	a separate `[local_files].include` allowlist plus explicit `--to`; never infer
151	export permission from `[worktree].include`.
152	
153	### Project-local Claude backend state
154	
155	`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
156	include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper preserves an existing
157	Copilot pin and creates/removes only its own pin when one was absent;
158	`codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither needs a copied project
159	file. Claude's Copilot proxy must already be running; the Codex path may
160	self-start its proxy flow.
161	
162	An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:
163	
164	```toml
165	[worktree]
166	include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
167	```
168	
169	Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
170	launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
171	only, never its contents.
172	
173	## Dependency strategies
174	
175	- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
176	- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
177	- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
178	- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.
179	
180	`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
181	reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.
182	
183	## Cleanup
184	
185	- `dev git worktree rm <branch>` removes only the checkout after external runtime safety checks; branch survives.
186	- `dev work park` records WARM; when called from its own runtime it leaves that runtime alive for normal exit.
187	- `dev work park --cold --push` closes eligible runtime state and removes the pushed worktree only from outside.
188	- `dev work done --ff` integrates and records MERGED; runtime/worktree/branch survive.
189	- `dev work done --pr` leaves everything active for review.
190	- `dev work retire` is the only complete close/wait/remove/reap path.
